• You should be obsessed with beating the competition on mergers, LBOs and hostile takeovers.You must be well sourced inside the banks, law firms, advisers and everywhere in the M&A world. You also need to have the expertise to clearly explain why it all matters to Axios readers.

• We will boost your profile on the beat through our unique audience, as well as through appearances in our national newsletters and as an expert on tv, radio, podcasts and social media.

• Expertise for driving the conversation with scoops and trend stories

• Experience on stage at conferences getting sources to break news in a live setting

• A commitment to building and supporting a diverse and inclusive environment

jobs.title: Electrical Manager
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking an Electrical Engineering Manager (Team Lead) to be based in Denver, CO. This role is a senior leadership position within AECOM’s Buildings + Places electrical engineering practice, responsible for technical excellence, people leadership, and electrical discipline delivery across a diverse portfolio of building projects.

The Electrical Engineering Manager will lead and grow our team of electrical engineers supporting projects across commercial, science & technology, aviation, federal, industrial, and mission‑critical markets. Typical project sizes range from $5M to $500M in construction value, with opportunities to support large, complex, multidisciplinary programs.

This role is ideal for a senior electrical engineer who has served as a technical lead, project manager, or department‑level leader and is ready to formally step into team leadership, delivery ownership, and practice development responsibilities, while remaining technically engaged in electrical design.

About Buildings + Places

AECOM’s Buildings + Places practice integrates architecture, interiors, structural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing engineering, planning, landscape architecture, and advisory services to deliver holistic, resilient, and innovative building solutions. Our teams work across the full project lifecycle—from planning and design through construction administration—delivering projects that emphasize performance, sustainability, resiliency, and long‑term value.

Responsibilities

• Technical & Project Leadership
• Serve as the electrical discipline lead and formal Engineer of Record for assigned projects
• Lead electrical design for mid‑size projects and major scopes on large, complex multidisciplinary projects
• Perform and review advanced electrical engineering calculations, drawings, specifications, and technical reports
• Provide technical expertise in:Power distribution and service entrance systemsLighting and lighting controls designEmergency, standby, and critical power systemsGrounding, bonding, and lightning protectionFire alarm, communications, security, and other low‑voltage systems
• Support delivery of resilient, energy‑efficient, and electrification‑focused designs
• Oversee construction administration activities including submittals, RFIs, site observations, and technical issue resolution
• Represent electrical engineering in client meetings, interdisciplinary coordination, and design reviews

People & Practice Leadership

• Lead, manage, and grow electrical engineering teams, including workload planning, resourcing, and technical oversight
• Support hiring, onboarding, mentoring, and professional development of Engineer staff
• Provide performance feedback, goalsetting, and career guidance aligned with AECOM expectations
• Mentor engineers toward professional licensure, technical upskilling, and future leadership roles
• Foster a culture of quality, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement
• Support workforce forecasting and coordination with discipline, department, and regional leadership

Delivery Ownership & Business Support

• Own electrical discipline delivery on assigned projects, ensuring quality, schedule, and budget performance
• Act as an Electrical Lead, supporting scope development, staffing plans, and coordination
• Contribute to technical proposals, pursuit strategies, interviews, and client presentations
• Support and strengthen client relationships through trusted technical leadership
• Assist discipline leadership with development of standards, tools, and delivery best practices

Thought Leadership & Regional Collaboration

• Participate in technical reviews, internal knowledge sharing, and mentoring initiatives
• Collaborate with electrical teams across the large network of AECOM offices
• Support innovation initiatives related to digital delivery, sustainability, and resilient infrastructure
• Participate in shaping regional technical standards, and innovation initiatives within the Buildings + Places practice

Minimum Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering from an accredited program and 8+ years of progressive electrical engineering experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education

Preferred Qualifications:

• Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering
• 12+ years of electrical engineering experience
• Licensed Professional Engineer (PE) in Colorado or ability to obtain via comity within 6 months
• Strong working knowledge of NEC, NFPA, IES, and applicable building codes
• Experience designing building electrical systems including power, lighting, emergency, and low‑voltage systems
• Proficiency with electrical analysis and design tools such as SKM, ETAP, Easypower, Revit, and AutoCAD
• Strong written and verbal communication skills
• Ability to perform site visits; valid driver’s license required
• Prior experience in a team lead, department lead, or mentoring‑heavy role
• Experience with aviation, federal, mission‑critical, or science & technology facilities
• Background in resilient power systems, microgrids, electrification, or sustainability‑driven design
• Advanced BIM coordination experience
• Credentials such as LEED AP, CEM, or NCEES Record

Career Path & Growth

This role provides a clear pathway toward Senior Engineering Manager, Electrical Discipline Lead, or broader multidisciplinary leadership roles within AECOM’s Buildings + Places practice. The position offers long‑term opportunity to expand leadership scope, regional impact, and influence technical strategy.

Due to the nature of the work, sponsorship is not available for this position.

This position requires a hybrid work schedule with regular in-office presence in Denver, CO.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

As the voice of the company, agents provide exceptional guest service by answering phone calls, responding to emails and chats, processing orders, and offering expert advice to enhance the guest experience. The ideal candidate is highly motivated, customer-focused, and passionate about Aspen Snowmass and the surrounding areas where Aspen Skiing Company operates. This position reports to the MSCC Manager.

This position is eligible for commission-based earnings in accordance with the Company's commission plan, in addition to base compensation.

Applications for this position will be accepted until October 22, 2026 for the 2026-2027 Winter Season.

Essential Job Functions / Key Job Responsibilities

• Sell Aspen Snowmass products and services, including lift tickets, season passes, lessons, equipment rentals, and on-mountain activities via phone
• Answer inbound calls using sales and reservation software, providing expert recommendations and outstanding guest service
• Utilize professional sales techniques to guide conversations effectively and convert leads into sales with confidence, supported by an uncapped commission structure
• Address general inquiries about Aspen Snowmass products and the surrounding area, and offer personalized recommendations based on guests' needs
• Research, troubleshoot, and resolve guest issues efficiently, ensuring a seamless experience; redirect calls to the appropriate department when necessary

• Stay current on all Aspen Skiing Company products, services, policies, and events through ongoing training

jobs.title: The Hollywood Reporter: Production Associate, Video & Social Media
jobs.description:
The Hollywood Reporter is seeking a highly organized, proactive Production Associate to support our Video and Social teams. This role will work closely with the Head of Studio & Creative Content, producers, creative producers, editors, and social media team to coordinate productions from initial planning through final delivery and archival.

The ideal candidate is exceptionally organized, comfortable managing multiple productions and deadlines at once, and understands the fast-moving nature of editorial, entertainment, video, and social media production. This person will serve as a central point of coordination across shoots, crews, schedules, locations, production paperwork, footage, and post-production workflows.

Key Responsibilities

Production Coordination

• Coordinate video, social, editorial, branded content, studio, and location shoots.

• Maintain production calendars and coordinate schedules across producers, talent, crews, editors, photographers, and social teams.

• Assist producers with pre-production planning and day-to-day production logistics.

• Book freelance crews, including camera operators, DPs, audio mixers, gaffers, editors, production assistants, and other production personnel.

• Confirm crew availability, rates, call times, equipment needs, and production details.

• Prepare and distribute call sheets, schedules, production notes, contact sheets, and other shoot documentation.

• Coordinate studio bookings, location shoots, permits, parking, load-in/load-out, dressing rooms, and other production logistics.

• Assist with equipment rentals, production supplies, transportation, shipping, couriers, and other shoot needs.

• Coordinate production travel, including flights, hotels, ground transportation, and itineraries when necessary.

• Help ensure shoots remain on schedule and that all departments have the information and resources they need.

Crew, Contracts & Payments

• Maintain an organized database of freelance crew, vendors, rates, contact information, and availability.

• Coordinate freelancer agreements, contracts, releases, W-9s, certificates of insurance, and other required production paperwork.

• Work with producers and internal teams to ensure contracts are completed before productions.

• Collect, track, and process crew and vendor invoices.

• Assist with purchase orders, payment requests, expense tracking, and production reconciliation.

• Track outstanding invoices and payments and follow up with internal accounting and finance teams as needed.

• Maintain accurate records of production costs and help producers track projects against approved budgets.

Footage & Asset Management

• Upload, download, transfer, organize, and distribute video and social footage.

• Create and maintain consistent folder structures and naming conventions across productions.

• Ensure footage, audio, photography, graphics, project files, and final deliverables are properly labeled and stored.

• Coordinate footage transfers between production crews, producers, editors, and social teams.

• Maintain organized archives of raw footage, project files, masters, social cuts, and other production assets.

• Help manage company storage systems and ensure important footage and finished projects are properly backed up and archived.

• Locate and retrieve archived footage and assets for producers and editors as needed.

Post-Production & Deliverables

• Work closely with producers and editors to track projects from shoot through edit, review, approval, and final delivery.

• Maintain post-production schedules and help prioritize projects based on editorial and publishing deadlines.

• Track rough cuts, fine cuts, final masters, social versions, vertical edits, and other deliverables.

• Coordinate the delivery of footage, graphics, music, logos, photography, and other assets to editors.

• Help ensure final videos are delivered in the correct formats and specifications for YouTube, social platforms, websites, partners, and other distribution channels.

• Upload and organize final videos and assets for publishing teams when needed.

• Maintain clear records of completed and outstanding deliverables.

Social & Editorial Production Support

• Work closely with the Social Media Manager and social producers to coordinate social-first shoots and content capture.

• Help organize vertical video, BTS content, talent social moments, red carpet coverage, events, and other social deliverables.

• Coordinate with video and social teams to maximize content captured during shoots across multiple platforms.

• Help ensure social teams receive footage and assets quickly for time-sensitive publishing.

• Assist with coordinating coverage for premieres, festivals, awards shows, red carpets, panels, roundtables, and other entertainment industry events.

Rights, Releases & Production Documentation

• Track talent releases, appearance releases, location releases, crew agreements, and other required production documentation.

• Maintain organized records of footage sources, licensing information, and courtesy credits.

• Help producers confirm that third-party footage, photography, music, and other assets have the necessary information and documentation before publication.

• Maintain organized digital production files for each project.

Team & Department Support

• Work closely with the Head of Studio & Creative Content, producers, creative producers, editors, and Social Media Manager on daily production priorities.

• Serve as a central point of communication between production, post-production, social, editorial, finance, freelancers, vendors, and outside partners.

• Help maintain a master production calendar covering shoots, edits, publishing dates, and major department deadlines.

• Anticipate production needs, identify potential scheduling or logistical conflicts, and flag issues before they become problems.

• Help develop and maintain efficient production workflows and organizational systems for a high-volume video and social department.

• Support multiple projects simultaneously while responding quickly to breaking news, talent availability, and changing editorial priorities.

Qualifications

• At least 2+ years of experience in production coordination, video production, digital media, social media production, television, entertainment, or a related field.

• Strong understanding of video production and post-production workflows.

• Exceptional organizational and project-management skills.

• Ability to manage multiple productions, deadlines, and priorities simultaneously.

• Experience booking and coordinating freelance production crews.

• Familiarity with production contracts, invoices, purchase orders, releases, and vendor paperwork.

• Experience managing large amounts of video footage and digital assets.

• Comfortable working with cloud-based storage, review, and asset-management platforms.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Extremely detail-oriented and comfortable maintaining schedules, trackers, budgets, and production documentation.

• Ability to work calmly and efficiently in a fast-paced entertainment news environment where priorities can change quickly.

• Collaborative, resourceful, proactive, and willing to jump in wherever needed.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal Production Coordinator is someone who is always thinking several steps ahead. They know where a production stands, what is due next, who is booked, what paperwork is outstanding, where the footage lives, which editor has the project, when the final cut is due, and whether everyone has been properly invoiced and paid.

This role is ideal for someone who loves both the creative energy of video and social production and the organization required to keep a busy production department running smoothly.

As The Hollywood Reporter values in-person collaboration and team cohesion, employees work onsite four days a week and remotely one day a week, with a focus on maintaining a vibrant and inclusive culture. This position is based in Los Angeles.

A good faith estimate of the salary range is $70K - $75k upon hire. Factors that could be used to determine your actual salary may include your specific skills, years of experience and comparison to current employees already in this role. The total compensation package for this position will also include other elements, a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits including 401(k) eligibility and paid time off benefits.

PMC is committed to the health and wellness of our employees. As part of our company-wide rollout of PMC’s paid healthcare plan, for this role the company pays 100% of the monthly health, dental and vision plan premiums for the employee and their family. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.

If you have more or less experience than specified on this job posting, please apply and list your salary expectations.

If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors).

It’s all About You…

PMC's comprehensive benefits package is thoughtfully designed to support every aspect of your life, empowering you to thrive both personally and professionally. We offer PMC-Paid Healthcare with no employee paycheck contributions on medical, dental, and vision for you and your family. PMC also offers Flexible Spending Accounts (Healthcare, Dependent Care & Commuter), an Employee Assistance Program, Life Insurance, Short & Long Term Disability, Paid Parental Leave, and a 401(k) Retirement Plan with an Employer match. Employees are also eligible to take advantage of company discounts and perks including Pet Insurance, Home & Auto Insurance, Mortgage discounts, and a variety of other savings on wellness, lifestyle, and financial essentials. As part of PMC's dedication to consistently meet employee’s needs, we are currently launching a new Flexible Vacation Policy.

About The Hollywood Reporter:
The Hollywood Reporter provides unparalleled access to and intelligence about the business of the entertainment industry, as well as the people and the culture behind it. THR is an urgent and timely blend of rigorous breaking news, analysis, investigative reporting, insightful features, as well as lively design and elegant, creative photography across multiple platforms — a high-octane 24/7 website, a luxurious weekly print magazine, video series, podcasts, exclusive events and robust social media accounts. THR sets the entertainment agenda, elevating and broadening the style and substance of the Hollywood conversation

About Penske Media Corporation (PMC)

Penske Media Corporation (PMC) is a leading global media and information services company whose award-winning content attracts a passionate monthly audience of more than 500 million people.  Since 2004, PMC has been a pioneer in digital media and owns over 300 live events, while reaching audiences across all screens. Penske Media is recognized, as one of the Top 100 Private Companies in the United States and North America.

Our Companies & Brands

• Iconic Media Brands (PMX): Variety, Rolling Stone, The Verge, Billboard, The Hollywood Reporter, WWD, SHE Media, Robb Report, Deadline, Eater, Sportico, ARTnews, Fairchild Media, VIBE, IndieWire, SB Nation, ARTFORUM, POPSUGAR, Gold Derby, BEAUTY INC, Art in America, Punch, The Dodo, and more.

• Live Events & Experiences: The Golden Globes, SXSW, Academy of Country Music Awards (ACMs), Billboard Music Awards (BBMAs), Dick Clark's New Year’s Rockin’ Eve, SXSW London, American Music Awards (AMAs), and Latin Music Week.

• Data & Analytics: Luminate, the premier music and entertainment data and analytics company.

Global Footprint

PMC and its subsidiaries are co-headquartered in New York and Los Angeles, with additional offices spanning 14 countries worldwide.

Want to learn more? Visit www.PMC.com to explore our complete portfolio.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager- Strategic Sourcing MRO
jobs.description:
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Sr. Manager of Strategic Sourcing, MRO

• Hire, train, develop and lead a team of sourcing professionals for the Maintenance, Repair and Operations (MRO) commodity.
• Develops and support the overall vision, strategy and execution plan for the MRO Sourcing function. Achieving deeper alignment with stakeholders to pursue business strategies in innovation, agility and supply reliability.
• Conduct RFP and lead cross functional teams through the selection process of preferred suppliers with effective scoring criteria to critically evaluate supplier proposals in accordance with company policies
• Collaborate with Operations/Legal stakeholders to assess, understand, and prioritize business needs to optimize value with WD’s supply base
• Conduct spend/contract/proposal analysis for MRO Services, and present recommendation’s to Sourcing and MRO leadership team
• Lead negotiations on commercial procurement agreements, including, but not limited to, Master Agreements (MSA’s), Statements of Work (SOW’s), Change Orders (CO’s) balancing business deliverables, legal interests and pricing
• Analyze total costs, assist business functions with ROI analysis, price and rate benchmarking and negotiate favorable business terms to leverage Western Digital purchasing power
• Research market intelligence to understand cost drivers and market trends

Category Management

• Develop, refine and implement category strategies and tactics that enable the procurement of technology products and services at the highest value benefit to the company
• Cultivate, enhance, and deepen cross functional stakeholder relationships at all levels serving as the subject matter expert on behalf of the procurement organization
• Actively monitor internal/external trends, synthesize and distill the business intelligence into actionable opportunities and pipeline projects that can and will be delivered Western Digital’s bottom line on an ongoing basis

Supplier Management

• Manage supplier relationships with a focus on supply/contract and cost management
• Lead supplier performance business reviews on a quarterly basis to enhance performance delivery from strategic partners
• Mediate supplier issues and resolve supplier contract disputes as needed
• Develop supplier rationalization entitlements for each category

Contract Management

• Evaluate processes and recommend improvements to standardize lifecycle contract and sourcing processes and systems
• Ensure pricing & deliverables as negotiated are included in the contract; coordinate comparison of proposals and final contract terms
• Act as liaison between Legal and the business

REQUIRED:

• Bachelor’s degree with 10+ years of experience in indirect strategic sourcing with a multi-national organization with an emphasis in MRO
• MBA or JD preferred
• Extensive experience leading sourcing initiatives of all kinds (e.g., rapid sourcing, targeted negotiations, complex category strategies, supplier relationship management, outsourcing)
• Contract Negotiation / Vendor Mgmt. / Influencing skills required
• Experience and expertise with sourcing & contracting ERP tools (SAP and/or Oracle)

SKILLS:

• Self-motivated, flexible, and creative leader, able to prioritize, multi-task, and work in a fast-paced and demanding environment.
• Skilled negotiator with experience developing and executing complex negotiation strategies.
• Strong leadership presence with ability to garner respect through sound technical analysis, business judgment and clear decision-making.
• Excellent interpersonal skills with ability to lead, interact with, influence, resolve conflict and drive decisions among individuals from a variety of cultures and disciplines.
• Excellent analytical, interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.
• Proficient with Microsoft Office applications: Excel, Word, PowerPoint

jobs.title: Career Advisor, Adult/Dislocated Worker
jobs.description:
Career Team is a leading workforce development organization on a mission to transform lives.  We blend cutting-edge technology with compassionate, high-touch services to drive real, measurable outcomes in the lives of job seekers across the country.  At Career Team, we’re solving today’s unemployment challenges with smart software, world-class trainers, dedicated case managers, dynamic job developers, and innovative partners. If you're passionate about making a difference and believe in the power of technology to transform lives, you’ll feel right at home here.

TITLE: Adult/Dislocated Worker Career Advisor

REPORTS TO: WIOA Program Lead

LOCATION: Snohomish County, WA

EMPLOYMENT TYPE: Full-Time, Non-Exempt Employee

Priority Review: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and interviews may be scheduled before the application window closes. We encourage interested candidates to apply and complete the interview process as early as possible.

Career Team is looking to hire a Career Advisor who will perform professional work providing career counseling, intensive case management, and follow-up services. Work is performed under the supervision of the WIOA Program Lead.

Your Impact on Career Team’s Success:

• Provide information and case management services to the community

• Complete intake and eligibility determination for the workforce programs

• Assess career seekers’ employment, abilities, and training needs through interviewing, testing, and other methods

• Serves as a liaison between workforce development programs and community partners

• Enter data into and otherwise use and process career seekers through any participant information system as required

• Guide career seekers through the preparation of individual employment plans (IEP) based on their specific occupational goals

• Stay on top of labor market trends and best practices

• Counsel career seekers on available job opportunities, training programs, and other services

• Refer individuals to appropriate services, training programs, or job opportunities and follow up on those activities

• Conduct orientation sessions, workshops, job clubs, and other group presentations for career seekers

• Ability to work in a dynamic team environment - must have excellent teamwork and interpersonal skills

• Follow all policies, procedures, and regulations related to eligibility documentation

• Maintain accurate individual case files for each registered customer assuring that each file contains all required eligibility documents and meets compliance requirements

• Meet and/or exceed program benchmarks

• Participate in all staff-related events as required including but not limited to training and team meetings

• Complete all required reports within the data management system

• Approach each day and task with a solutions-oriented and responsive mindset

This position is expected to be 100% onsite. The selected candidate will be required to work onsite at the listed location.

To Qualify for This Role, You Must Have:

• Bachelors’ degree or higher or an equivalent combination of education and experience

• Strong communication skills and knowledge about community resources

• Possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make well-thought-out decisions

• Must be computer literate and have MS Word and Excel skills at minimum, and the ability to learn specialized databases and software systems

• Ability to work in a variety of settings with a culturally diverse customer base with the ability to be culturally sensitive

• Ability to motivate career seekers towards achieving goals

• Strong business acumen

• Ability to meet and exceed set goals and objectives

• Excellent interpersonal, time management, customer service, organizational skills, and communication skills, both oral and written required

• Knowledgeable about the WIOA program and other workforce program requirements

• A demonstrated ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment while remaining flexible, proactive, resourceful, and efficient in maintaining a high level of confidentiality

• Exceptional time management skills to meet deadlines and work under pressure

• A Valid Driver’s License

Additional Skills/Knowledge Career Team Would Love for This Role:

• Master’s or MBA degree

• Knowledgeable about the local region and relevant partners

• Bilingual or multilingual

Salary: $54,500 - $57,000/yr

Salary is commensurate with education and experience. Career Team offers a competitive benefits package including healthcare, dental, and personal/vacation time.

Travel:

Travel for this role is primarily limited to necessary trips within Snohomish County to support career seekers.

About Career Team:
Founded in 1996, Career Team, LLC is a private workforce development organization.

Career Team’s outstanding record of accelerating the human condition has resulted in numerous honors:

• Named by Inc. Magazine as one of America's 500 fastest growing privately held companies

• Recipient of the US Chamber of Commerce Blue Chip Enterprise Award for innovation

• Featured by 60 Minutes, CNN, Money Magazine, Inc. Magazine and the British Broadcasting Network as an innovative, government funded solutions program

• Invited to the White House after being cited by the National Welfare-to-Work Partnership and National Alliance of Business as a top 10 US training provider

As a socially conscious organization, Career Team has found a healthy balance between for-profit innovation and community enrichment. Looking ahead, the organization will continue to close the nation’s opportunity divide with additional government-funded workforce sites; while also building staff capacity of workforce funding sources and industry providers. See www.careerteam.com for more information.

About Our Practice

Our Rocky Mountain Regional Offices have a vast market spread, providing opportunities across a wide range of project typologies, including Science & Technology, Advanced Manufacturing, Commercial, Aerospace, Higher Education, Industrial and Process, Transportation, Aviation and Federal market sectors. A dynamic team of Architects, Planners, and Engineers we to incorporate beauty, sustainability, resiliency, equity, and innovation in our projects.

Some of our recent projects include a new Research and Development Facility for Sandia National Labs, the Cadet Chapel historic renovation at the US Air Force Academy, Energy Master Planning for the University of Colorado, and the Nation's largest sewer heat recovery central plant at the National Western Center Complex.

Job Summary/Responsibilities

The Senior Structural Engineer should be capable of leading teams to complete both small and large projects. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with internal and external clients is required. Candidate must be well organized, be able to work independently or part of a collaborative team and quickly recognize issues and be part of the solution.

As Senior Structural Engineer, you will be expected to:

• Be self-motivated with strong work ethic and take pride in your work
• Complete Structural designs for multiple types of projects varying in size and delivery method
• Make major design recommendations and design decisions in a collaborative multidiscipline team environment.
• Plan design work, and time schedules to assign design duties to junior staff working on projects
• Proactively coordinate design and schedule with other disciplines such as architectural, mechanical, electrical, geotechnical and technology
• Maintain accurate, clear and concise project documentation and design data.
• Mentor more junior staff through project work, reviewing their tasks and ensuring quality.
• Occasionally meet with clients, prepares proposals and presentations while maintaining good client relations
• Assist in project checking for quality control on other projects
• Have thorough knowledge of design techniques, tools, and principles involved in production of technical plans and drawings
• Use 3D structural analysis software to evaluate buildings for gravity and lateral loads.
• Represent the organization and maintains liaison with individuals and related organizations

Minimum Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree (B.S.) in Civil/Structural Engineering or Architectural Engineering or related field plus eight (8) years of structural analysis and design experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
• Professional Engineer license

Preferred Qualifications:

• Ten (10) plus years of related experience
• Structural Engineer (SE) License
• Master’s Degree in Civil and/or Structural Engineering
• Experienced in Structural Design and Calculation Software
• Experience and passion for mentoring younger structural engineering staff
• Skilled in the use of Microsoft programs and BIM software (primarily Revit and AutoCAD)
• Ability to clearly communicate in both oral and written communication to individuals or groups

Position Summary:

As the Regional Director of Operations, you will oversee, plan, and manage the operations of multiple dermatology centers within a designated territory. Develop and implement strategic business plans for each center to achieve financial and service objectives in alignment with PhyNet’s corporate goals.

Essential Functions:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to execute each essential function with excellence, with or without reasonable accommodation.

• Clinic Operations Management: Oversee clinic operations to ensure alignment with corporate goals related to service, associate engagement, and patient experience. Foster a culture focused on quality medical care and superior customer service while supporting the needs of physicians within the organization.

• Administrative Oversight: Direct, supervise, and coordinate the functions and activities of clinics, including systems management, budgeting, materials management, human resources, data processing, and facility maintenance.

• Daily Operations: Supervise daily operations such as patient registration, cash collection, charge processing, and referral/authorization management.

• Clinical Understanding: Develop a comprehensive understanding of dermatology clinic operations, including patient visits, surgical procedures, referral processes, pathology lab interactions, and cosmetic services, to support providers, patients, and the financial goals of PhyNet Dermatology.

• Corporate Strategy Development: Contribute to the development of corporate goals, objectives, and policies to guide clinic operations.

• Quality Healthcare Promotion: Advocate for the provision of cost-effective, high-quality healthcare services to patients.

• Patient and Client Satisfaction: Ensure a high level of satisfaction among patients and clients at all clinics.

• Team Development: Foster initiative, motivation, and positive morale among center staff.

• Compliance Management: Ensure compliance with government regulations and third-party payer requirements.

• Quality Standards Maintenance: Uphold standards of quality care across all facilities.

• Operational Planning: Develop and implement operational plans to ensure the medical and logistical viability of the clinics, achieving goals in an efficient and coordinated manner.

• Budget Management: Develop and manage budgets, including revenue forecasting, workload assessment, and resource allocation, to ensure financial stability. Report and analyze monthly and annual data to ensure budget compliance.

• Marketing Strategy Implementation: Assist in the development and execution of marketing plans, including corporate strategy, promotion of clinics and services, and product/service assessment. Manage public relations and referral relationships.

• Market Analysis: Analyze market conditions, identify trends, and initiate policy or procedural changes as needed. Negotiate client discounts to stay competitive.

• Conflict Resolution: Address conflicts within the organization while safeguarding the professional and legal rights of all parties involved.

• Resource Management: Resolve issues related to staffing, facility utilization, equipment, and supply management.

• Process Improvement: Analyze and refine systems and procedures to enhance workflow efficiency. Compile and maintain statistics as required by senior management.

• Facility Improvement: Recommend and oversee facility improvements, including construction, renovations, and equipment purchases.

• Policy Communication: Communicate corporate policies, objectives, and operational procedures to center employees effectively.

• Staff Recruitment and Training: Lead the recruitment, selection, and orientation of center personnel. Collaborate with staff to develop and implement performance goals and objectives, and oversee merit increases, promotions, and disciplinary actions.

• Interdepartmental Coordination: Work closely with other Center Administrators and senior management to ensure coordinated efforts in professional relations and contractual arrangements with third-party payers, clients, and government agencies.

• Compliance with Standards: Consult with medical staff to ensure compliance with standards and regulations.

• Public and Professional Representation: Represent clinics at public and professional meetings and conferences as required. Participate in center communication and public relations programs.

• Professional Development: Maintain professional affiliations and pursue ongoing professional development to stay current with trends in healthcare administration.

• Confidentiality: Maintain the highest level of confidentiality in all matters.

• Additional Duties: Perform other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

• A minimum of seven years of management experience, including at least three years in a healthcare organization. A minimum of five years of experience in budgeting and financial analysis, with dermatology experience preferred.

• Bachelor’s degree in health or business administration, preferably with an emphasis in finance or accounting. A master’s degree is preferred.

• Expertise in financial planning, budget preparation, trend analysis, and financial analysis.

• Exceptional interpersonal skills with the ability to motivate, collaborate with, and work effectively with others.

• In-depth knowledge of organizational policies, healthcare administration, and operating procedures.

• Proficiency in fiscal management and human resource management techniques.

• Familiarity with healthcare administration systems and governmental regulations.

• Competency in computer systems and applications.

• Strong planning, organizing, and supervisory skills.

• Ability to exercise initiative and sound judgment.

• Skill in developing and maintaining effective relationships with medical and administrative staff, patients, and the public.

• Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.

• Ability to analyze and interpret complex data.

• Proficiency in researching and preparing comprehensive reports.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

This role requires a proactive, dependable, and detail-oriented individual with the ability to manage multiple tasks in a dynamic healthcare environment. The ideal candidate demonstrates a strong commitment to patient care and operational excellence.

Physical and Mental Demands:

The physical and mental demands described below are representative of those required to perform this job successfully. Reasonable accommodations may be provided for individuals with disabilities:

• Physical Requirements:

• Occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for extended periods.

• Use hands to handle objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms.

• Occasionally required to climb stairs, balance, stoop, kneel, bend, crouch, or crawl.

• Occasionally lift, push, pull, or move up to 20 pounds.

• Vision Requirements:

• Close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

Note:
This job description is intended to provide a general overview of the role. Additional responsibilities may be assigned, or duties modified by the department supervisor based on operational needs.

jobs.title: Controller
jobs.description:
ABOUT CAPE

Cape is America’s privacy-first mobile carrier. Our mission is to be a force for good in global wireless. Cape was founded in 2022 by people who believe privacy is a fundamental right, not a luxury to be traded away. Our journey began when our founder recognized a critical vulnerability in our modern world: everyone relies on the same stagnant cellular infrastructure and legacy systems that track our every movement, monitor and profile our connections, and lose and sell our personal data.

Instead of accepting the status quo, we decided to fix it. National security professionals, journalists, parents, and everyone in between can stay connected and have privacy.

We didn’t just build a layer on top of old tech; we built America’s most private and secure mobile carrier from the ground up. By building our own network from scratch, we are able to design and build a suite of privacy and security features that no other carrier on the planet can offer.

Today, Cape provides our secure network to consumers, businesses, and government agencies alike. We closed our Series C in March 2026, and we are scaling rapidly, with the goal of giving people back control of their most personal information.




THE TEAM

At Cape, we are the architects of a privacy-centric movement that is just getting started. We are relentless builders, constantly innovating at the edge of what's possible in telecommunications. We operate on a foundation of high trust and high expectations. Our structure is flat, and collaboration matters more than hierarchy. As a member of our team, you will collaborate with world-class engineers, architects, and visionaries, and work across organizational lines to solve "impossible" problems and deliver mission-critical results for our users every single day.




THE ROLE

We are looking for a Controller who can flex from building a team to developing processes to maintaining our books, all while supporting a high-velocity business day-to-day. You are an accounting wizard and also, at your core, you are a builder. You will make an immediate impact by leveraging your accounting expertise and passion for building to update our processes to meet our stage of growth. The ideal candidate is a systems-oriented thinker who thrives when they can strategize, own, fix, and execute all at the same time. This role reports to our Head of Internal Operations.






WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON

 - Build robust processes: Design and implement accounting best practices that maintain high business velocity while meeting GAAP standards

 - Design Systems: Implement an ERP, in partnership with other key stakeholders, and provide leadership in managing the quote-to-cash process

 - Make Cape Audit-ready: Prepare Cape for, and then lead Cape through, its first PCAOB audit

 - Own Financial Operations: Own AR, AP, payroll, tax, and state compliance. Prepare and maintain accompanying audit-ready books and regular financial statements.

 - Build a team: Hire and develop an accounting team ready to meet Cape’s next stage of growth.






EXPERIENCE

 - CPA certification and understanding of ASC 606 revenue recognition standards.

 - 6+ years of progressive accounting experience. At least 2 years of Big 4 experience. Operational accounting within a fast-paced, high-growth start up.

 - Comfort creating and editing journal entries yourself in QBO, as well as implementing departmental accounting practices across our systems.

 - Have successfully led an audit end to end

 - Demonstrated ability to excel in dynamic environments. A self-starter with a history of identifying and implementing process improvements to enhance accuracy and timeliness of close

 - Strong collaboration skills to work effectively across business partners, customers, and vendors.

 - Meticulous organization skills, with a proven track record managing large projects end to end and owning recurring processes

 - (Bonus Points) Experience with NetSuite






COMPENSATION

We offer competitive compensation that is geo-adjusted based on your location, along with meaningful equity so you share in the value you help create. Salary range for this role in New York, NY or Arlington, VA is $230,000 - 270,000 depending on experience and interview performance.

Our benefits include:

 - 401(k) match

 - 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision premiums for you and your dependents

 - 12 weeks paid parental leave (for all parents, no waiting period)

 - Stipends for
   
   - Family-forming needs
   
   - Gender-affirming care

 - Unlimited PTO




OUR CULTURE & VALUES

 - We hire excellent people, give them outsized responsibility, and trust them to execute. Every person at Cape has a proven track record of tackling hard problems and winning.

 - We believe that personal privacy and national security are not at odds, and that they can be reconciled through strong technology.

 - We believe companies exist to build awesome things and take care of the people who build them, so we offer top-tier healthcare, 401(k) matching, and a generous vacation policy that our team actually uses to recharge.

 - We believe that a stronger company and a better product are built by people from all walks of life. We hire without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, disability, or Veteran status. If you are great at what you do, you belong here.
   
   


HOW TO APPLY

Click the link below to apply.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin, and without regard to disability or status as a protected veteran, or any other status protected by law.

About Us  - Big Changes, Better Benefits - Join us today!

The Aviation Institute of Maintenance (AIM), established in 1969, is a premier institution dedicated to advancing the field of aviation maintenance through exceptional education and training. With 15 campuses nationwide, AIM is a cornerstone in the aviation industry, accounting for 20% of all students attending FAA-certified Airframe & Powerplant (A&P) schools across the country. Each year, AIM proudly contributes to the graduation of nearly one in four certified aircraft technicians in America.

At AIM, you'll become part of a dynamic team of educators and leaders, all united by a shared commitment to delivering top-notch training and ensuring student success. We are passionate about equipping the next generation of aircraft technicians with the skills and knowledge needed to excel in the aviation industry. If you are eager to make a meaningful impact and help shape the future of aviation maintenance, AIM offers a rewarding environment where your contributions will truly matter.

Location:📍 459 NJ-17, Hasbrouck Heights, NJ 07604

Compensation: $25-$30/hr.

Schedule:

• Monday - Friday Three days: 8am - 5pm Two days: 11:00 AM–8:00 PM

• One Saturday per month: 8am - 5pm One weekday off in lieu of working Saturday

Position Purpose

The Financial Aid Officer serves as a primary point of contact for students throughout the financial services process in a higher education environment. This position guides and supports students with financial aid, funding requirements, tuition and fees, account balances, and payment arrangements.

The Student Finance Officer ensures financial requirements are completed accurately and on time while providing students with clear, responsive support and maintaining compliance with applicable federal, state, institutional, and funding source requirements.

Key Duties

• Guide students through the financial aid and funding process, clearly explaining requirements, available options, and individual responsibilities.

• Review and process financial aid documentation while ensuring student files are accurate, complete, and compliant with applicable requirements.

• Monitor student accounts to identify incomplete requirements, funding gaps, outstanding balances, and other issues requiring follow-up.

• Work directly with students to resolve financial concerns, establish appropriate payment arrangements, and help them meet their educational financial obligations.

• Provide a high level of student service while navigating sensitive financial conversations with professionalism and empathy.

• Partner with campus and Student Financial Services teams to resolve issues and support students throughout their enrollment.

Job Responsibilities

• Meet with incoming students to explain financial requirements, available funding options, student responsibilities, and required documentation.

• Guide students through required financial aid applications, forms, and documentation necessary to determine eligibility and secure educational funding.

• Process and maintain documentation for applicable funding sources, including Title IV federal student aid, VA Education Benefits, Military Tuition Assistance (TA), scholarships, cash payment plans, and alternative funding sources.

• Monitor FAFSA submissions and receipt of Institutional Student Information Records (ISIRs), resolving verification requirements, conflicting information, C-Codes, and other outstanding items.

• Monitor completion of required student and parent documentation, including Master Promissory Notes (MPNs), as applicable.

• Conduct required entrance and exit loan counseling individually or in group settings.

• Regularly review student financial aid and account information to identify incomplete requirements, funding gaps, outstanding balances, or other issues requiring action.

• Work with students to address outstanding financial requirements and develop appropriate solutions for meeting their financial obligations.

• Clearly explain tuition, fees, account balances, payment expectations, and available payment options.

• Establish payment arrangements in accordance with institutional policies and monitor student accounts for timely payment.

• Conduct timely outreach and follow-up regarding outstanding balances, missed payments, incomplete financial requirements, and other account-related matters.

• Maintain accurate and complete student financial records and ensure required information is updated in applicable systems.

• Prepare weekly deposits and month-end deposits and submit required documentation to Corporate Accounting.

• Maintain current knowledge of financial aid, student account, VA, Military Tuition Assistance, and institutional requirements, policies, and procedures.

• Serve as a trained VA School Certifying Official, as assigned.

• Attend required campus meetings, Home Office training, professional development activities, conferences, and seminars.

• Participate in the formal and informal mentoring of new employees to support onboarding, training, and a positive work environment.

• Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Required Qualifications

• High School Diploma or GED, or equivalent on-the-job experience.

• Must not be in default on Federal Student Loans.

• Strong numerical, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to review financial information, identify discrepancies, and resolve account-related issues.

• Strong understanding of financial aid and student account processes, with the ability to learn, interpret, and apply applicable regulations, policies, and procedures.

• Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced, compliance-focused environment.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to explain financial information, requirements, and options clearly.

• Strong interpersonal and customer service skills with the ability to build rapport with students and professionally navigate sensitive or difficult financial conversations.

• Demonstrated initiative, sound judgment, integrity, discretion, and accountability when handling confidential student and financial information.

• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with Student Financial Services, campus teams, and other departments.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Outlook, SharePoint, and Teams.

• Ability and willingness to work outside regular business hours, including evenings and weekends, as business or student needs require.

Preferred Qualifications

• Associate degree or higher in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Higher Education Administration, or a related field.

• Two (2) or more years of experience in student financial services, financial aid, student accounts/bursar operations, or a related financial services role.

• Experience within a proprietary or career education environment.

• Experience with Anthology or another student information system.

What We Offer

• 401(k) and Matching: Secure your future with our competitive retirement savings plan.

• Comprehensive Health Coverage: Enjoy Health, Dental, and Vision insurance to support you and your family.

• Life Insurance: Peace of mind with life insurance options.

• Parental Leave: Support for new parents during important life transitions.

• Paid Time Off: Recharge with paid time off to promote work-life balance.

• Employee Assistance Program: Access resources for personal and professional support.

• Tuition Reimbursement: Invest in your future with financial support for further education.

We are committed to providing a rewarding compensation package that supports both your professional growth and personal well-being.

AIM is a proud equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We believe that a diverse workforce contributes to the success of our company and are dedicated to fostering a culture of respect, equity, and inclusion.

jobs.title: Director, Consumer Product
jobs.description:
AXS connects fans with the artists and teams they love. Each year we sell millions of tickets to thousands of incredible events – from concerts and festivals to sports and theater – at some of the most iconic venues in the world. Since our founding in 2011, we’ve consistently pushed the industry forward and improved experiences for fans, making it easier than ever to discover events, find the perfect seats, and enjoy unforgettable live entertainment, and we continue to lead the evolution of our industry today.

We’re passionate about improving the fan experience and providing game-changing solutions for our clients, and we’re always looking for smart, motivated people to help make it happen. Bring your enthusiasm, your big ideas, and your desire to team up with some of the best and brightest in technology and entertainment.

The Role

We are looking for a Director, Product Management to lead Conversion, inclusive of ticket selection and checkout for our entire purchase funnel including LA28. In this role, you will define a product strategy for your areas of ownership that is in line with business goals and partner with your team to ensure smooth execution of a prioritized roadmap. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to prioritize features, determine trade-offs, ensure proper resourcing, and align dependencies. You will assess opportunities through stakeholder interaction and data analysis.

The ideal candidate is customer-obsessed, data-driven, passionate about delivering best-in-class consumer experiences, and is skilled in leading and developing high-performing teams.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Lead your team in prioritizing, managing and executing on the product roadmap for ticket selection and checkout, ensuring features are prioritized based on business goals, customer insights, and market trends

• Partner with leadership across engineering, design, product operations, account management, client services, marketing, LA 28, and other stakeholders to validate requirements, develop, test, and launch new features

• Optimize conversion funnels, personalization, performance, and user engagement to improve fan experiences and business outcomes.

• Conduct user research and analyze data to drive decision-making and continuous improvement.

• Communicate product updates, milestones, and priorities to stakeholders and leadership, showcasing product value

jobs.location: Austin, Texas, New York, New York
jobs.description:
About Us

• Insurance brokers sit at the intersection of care, cost, and access — yet remain one of the most underleveraged assets in the $5T healthcare value chain. They guide millions of Americans through plan selection, coverage questions, and care navigation, yet still rely on spreadsheets, manual workflows, and outdated tools that limit their growth and impact.

• Gyde is reimagining this. We’re building the first AI-native insurance brokerage platform—a system that learns from every client interaction to automate operations, power intelligent voice and chat experiences, and predict the right coverage and products for every individual or business.

• Our approach combines acquisition and AI: we acquire traditional brokerages and transform them into next-generation, data-driven organizations. Through Gyde’s platform, agencies run more efficiently, serve clients more personally, and scale faster than ever before.

• Join us if you’re excited to: Redefine how millions of people access and understand their healthcare coverage, by building systems that turn unstructured data, human conversations, and fragmented processes into intelligence. Build AI systems that improve how people access healthcare Design production-grade voice, chat, and predictive models for a highly regulated domain Launch technologies that augment human judgment and make complex decisions transparent and scalable Help reinvent an entire industry from the inside out

• We’re creating the future of brokerage — where every interaction, insight, and decision is powered by intelligence.

• Our founding team boasts pedigrees from Oscar, Stripe, Vista Equity Partners, and Alpine. Lightspeed led Gyde’s $60M financing, with participation from Optum Ventures, Crystal Venture Partners, Virtue, MVP Ventures, and multiple endowment funds, among others. Hear why on LSVP Investment Memo.

Role Summary

We’re looking for an M&A Analyst to power the analysis behind every brokerage Gyde evaluates, acquires, and closes.

Acquisitions are the engine of Gyde’s growth. Every agency we bring onto the platform starts as a set of seller financials, a book of business, and a handful of carrier statements. The quality of our analysis determines what we pay, how we structure the deal, and whether we should do it at all. As Gyde scales its acquisition pace across Medicare Advantage, ACA, employee benefits, and wholesale distribution, the speed and rigor of that analysis becomes one of the highest-leverage levers in the company.

You’ll sit at the center of the deal team. You’ll turn messy seller data into clean financials, build the EBITDA bridges and valuation models that set our price, and write the analysis that goes into our investment committee memos. You’ll coordinate diligence requests and third-party workstreams, keep the live deal pipeline accurate, and help build the AI-assisted tooling that lets a small team evaluate far more deals than a traditional corporate development function could.

This role is ideal for an analytically rigorous early-career professional from investment banking, private equity, corporate development, transaction advisory, or strategy consulting who wants real ownership on live deals. You’re as comfortable reconciling a carrier commission statement line by line as you are pressure-testing a seller’s adjusted EBITDA and forming a point of view on what a business is actually worth.

Key Responsibilities

• Build and maintain the financial models behind every deal, including EBITDA bridges, quality-of-earnings adjustments, valuation, sources and uses, and returns

• Spread and normalize seller financials, tax returns, and carrier commission statements into one clean, defensible set of numbers

• Pressure-test seller addbacks and revenue quality, including owner compensation, one-time items, carrier concentration, renewal versus new business, and producer dependency

• Draft the analysis, charts, and recommendations that go into investment committee memos, and help shape deal structure (earnouts, rollover equity, and retention)

• Screen inbound and outbound targets against Gyde’s acquisition criteria, and keep the live deal pipeline and deal trackers current and accurate

• Run diligence request lists end to end across financial, legal, compliance, and tax workstreams, tracking open items and chasing sellers for what is missing

• Coordinate with third-party advisors on Quality of Earnings, tax, and legal diligence, and translate their findings into model and structure changes

• Support signing and closing: purchase agreement schedules, working capital, funds flow, and closing checklists

• Build and improve the AI-assisted workflows, templates, and scorecards that make Gyde’s deal process faster and more repeatable

• Hand off clean deal data and context to the Value Creation team so every acquired agency starts integration with a clear baseline

What you bring / core competencies

• 1-3 years of experience in investment banking, private equity, corporate development, transaction advisory / Quality of Earnings, or strategy consulting

• Strong command of accounting and financial statements, and the ability to build a three-statement or deal model from a blank spreadsheet

• Command of the mechanics: EBITDA normalization, addbacks, valuation multiples, debt and equity financing, and returns analysis (MoM and IRR)

• Exposure to insurance distribution, brokerage, or healthcare services preferred; familiarity with commission-based revenue models a plus

• A practical, daily user of AI tools who knows how to get reliable output from them while retaining human judgement

• Meticulous attention to detail; your numbers tie, your sources are cited, and your assumptions are labeled

• Clear, concise writer who can turn a complex analysis into a recommendation a decision-maker can act on

• Entrepreneurial mindset with a strong sense of ownership; you want to run the work, not just support it

• Able to manage multiple live deals and competing deadlines without dropping the details

• Ability to travel up to ~10% for seller meetings and on-site diligence

What we offer

Gyde offers a competitive benefits package to all employees.

• $100,000-120,000 Base Salary + Equity

• Flexible (Unlimited) Paid Time Off

• Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits for you and your family

• Retirement Plan (e.g., 401K)

• Parental Leave

jobs.description:
Role Overview

We are seeking a Software Engineer to join our QPU SW Engineering team. In this role, you will develop the software that orchestrates and controls our quantum hardware stack—from real-time control of lasers and FPGAs to system-wide configuration, diagnostics, and feedback. Working closely with physicists, systems architects, and hardware engineers, you’ll build the tools and infrastructure that enable precise, reliable, and scalable quantum operations.

Key Responsibilities

• Design and implement software systems for orchestrating quantum experiments, including pulse sequence generation, device coordination, and real-time system control.

• Develop and maintain APIs and middleware that connect hardware control layers (e.g., FPGA, DACs, timing systems) with higher-level orchestration software and compilers.

• Implement reliable communication and synchronization protocols across embedded and distributed system components.

• Collaborate with system architects and physicists to translate experimental requirements into testable, high-performance software features.

• Contribute to diagnostic and calibration routines for hardware validation and performance monitoring.

• Develop tooling to support automation, test infrastructure, system state management, and logging.

• Participate in system bring-up, integration testing, and cross-disciplinary debugging efforts.

• Contribute to software architecture decisions, code reviews, and best practices across the engineering team.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field.

• 5+ years of experience developing software for hardware control, embedded systems, or distributed systems.

• Strong programming skills in Python and/or C/C++, and experience working with hardware interfaces (e.g., SPI, I2C, UART, Ethernet).

• Experience with real-time systems or hardware-in-the-loop control environments.

• Familiarity with timing systems (e.g., PTP), and communication stacks.

• Proficiency in system integration, testing, and performance tuning.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with scientific instrumentation, lab automation, or quantum hardware control systems.

• Familiarity with FPGA systems, DAC/ADC control, or pulse sequencing frameworks.

• Exposure to embedded Linux, RTOS, or custom firmware development.

• Knowledge of calibration, feedback, or control loop algorithms.

• Experience in multidisciplinary teams working at the intersection of hardware, software, and science.

jobs.title: Manager, Supply Chain
jobs.description:
Purpose

The Site Supply Chain Manager is a hands-on operational leader responsible for the day-to-day execution of supply chain activities supporting site operations. Reporting to the Associate Director, Materials Management, this role leads site planning, scheduling, inventory management, master data, and logistics activities to ensure materials, capacity, and resources are available to support production and business requirements.

The Site Supply Chain Manager works closely with manufacturing, purchasing/procurement, quality, engineering, supply planning, and warehouse teams to identify challenges, resolve issues, and drive actions to completion. This role requires a strong presence within site operations, regular engagement with cross-functional teams, and a willingness to work through operational details to support reliable execution.

As the primary supply chain representative for the site, the manager communicates priorities, risks, and recovery plans, aligns stakeholders on actions and decisions, and helps establish the processes, routines, and team capabilities needed to support a growing medical device manufacturing operation. The role balances daily operational execution with team development, process improvement, and continuous problem solving.

Responsibilities

1. Lead and develop the site supply chain team.

Directly manage site supply chain personnel responsible for planning, scheduling, inventory management, master data, and logistics activities. Establish performance expectations, monitor workloads, provide coaching and development, conduct performance reviews, and create a positive and accountable work environment. Participate in hiring, onboarding, and talent development activities as needed.

2. Own daily site supply chain execution.

Lead daily and weekly reviews of material availability, inventory position, capacity readiness, schedule performance, and logistics requirements. Establish priorities, assign actions, and track progress to completion. Maintain a visible presence in site operations and work directly with team members and site partners to identify and resolve constraints affecting execution.

3. Oversee production scheduling and schedule adherence.

Provide direction and oversight for developing and maintaining an executable production schedule that supports customer commitments and operational objectives. Partner with manufacturing, purchasing/procurement, quality, and planning resources to assess readiness, manage constraints, and support schedule execution. Ensure proposed changes within the locked schedule period are evaluated for impact and managed through established approval and communication processes.

4. Oversee materials, inventory, and capacity readiness.

Lead efforts to identify material shortages, inventory risks, and capacity constraints that could impact production. Review inventory levels, planning requirements, and material availability to support site operating needs while minimizing disruptions. Facilitate regular reviews of manufacturing capacity, labor availability, equipment constraints, and material readiness to identify risks and coordinate mitigation plans. Partner closely with purchasing/procurement to align material requirements, supplier commitments, and changing site priorities.

5. Lead operational problem solving and recovery actions.

Serve as the primary escalation point for supply chain issues affecting site execution, including shortages, scheduling conflicts, inventory risks, capacity constraints, and logistics disruptions. Bring together the appropriate stakeholders to assess impacts, establish action ownership, and coordinate recovery plans. Drive root cause investigations and ensure corrective actions are implemented and sustained.

6. Represent supply chain in site operations discussions.

Communicate supply chain performance, material readiness, inventory position, capacity risks, and recovery plans to the Associate Director, Materials Management and site leadership teams. Align stakeholders on priorities, timing, responsibilities, and operational decisions. Ensure changes in business or operational requirements are reflected in supply chain activities.

7. Oversee logistics and partner with warehouse leadership.

Provide oversight of logistics activities that support inbound material flow, internal material movement, and outbound shipments. Partner closely with warehouse leadership to coordinate priorities, resolve operational issues, and improve material flow throughout the facility. Ensure effective coordination between supply chain and warehouse functions to support production requirements.

8. Establish effective planning and master data processes.

Support the development and execution of planning routines, standard work, escalation processes, and operating procedures that enable consistent execution. Ensure master data is accurate, maintained according to established controls, and supports effective ERP/MRP execution. Partner with site teams to improve planning processes, system utilization, and operational discipline.

9. Support compliant material operations.

Ensure all supply chain activities are executed in compliance with site procedures and quality requirements for regulated medical device manufacturing. Partner with quality, manufacturing, purchasing/procurement, and warehouse teams to ensure material status, traceability, shelf-life requirements, and approved changes are properly managed. Support audit readiness and resolution of supply chain-related quality issues.

10. Manage performance and continuous improvement.

Monitor and improve key performance indicators including material availability, inventory health, schedule adherence, capacity readiness, logistics performance, and master data accuracy. Use performance trends, operational feedback, and root cause analysis to improve reliability, reduce recurring issues, and support continuous improvement initiatives across the site.

• Min 5 years of experience in Supply Chain Management in MNC, preferably in pharmaceutical industry.
• Bachelor's degree in Production Operations Management, Logistics Management, Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, or Supply chain management disciplines preferred, or equivalent work experience
• Strong teamwork skills required to work effectively in a team environment and establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external supply chain partners.
• Effective written and oral communication skills are required, especially in English, to facilitate information flow across the supply chain.
• Strong analytical skills are required for KPI, and inventory analysis.
• Excellent organization and follow up skills are critical to ensure timely communication across the supply chain

jobs.title: Billing & Compliance Coordinator
jobs.description:
We do not accept unsolicited resumes from third-party agencies. Resumes submitted without prior approval from our Talent Acquisition team will not be eligible for placement fees.

At Fortis Fire & Safety, we provide industry-leading fire protection & security services across the United States. Our ever-growing footprint can be seen in California, Florida, North Carolina, and Chicago, and we are acquiring new brands all the time.

We are proud to work together as one team under the Fortis Fire & Safety family, which includes CJ Suppression, Diversified Systems, Inc., Integrated Fire & Security Solutions, LaMarco Systems, LifeSafety Management, Piper Fire Protection, and VFS Fire & Security Services. United by a shared mission, we deliver comprehensive fire protection and security solutions nationwide.

Joining Fortis means becoming part of a nationwide, next-generation fire protection company. We’re dedicated to a People-First philosophy, where we invest in our team through training and development, as well as a competitive benefits package. In return, we expect the very best from each of our employees every day.

If you are ready to be exceptional in your chosen career, apply to work with us today!

Here at Fortis and throughout our family of brands, we offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

• Paid vacation and sick time

• Company Paid Holidays

• Additional paid time off for life events (e.g., jury duty, bereavement)

• Competitive compensation
