jobs.title: Senior AWS Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior AWS Cloud Infrastructure Engineer

You’re Opportunity:

At PLACE, we’re building a category-defining company at the intersection of real estate, technology, business services, and the consumer. As a profitable, hypergrowth startup, on the path to an IPO, our standards are high, and our team is scrappy, and our commitment is to execute the best work of our lives.

This is YOUR CHANCE to shape the backbone of a company that’s scaling rapidly and innovating boldly. As our Senior AWS Cloud Infrastructure Engineer, you’ll partner with our Platform & Infrastructure Engineering leadership, founders, and executives to architect and govern our enterprise AWS cloud platform, drive CI/CD and infrastructure automation strategy, and set the technical standards that keep our systems secure, scalable, and reliable across every engineering team. If you thrive in complexity, entrepreneurial problem-solving, and believe in scaling through tech and AI, this is your PLACE. This is a hybrid role based in Bethesda, MD.

Who Develops You: VP Software Engineering and IT Operations

What You’re Great At:

You are a hands-on cloud platform expert who thinks in systems, not just servers. You’ve spent years deep in AWS — EC2, ECS/EKS, Lambda, RDS/Aurora, API Gateway — and you know how to turn that expertise into infrastructure-as-code that other engineers can trust and build on. You’re as comfortable standing up a multi-region disaster recovery plan as you are leading a root-cause analysis after a production incident. Security and cost aren’t afterthoughts for you; they’re built into every architecture decision you make. You mentor generously, communicate clearly with product and engineering leadership, and you’ve got the scars — and the certifications — to prove you’ve done this at scale before.

What You’ll Do:

• Design and maintain enterprise AWS infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code (IaC); establish and enforce cloud architecture standards and operational best practices.

• Develop reusable infrastructure modules and deployment patterns; monitor and optimize AWS infrastructure costs (FinOps) without compromising reliability; partner with vendors on large-scale, cost-effective cloud solutions.

• Design, implement, and govern CI/CD pipelines (CodePipeline, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, and/or Jenkins/GitHub Actions); standardize deployment processes across multiple development teams.

• Design and maintain load-testing environments and automated performance benchmarks; validate auto-scaling for EC2, ECS/EKS, Lambda, and RDS/Aurora workloads.

• Implement security controls aligned with enterprise standards, including IAM roles/policies, AWS KMS, Secrets Manager, and least-privilege access models.

• Design, configure, and maintain AWS WAF and Shield policies and Amazon API Gateway, including throttling, rate limiting, usage plans, and API governance standards.

• Implement enterprise observability using CloudWatch, X-Ray, and CloudTrail; lead root cause analysis following production incidents.

• Mentor engineers on AWS, DevOps, automation, and cloud-native architecture; lead technical design reviews and serve as subject matter expert for cloud operations and platform reliability.

• Work across departments and with product/engineering teams (Agile/Scrum) to establish software standards, drive automation, and align infrastructure delivery with business priorities.

Salary: $165,000-$170,000/year depending on experience.

Why PLACE:

We believe people do their best work when they’re trusted, supported, and surrounded by others who are equally driven. That’s why this role includes a “work from the PLACE you work best” approach – at home, in an office, or on the move. Our competitive benefits include PTO as needed, comprehensive insurance coverage, a 401(k) match, stock option grants, and a stock purchase plan. Every team member is an owner, building the “PLACE” they are proud to call “my company.”

jobs.title: Executive Assistant
jobs.description:
EXECUTIVE ASSISTANT

San Francisco, CA

At Rothy’s, we know there’s a better way to do business, and it starts by putting the planet and its people first. More than 225 million single-use plastic bottles and 715,000 pounds of ocean-bound marine plastic have been transformed into our signature thread, creating wardrobe staples that look just as good as they feel.

Striving for zero waste, we combine 3D knitting technology and handcrafted assembly to create machine washable styles that don’t compromise on comfort. From classic shoes to carry-everywhere bags, we create essentials for wherever you go.

At Rothy’s, building a sustainable future is at the heart of everything we do. We pride ourselves on fostering an inclusive environment at our HQ, retail stores and wholly-owned factory, and are growing our community every day.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

Rothy's is looking for an experienced and energetic Executive Assistant to support members of our Executive Team. In this role, you'll do more than keep things moving — you'll be a trusted thought partner, helping our executives communicate with clarity, show up prepared, and lead with impact. Do you think three steps ahead, have a positive/can-do attitude, and thrive on gracefully handling multiple demands in a fast-paced environment? Are you collaborative, kind, and curious? If this sounds like you, this might be the right fit!




WHAT YOU’LL DO:

jobs.description:
Who we are:

Since 2009, we've been on a mission to bring sustainable fashion to everyone. Named one of Fast Company’s Brands That Matter and winning a Best Carbon Footprint award, we have big goals like being Climate Positive by 2025, Circular by 2030, and pushing the whole industry forward along the way. Our work has gotten love in Drapers and Sourcing Journal, and TIME wrote about how great our CEO, Hali Borenstein, is. Basically, we're saving the Earth and looking damn good doing it.

We're a global brand with 50+ stores (and counting) around the world, and our own sustainable factory in LA. We innovate across categories like accessories, swimwear, and sleepwear, and we reach millions of people with campaigns like this, this and this.

None of this work is possible without the incredible people behind it. We're a mission-based company that invests in an inclusive culture, so we can innovate together and ensure everyone has the space to grow, thrive, and belong.

And starting right now, we want to do all that with you.

Work Location/ Schedule:

• Available to work a minimum of 30 hours per week, but up to 40 hours per week

• Daily open availability across a full 7 day work week

• Able to work flexible schedule (days, nights, weekends, & holidays if required to meet the needs

Full Time Sales Lead

At Reformation, the sales lead is an elite sales professional and a central figure in the Reformation store ecosystem. This is an elevated, commission-based role designed for a high-performing entrepreneur who views retail as a career. You are a Wardrobe Consultant, responsible for managing a private book of business, driving exceptional SPH, and acting as a trend authority. You don't just facilitate transactions; you foster long-term loyalty through expert service and sophisticated clienteling leading to transformational experiences.

Reporting to the Store Manager, essential responsibilities include but are not limited to:

What You’ll Do

Drive Performance & Revenue

• Own Your Business: Consistently meet and exceed individual sales goals with a relentless focus on driving a high SPH (Sales Per Hour) and KPI’s.

• Customer Mindset: Act as an entrepreneur within the store, leveraging your product expertise to maximize every customer interaction.

• Proven Excellence: Maintain extraordinary customer feedback scores (NPS) by delivering an elevated service level that surprises and delights.

• Strategic Styling: Move beyond single-item requests to provide styling consultations, anticipating your client's needs for their entire seasonal wardrobe.

Sales & Operational Ownership (Keyholder):

• Opening & Closing: Ensure the store is ready for business the day of and for the next morning, according to the opening and closing checklist. Serve as a trusted keyholder responsible for opening and closing of the store, ensuring all operations, and visual standards are flawlessly executed.

• Safety & Compliance: Act as the primary leader for facility issues, loss prevention incidents, and emergency procedures during assigned shifts.

• Seamless Sales Leadership: Maintain sales floor energy and service standards during your segments, acting as the point of contact for the team and customers ensuring flawless store operations that keeps our elevated service seamless from open to close.

• Transition Management: Conduct chat-ins and handovers during segment changes to communicate key information, ensuring no service gaps occur during staff breaks by maintaining a minimum coverage ratio on the sales floor.

• Floor Leadership: Lead the sales floor energy and adjusting staff in real-time to balance task business needs, serving as the leader for customer escalations and employee inquiries, and maintaining a solutions-first mindset to keep store energy high.

• Visual Excellence: Uphold the VM Guidelines throughout your segment, ensuring recovery during time periods.

• Performance Coaching: Provide in-the-moment coaching and support to associates to ensure sales and service align with the Ref’s service model.

Master Clienteling & Retention

• Build and Manage a Book: Actively generate and manage a personal client database using Endear and other digital tools to drive repeat business and private appointments.

• Clienteling: Execute personalized, product-focused, and purposeful outreach strategy to ensure your clients are the first to know about new drops and community activations tailored to the client’s specific "Ref Journey" and life milestones.

• Wardrobe Curation: Go beyond the "plus-one", style head-to-toe looks that anticipate your client's needs for their entire lifestyle.

• Appointment Culture: Proactively schedule and host one-on-one styling appointments, providing an elevated, "white-glove" experience that secures customer retention.

Brand & Product Authority

• Sustainability Educator: Act as a brand ambassador, sharing the Reformation story and educating customers on our mission to be a circular, climate-positive leader.

• Product Expert: Share deep product knowledge with genuine enthusiasm, translating technical sustainability details into benefits for the customer.

• Feedback Loop: Communicate high-level product feedback to leadership to help continuously improve our merchandising and assortment.

• Team Mentorship: Lead by example on the floor, modeling the sales and service model and sharing pro-tips with the broader team to elevate the collective service level.

Operational Excellence

• Floor Standards: Ensure the selling floor reflects brand standards at all times, including meticulous attention to visual merchandising and steaming.

• Integrity: Understand and uphold inventory accuracy, loss prevention standards, and a professional, productive work environment.

What You’ll Bring

• Proven Track Record: At least 2–3 years of experience in a high-volume, sales-driven, or commission-based luxury/premium retail environment with a history of consistently hitting or exceeding SPH and personal sales targets.

• Interpersonal Mastery: Exceptional communication skills and emotional intelligence with the ability to build instant rapport and navigate diverse personalities with ease and professionalism.

• Wardrobing Expertise: A deep passion for styling with a proven ability to "edit" collections for clients based on body type, occasion, and personal style.

• Self-Starter Mentality: A driven approach to challenges and the self-motivation to treat your role like a career, not just a job.

Compensation:

At Reformation, we believe in transparency and equity when it comes to compensation. For this role, the anticipated base hourly range is $22 - $28 per hour depending on a variety of factors, including but not limited to relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and internal compensation equity.

Please note that compensation decisions are made thoughtfully and may vary from the listed range to reflect individual circumstances and evolving business needs. Our total rewards package also includes benefits, perks, and opportunities for growth that contribute to overall compensation.

Benefits & Perks:

• Eligible employees get employer-sponsored private medical, dental, and vision insurance, as well as commuter benefits to help support your travel to and from work.

• We offer competitive paid time off policies including vacation, sick leave, and company holidays for eligible employees.

• We offer retirement planning support for eligible employees, including the option to invest in Environmental Social Governance-aligned (fancy way to say sustainable) funds.

• We offer a clothing discount, culture events (like our annual Ref Values week and Volunteer Time Off), you know, all the meaningful and fun stuff!

Reformation is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team that reflects the world we want to live in. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, or veteran status—in accordance with applicable international, federal, state, and local laws.

If you require accommodations during the application or interview process, please let us know. We’re here to ensure you have what you need to show up as your best self.

Still don’t know if you should apply? We get it—studies show that many women and individuals from historically underrepresented communities hold back from applying unless they meet every single requirement. At Reformation, we’re all about growth, not gatekeeping. If you’re passionate about the role and excited about making fashion more sustainable, we’d love to hear from you. If this role doesn’t totally excite you, consider applying to our general application.

jobs.title: Director, Content
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a senior content leader to own the voice of two brands: Darkroom, our growth marketing agency, and Shadow, our AI commerce platform. Ad Age recently described us as "if Omnicom was rebuilt on AI." Your job is to turn a line like that into an argument the market repeats back to us. The split is roughly 80% Darkroom, 20% Shadow.

We are making a category bet on the forward-deployed marketer, the operator who sits inside a business and builds with AI rather than briefing the work out. We intend to make that a term of art through Darkroom: the article, the LinkedIn engine, the video, the webinars, the press. You own that campaign end to end.

You'll report to our VP of Marketing, who sets direction and makes the calls. You'll help shape the thinking behind it: how content maps to the funnel, which channels carry which offers, and what actually turns attention into pipeline. Then you build the content that proves it.

Our marketing operations manager owns the calendar, the publishing, and the deployment. You make the content that fills all of it, across LinkedIn, video, email, paid, and creator, and you brief our designer, video editor, and SEO specialist so one idea becomes a post, a video, an email, and an ad in the same week. This isn't a writing-only role.

Alongside content, you own the creative half of the creator program: who we work with, what we ask them to make, and the call on whether we go wide with many creators or deep with a few. You source and negotiate the partnerships and write the briefs. Marketing Ops runs the admin behind it. Creator content is one of our two strongest lead sources today and the one with the most room left in it.

This is a New York-based role operating in the EST Time Zone, hybrid out of our new NYC office, and all business is conducted 100% in English.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Brand Narrative: Define and defend what Darkroom and Shadow say. Own the positioning arguments, the category bet, and the point of view that shows up everywhere else.

 - Funnel & Strategy: Work with the VP of Marketing on how content builds pipeline: which channels, which offers, which lead magnets, and what the content has to do at each stage. You help build the model, then you feed it.

 - LinkedIn & Video: Build our LinkedIn engine across the company page and our executives' accounts, including video made for the feed it runs in. This is where our buyers spend their day and where we have the most ground to take.

 - Creator Strategy & Briefs: Decide who we work with and what they make. Source creators, negotiate the partnerships, write the briefs, and set the strategy between a wide roster and a small group of anchor creators. Marketing Ops handles the CRM, deadlines, content collection and reporting.

 - Email & Newsletter: Own what goes into our newsletter and to our list. Marketing Ops handles deployment. The thinking, the cadence, and the reason anyone opens it are yours.

 - Shadow Content: Take Shadow's content from scattered to a funnel: posts into webinars and lead magnets into signups. Product marketing for a platform that sells to operators.

 - Paid Copy: Partner with our designer, video editor and performance team on the words behind our ads, so the organic and creator assets that work become the ads that work.

 - Editorial Direction: Brief the team, review the work, and hold a consistent standard across every surface both brands touch.

 - Events & Moments: Turn our NYC office, our activations, and our press into content programs instead of one-off posts.

 - Measurement: Work with Marketing Ops on the weekly scoreboard: reach, follower growth, earned media value, and how content traffic converts.




YOU SHOULD APPLY IF THIS SOUNDS LIKE YOU

 - 5+ years in content, brand, or creator marketing, from an agency or a commerce brand, with B2B or pipeline accountability. SaaS or martech experience is a plus.

 - You have owned content that was accountable to a business number. You can explain how a post becomes traffic, becomes a conversion, becomes a lead, and you have been graded at the end of that chain. If content has always been someone else's funnel, this role is not for you.

 - You know this world. DTC, e-commerce, performance marketing, social commerce, AI tooling. You can write about TikTok Shop, retention, or attribution without a briefing and without getting it wrong.

 - You have sourced, negotiated with, and briefed creators yourself. You know what separates a brief that produces something usable from one that wastes everybody's month.

 - You have a public track record. A newsletter, bylines, a brand account you grew, a campaign that landed, a term you helped popularize. Send the link.

 - You get output out of people who don't report to you, and you can give a designer or an editor feedback that makes the next version better.

 - You arrive with a list. In the first interview, we will ask what you would change about our LinkedIn, our newsletter, and our creator content. We expect specifics.

 - You already work with Claude, ChatGPT, or similar daily and have shipped real work with them. We are a Claude-first company.




HARD DISQUALIFIERS

 - No published writing or no portfolio link.

 - Never sourced or briefed a creator yourself.

 - Content experience with no accountability for pipeline.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT

Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace—we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national orientation, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

jobs.title: Growth Marketing Generalist
jobs.description:
About WorkOS 🚀

WorkOS builds modern developer tools and APIs that make it easy for companies to become Enterprise Ready. Our platform powers authentication, identity, authorization, and other critical infrastructure that developers need to securely scale their products to large organizations.

We recently raised a $100M Series C, valuing the company at $2B, led by Meritech and Sapphire with participation from Greenoaks, Craft, Abstract, and Audacious. WorkOS powers enterprise features for many of the fastest-growing AI companies, including OpenAI, Cursor, and Perplexity, Sierra, and Plaid.

As AI reshapes software, WorkOS is at the frontier of Human and Agent Authentication, Identity, and Access Control helping companies answer a new critical question: who are your agents, and what are they allowed to do? Our fast-growing customer base includes hundreds of modern software companies building the next generation of enterprise-ready products.


ABOUT THE ROLE 

WorkOS has a strong bottom-up, developer-focused GTM motion. Our growth team sits at the center of it, running the campaigns, events, and demand programs that put WorkOS in front of technical buyers. As those programs have grown, so has the volume of work that makes them happen, and we're looking for a Growth Marketing Generalist to own it.

This is a hands-on execution role. You'll work across campaign management, events, and content, taking programs from brief to live and getting the details right. One week that means running a developer event in San Francisco; the next, pulling together campaign assets. You'll get clear direction and real ownership.

This is a great fit if you like variety, move fast, and want to build range across every part of a growth function. You'll work directly with the Growth lead and partner closely with sales, design, and product. You don't need to have marketed to developers before, though it's a plus. What matters is that you come from a technical or B2B software environment where you understood what the product did and who was buying it.


RESPONSIBILITIES 

 - Events and Field Marketing: Support with logistics and execution of our developer events, conferences, and dinners, including venue and vendor coordination, invite and registration flows, on-site support, and follow-up.

 - Project Management: Own timelines for creative assets and copy for growth programs (e.g. newsletter sponsorships), keeping designers and campaigns on schedule so deliverables are ready and submitted on time.

 - Copy and Content: drafting variations of email copy, social posts, invites, and event materials, keeping it clear and on-brand for a technical audience

 - Reporting: Track performance across programs and report on what worked, surfacing what we should do more or less of.

 - Measurement & Tracking: A clean tracking foundation across UTMs and campaigns so we can confidently measure performance.

 - Cross-functional Partnership: Work with sales on event follow-up and pipeline handoff, and with design and product on assets and messaging.

 - Continuous Learning: Build real knowledge of WorkOS products, our developer audience, and the AI-native companies we sell to.


QUALIFICATIONS 

 - Experience: 2-4 years in a marketing role at a B2B software or technology company, ideally one selling to a technical audience.

 - Executional Strength: A track record of reliably shipping marketing work end to end, on time and with the details correct.

 - Project Management: Run several programs at once, keep track of the moving pieces, and follow through without needing to be chased.

 - Writing Ability: Clear writer who can adapt to a brand voice and write for a smart, skeptical, technical reader.

 - Events Experience: Hands-on experience running or supporting events, from small dinners to conferences.

 - Tooling: Comfortable in a modern marketing stack, including marketing automation or email tooling, a CMS, and analytics.

 - Domain Understanding: Enough technical context to understand what a developer tool does and why someone would buy it.

 - Self-starter: Previous startup experience, particularly in high-growth PLG organizations.

 - AI-Native: Hands-on experience building with AI-native tools, using LLMs, agents, and automation in your own marketing workflows.

Benefits and Perks (US Only) 💖

At WorkOS, we offer resources that emphasize personal and familial well-being. We offer healthcare coverage for you and your family, including medical, dental, and vision. We offer parental leave, paid-time off and fully remote working arrangements.

jobs.title: Enterprise Field Marketer
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Enterprise Marketing team helps the world’s largest organizations understand, adopt, and scale AI responsibly. We partner closely with Sales, Solutions, Product Marketing, Customer Success, Events, and executive leadership to create programs that accelerate strategic customer growth and strengthen OpenAI’s position as the leader in enterprise AI.

Within Enterprise Marketing, the Field Marketing team is responsible for translating business priorities into high-impact customer engagement motions across industries, regions, and strategic accounts. We build and run programs that create pipeline, accelerate opportunities, deepen executive relationships, and bring OpenAI’s latest innovations directly to enterprise decision-makers.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Enterprise Field Marketer, you will be a growth partner to Enterprise Sales, owning field marketing programs that create pipeline, accelerate strategic opportunities, and deepen relationships with priority enterprise accounts.

You will own the full program lifecycle: translating sales priorities into field plans, identifying the right accounts and moments, executing high-quality customer programs, driving follow-up with sellers, and measuring business impact. This is a hands-on role for someone who can move from territory strategy to tactical execution quickly, with strong commercial judgment and high accountability for outcomes.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or New York City. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance. Travel is expected for customer events, executive programs, industry conferences, and internal planning moments.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build and execute field marketing plans aligned to priority seller groups, strategic accounts, industries, and regions.

 - Partner closely with Sales leadership on account prioritization, territory planning, outreach strategy, pipeline goals, and follow-through.

 - Own the full lifecycle of field programs, from strategy and planning through execution, seller enablement, follow-up, and measurement.

 - Run high-impact customer programs including executive dinners, roundtables, forums, workshops, industry moments, roadshows, and third-party conference activations.

 - Turn marquee moments into measurable pipeline opportunities with clear target accounts, success metrics, seller ownership, and post-event conversion plans.

 - Collaborate with Product Marketing, Events, Comms, Marketing Operations, Solutions, Customer Success, Partnerships, and executive stakeholders to deliver compelling customer experiences.

 - Track performance, communicate business impact, and build repeatable playbooks that help field marketing scale across enterprise segments.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 8+ years of experience in enterprise field marketing, ABM, regional marketing, sales enablement, or related B2B growth roles supporting complex sales motions.

jobs.title: Scientist II, Analytical Development
jobs.description:
Legend Biotech is a global biotechnology company dedicated to treating and, one day, curing life-threatening diseases. Headquartered in Bridgewater, New Jersey, we are advancing the next generation of cell therapy through a portfolio of innovative technologies, including autologous, allogeneic, and in vivo cell therapy approaches. Our research spans chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T), T-cell receptor (TCR-T), natural killer (NK) cell-based therapies, and other emerging platforms designed to transform the treatment of serious diseases. From our global network of research and development sites, we are committed to discovering and developing safe, effective, and cutting-edge therapies for patients worldwide.

Legend Biotech entered into a global collaboration agreement with Johnson & Johnson to jointly develop and commercialize CARVYKTI® (ciltacabtagene autoleucel; cilta-cel). Through this strategic partnership, we combine complementary expertise and capabilities to advance innovative immunotherapies for patients living with multiple myeloma.

Legend Biotech is seeking a Scientist II, Analytical Development as part of the Technical Development team based in Somerset, NJ.

Role Overview

We are seeking a dynamic and scientifically driven Scientist II to join Functional, Flow Cytometry and BioAnalytics team within our empowered Analytical Development organization. This role will focus on the establishment, development and qualification of analytical methods, including compendial methods, flow cytometry, cell-based potency, and immunoassays to support the development and manufacture of Legend’s cell and gene therapy pipeline. This laboratory-focused role will require that candidates develop, optimize and execute analytical methods for product characterization, release and stability testing. This role will require authoring and reviewing documents, maintaining electronic laboratory notebooks, and contributing to cross-functional collaboration with other functional teams.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop, optimize, and execute analytical methods to support viral vector and CAR-T product characterization, including compendial methods, titer, particle size, flow cytometry, and cell-based potency methods.

• Author and review methods, protocols, and reports.

• Maintain reagent inventory and order materials as laboratory activities require.

• Generate and qualify critical materials for analytical methods.

• Observe all laboratory safety standards including PPE use and BSL2 best practices.

• Performing pre-qualification, assay qualification, product release testing, and product characterization testing in a quality control environment.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity:

As the Security Technical Program Manager, you will serve as the strategic operational bridge connecting the Security Risk Engineering function with global Product, Engineering, and SRE teams. You will orchestrate mission-critical security programs from inception to deployment, transforming abstract security, compliance, and risk initiatives into high-impact, actionable roadmaps. This role requires a balance of rigorous technical program management, financial services acumen, and modern technical insight across cloud architectures and AI ecosystems to ensure Flywire moves fast and remains secure by design.

Responsibilities and Tasks (in order of priority)

• Security Lifecycle Program Management: Lead and drive cross-functional "Security by Design" and Secure-SDLC initiatives across critical application launches, automated workflows, and emerging AI tools from ideation to deployment.
• AI-Driven Process Efficiency: Actively adopt and leverage internal enterprise AI tools and Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate program tracking, streamline documentation, optimize cross-functional security workflows, and continuously drive operational efficiency.
• Vulnerability & Threat Orchestration: Coordinate the end-to-end vulnerability lifecycle, partnering directly with Product, SRE, and Software Engineering to ensure rapid prioritization, tracking, and remediation of technical risks.
• Information Security Compliance & Regulatory Audits: Oversee complex technical security assessments and audits to ensure continuous, strict readiness for PCI-DSS, SOX, SOC 1, and SOC 2 frameworks.
• Strategic Roadmap & Operational Governance: Establish, maintain, and communicate the security engineering program roadmap, defining clear project charters, timelines, success metrics, and the technical "Definition of Done" for executive stakeholders.
• Cross-Functional Enablement: Partner with high-velocity software engineering and infrastructure teams to integrate secure technical guardrails seamlessly without inducing development velocity friction.
• Team Performance & Mentorship: Provide guidance and operational coaching to junior members of the security and program teams, cultivating a culture of technical excellence and collaborative risk awareness.

Here's What We're Looking For:

Education, Experience/Knowledge & License/Certification

• Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree required in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
• Core Experience: 2+ years of progressive experience in Technical Program Management (TPM), driving complex Information Security, Application Security, or Cyber Risk initiatives within highly scalable technology environments.
• Industry & Domain Requirement: Extensive experience operating within the Financial Services and global Payments Industry space is required. Must possess a deep structural understanding of high-stakes financial platform mechanics, transaction processing lifecycles, and payment clearing rails.
• Information Security Compliance & Audit Mastery: Proven track record of managing, executing, and delivering complex end-to-end audits for strict financial and core data privacy frameworks, with mandatory proficiency in PCI-DSS (v4.0), SOX, SOC 1, and SOC 2. Thorough working knowledge of emerging international standards (e.g., DORA) is highly preferred.
• Technical & AI Depth: Solid foundational understanding of modern cloud architectures (AWS/GCP/Azure), automated Secure-SDLC engineering pipelines, the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, and automated enterprise vulnerability management systems- all in the spirit of protecting Flywire global payment ecosystem from bleeding-edge threats.

Highly Preferred Certifications

• Core Security & Compliance: CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional), CISM (Certified Information Security Manager), or CCSK (Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge).
• Audit Focused: CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor).
• Program Execution: PMP (Project Management Professional) or certified Agile/Scrum Master.

Skills and Abilities

• Fintech/Financial Services Security Compliance Specialist: Exceptional ability to translate dense, high-stakes financial compliance requirements and complex technical vulnerabilities into frictionless, highly scannable, and actionable engineering remediation plans.
• Automation & Optimization Mindset: Demonstrated ability to look at legacy program management frameworks and replace manual, repetitive checkpoints with intelligent automation, workflows, and enterprise AI tools.
• Influence Without Authority: Natural leadership presence with a demonstrated ability to align, motivate, and drive cross-functional software engineers, product managers, and external financial regulators across globally distributed time zones.
• High-Pressure Decision Making: Impeccable resilience and analytical clarity in high-pressure scenarios, with the ability to manage transparency and guide risk-based decisions during active security incidents or compressed financial product launch windows.
• Strategic & Tactical Balancer with a Commercial Mindset: Highly hands-on and technically skilled. Strong strategic thinker with the ability to contribute to and translate team/program’s high-level vision into actionable plans and drive successful execution. Balances technical risk reduction with business enablement, ensuring security infrastructure serves as a competitive advantage that unblocks global revenue and enterprise-client acquisition.

jobs.title: Fabrication Team Lead - Houston, TX
jobs.description:
Fabrication Floor Lead

Crane Structural Fabrication

Location: Houston, Texas

Company: Konecranes

Position Summary

Konecranes is seeking a hands-on Fabrication Team Lead to lead fabrication personnel responsible for the manufacturing of custom-engineered crane structures, including bridge girders, end trucks, trolley frames, platforms, walkways, machinery structures, and other welded assemblies used in overhead and gantry crane systems.

The Fabrication Foreman is responsible for the safe, efficient, and high-quality execution of all fabrication activities, including material preparation, fit-up, welding, dimensional verification, and structural assembly. This position provides direct leadership to fabrication employees and is accountable for safety, productivity, quality, schedule adherence, and workmanship.

Success in this role requires a visible leader who actively engages on the shop floor, promotes accountability, and ensures all fabricated structures meet engineering requirements, dimensional tolerances, and applicable welding standards, including AWS D14.1. The ideal candidate understands that crane manufacturing demands exceptional precision, weld quality, and structural integrity to ensure safe and reliable operation in the field.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Team Development

• Lead and direct welders, fitters, fabricators, and production personnel.
• Establish clear performance expectations and hold employees accountable for safety, quality, productivity, and attendance.
• Promote a culture of craftsmanship, ownership, discipline, and continuous improvement.
• Provide coaching, training, and development opportunities for fabrication employees.
• Support employee development and succession planning within the department.
• Foster teamwork and collaboration between Fabrication, Engineering, Quality, Planning, and Assembly teams.
• Maintain a visible presence on the shop floor and actively support daily operations.

Fabrication Operations

• Oversee fabrication, fit-up, welding, grinding, structural assembly, and material handling activities.
• Coordinate manpower, equipment, and resources to meet production schedules and customer delivery commitments.
• Monitor workflow and remove obstacles impacting productivity and throughput.
• Ensure fabrication processes are executed in accordance with approved drawings, work instructions, and welding procedures.
• Manage daily production priorities and communicate progress, risks, and resource needs to management.
• Drive labor efficiency while maintaining quality and safety expectations.
• Coordinate with engineering and quality personnel to resolve fabrication issues and drawing discrepancies.

Welding Quality & Structural Integrity

• Ensure all welding activities are performed in accordance with approved Welding Procedure Specifications (WPS), quality requirements, and AWS D14.1 standards.
• Verify weld quality through proper fit-up, joint preparation, welding practices, and visual inspection standards.
• Ensure welders maintain required qualifications and certifications.
• Drive first-pass weld quality and minimize weld repairs and rework.
• Review weld defects, nonconformances, and repair activities and implement corrective actions.
• Work closely with Quality personnel to ensure compliance with inspection and testing requirements.
• Promote workmanship standards that result in safe, structurally sound crane components.
• Quality & Dimensional Control
• Ensure fabricated structures meet engineering drawings, specifications, and customer requirements.
• Maintain strict control of dimensional tolerances, structural alignment, and fabrication accuracy.
• Verify girder geometry, wheel alignment, rail alignment, span dimensions, camber requirements, and structural squareness.
• Ensure fabricated components transition to assembly operations without quality-related delays.
• Drive first-time quality and reduce fabrication-related rework.
• Support root-cause analysis and implementation of corrective actions for recurring quality issues.
• Ensure all required inspection documentation and production records are completed accurately.
• Safety Leadership
• Lead and promote a strong safety-first culture throughout fabrication operations.
• Ensure compliance with all Konecranes safety policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
• Conduct routine safety observations, audits, and corrective actions.
• Promote safe welding, cutting, rigging, lifting, and material handling practices.
• Maintain a clean, organized, and efficient work environment utilizing 5S principles.
• Actively investigate incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions and implement corrective measures.

*This position will be located on the factory floor

Desired Qualifications

• Experience leading fabrication, welding, structural steel, heavy equipment, or industrial manufacturing operations.
• Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate and develop hourly production personnel.
• Thorough understanding of welding processes, fabrication methods, and structural assembly techniques.
• Working knowledge of AWS D14.1 welding requirements and quality standards.
• Ability to read and interpret fabrication drawings, weld symbols, inspection reports, and engineering documentation.
• Experience with dimensional inspection, alignment verification, and structural tolerance control.
• Strong problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
• Crane manufacturing, structural steel fabrication, bridge construction, heavy equipment, or similar experience preferred.

What Success Looks Like

• Consistent achievement of fabrication schedules and production targets.
• High first-pass weld acceptance rates.
• Reduced weld repairs, rework, and quality escapes.
• Compliance with AWS D14.1 and Konecranes workmanship standards.
• Improved labor productivity and fabrication efficiency.
• Strong employee accountability, engagement, and development.
• Safe, organized, and disciplined fabrication operations.
• Delivery of structurally sound, dimensionally accurate crane components ready for assembly.

What we offer:

Benefits: Medical Plan, Dental, Vision, 401k plan with a match from day one, identity theft protection, accident insurance, travel insurance and so much more!

Vacation: 2 weeks of vacation per year (pro-rated for the first year depending on start date). 5-12 years of service, 3 weeks. 13+ years of service, 4 weeks.

Sick Leave: 5 days of Sick Leave per year. Pro-rated the first year after 90 days of service

Holidays: 10 paid holidays per year

Konecranes moves what matters. Konecranes is a global leader in material handling solutions, serving a broad range of customers across multiple industries. We consistently set the industry benchmark, from everyday improvements to the breakthroughs at moments that matter most, because we know we can always find a safer, more productive and sustainable way. That's why, with 16 000+ professionals in over 50 countries, we are trusted every day to lift, handle and move what the world needs.

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



The Role

Hadrian is building the most advanced manufacturing platform in the world, and Workforce Development is the team responsible for ensuring our people can keep pace with it. As Hadrian scales, one of the most critical challenges we face is this: the knowledge that makes our manufacturing processes work lives inside a small group of subject matter experts. It is undocumented, informal, and at risk of being lost as the company grows.

The Workforce Knowledge Analyst exists to solve that problem. You will embed with SMEs across Hadrian's manufacturing operations, ask the right questions, and extract the process knowledge that would otherwise never be written down. Your output -- transcripts, video, written process notes -- becomes the foundation that Workforce Development builds training and certification programs from.

This is a role for someone who is naturally curious, earns trust quickly with technical experts, and gets genuine satisfaction from bringing clarity to complex, unfinished knowledge. You do not need to be a manufacturing expert. You need to be the kind of person who knows how to get inside what an expert knows and put it into a form that anyone can use.



What You'll Do

 - Knowledge Extraction: Embed with SMEs to observe, interview, and document how manufacturing processes actually work, surfacing the tribal knowledge that would otherwise remain undocumented.

 - Multi-format Documentation: Produce transcripts, video recordings, and written process notes that capture process knowledge comprehensively enough to serve as source material for Workforce Development and other teams.

 - SME Relationship Management: Build trusted working relationships with SMEs to maintain ongoing access to the knowledge needed to keep capability documentation current and accurate.

 - Process Observation: Spend time on the factory floor observing work in practice, identifying gaps between what is documented and how work actually happens.

 - Handoff to Workforce Systems: Package and hand off captured knowledge to Workforce Systems in a clear, organized format that can be structured into training content and certification frameworks.

 - Staying Current: Re-engage with SMEs when processes change, ensuring captured knowledge reflects the current state of each capability at all times.



What We're Looking For

 - Knowledge extraction: you know how to surface what people know but struggle to articulate. You ask questions that go beyond the obvious, follow threads, and document what you find without filtering it prematurely.

 - Active listening and observation: you pay close attention to both what people say and what they do. You catch the details and nuances that others miss, and you know that the most important information is often what no one thinks to mention.

 - Clear and thorough documentation: you produce written and recorded outputs that are accurate, comprehensive, and organized well enough for someone else to act on without needing to ask follow-up questions.

 - Credibility in technical environments: you earn trust with subject matter experts quickly. You ask intelligent questions, know when something important is being glossed over, and build the kind of relationships that give you ongoing access to knowledge.

 - Adaptability: you move between technical domains comfortably. You do not need to be a domain expert in every capability, but you pick up new processes and environments quickly and adjust your approach accordingly.



What Will Set You Apart

 - Experience conducting structured or semi-structured interviews with subject matter experts

 - Background in journalism, UX research, ethnographic research, technical writing, or documentary production

 - Familiarity with a manufacturing or industrial environment

 - Experience working in a regulated environment where documentation accuracy has real consequences

 - Background in a technical or engineering domain with a genuine interest in knowledge capture and documentation


BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 


CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

jobs.title: Manager, Sales Compensation
jobs.description:
Founded in 2018 with co-headquarters in Dublin and Boston, Tines powers some of the world's most important workflows. Our intelligent workflow platform applies AI, automation, and integration with human ingenuity to drive real business results.

Tines serves a diverse range of customers, from startups to public companies, including Canva, Databricks, Elastic, Kayak, Intercom, and McKesson. As an integrator across the entire tech stack, Tines is vendor-agnostic integrating with any API-enabled service. This flexibility enables our customers to achieve their highest-priority goals faster. And because Tines is secure and private by design, it’s popular with security, IT, engineering, finance, and other security-focused teams.

At Tines, we're driven by our values of Simplicity, Speed, and Soundness. We're committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences while fostering a company culture that nurtures individual curiosity, growth, and integrity. We’re excited about what’s next, and we’re looking for others to join us on our journey.

We're looking for a sales compensation leader to own how we pay our go-to-market organisation, and how that changes as our commercial model changes. You will run the engine that pays roughly 350 GTM people accurately and on time, own the design of the plans, quotas and incentives behind it, and lead a small team of analysts.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will manage and coach a small team, and you will also be in the model, in CaptivateIQ, and in the plan documents yourself.

What you'll do

Run the compensation engine

• Own the monthly and quarterly compensation cycle end to end: crediting, calculation, review, approval and payout, delivered accurately and on time

• Own CaptivateIQ as our system of record for incentive compensation, including plan build, rule logic, testing and release

• Own crediting and comp data integrity across Salesforce and downstream systems, and work with Systems and Deal Desk to fix problems at source rather than in spreadsheets

• Oversee inquiry management ensuring clear SLAs and report on trends to improve overall processes

• Document and keep policies and process up to date for stakeholders and your team

Design the plans, quotas and incentives

• Own annual plan design in partnership with your Senior compensation analyst, GTM leadership, FP&A and People for all commissioned roles

• Collaborate with Revops business partners on the quota setting process for each function to ensure it aligns with broader compensation strategy and benchmarks

• Model attainment distribution, benchmarks and support finance in ad-hoc cost reporting

• Own and build SPIFFs and non-cash incentive programmes, including President's Club,

• Own plan communication and enablement, so reps and managers understand what they are paid for and can self-serve where needed

Evolve the compensation strategy as we grow

• Build the compensation approach for an evolving pricing model and mulit-product business in partnership with the Head of Revenue Operations and VP of Finance

• Represent compensation requirements during larger CPQ and CRM enhancements or changes

• Enhance our approach based compensation reporting: attainment by role and segment, payout curves, quota coverage and programme effectiveness

Lead and grow the team

• Manage, coach and develop a small team of compensation analysts, and set the standard and what good looks like

• Prioritise the team's work, capacity and quarterly OKRs to ensure a balance of reactiveness and impactful projects

• Stay hands-on. This is a doing and leading role, not a management-only role

What you'll bring

Required experience

• 6+ years in sales compensation, revenue operations, sales finance or a closely related field, with experience managing or formally mentoring analysts

• 2-3 years direct management experience

• Proven ownership of a full incentive compensation cycle for a distributed GTM team, including crediting, calculation, payout and dispute resolution

• Hands-on administration of an ICM platform, ideally CaptivateIQ, including building and testing plan logic yourself

• Demonstrated plan design experience: pay mix, leverage, accelerators and quota setting, with the modelling to back the recommendation

• Strong Salesforce data fluency, and the ability to translate commercial requirements into system and crediting logic

• Advanced Excel or Google Sheets modelling, including capacity, attainment and cost of sale models

• Excellent stakeholder management, with the credibility to hold a position with Sales leaders and the judgement to know when to flex

• You can communicate simply, clearly, and directly, especially with senior leaders, and your written work is polished enough to go straight to an executive audience

Bonus points

• Experience with consumption, usage-based or hybrid pricing models and their compensation implications

• Experience through a CPQ or quote-to-cash migration, ideally Salesforce CPQ or Dealhub

• Experience in cybersecurity, IT or AI markets

• Familiarity with ASC 606 commission capitalisation and audit requirements

• Experience compensating post-sales and partner roles, not just AEs

Compensation: $153k-$183k OTE

jobs.title: Training Specialist
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Aspire is seeking a Training Specialist to deliver practical, engaging, and role-specific training that helps employees succeed across our human services, educational, clinical, administrative, and community-based programs.

The Training Specialist partners with program leaders, schools, administrative teams, Quality Assurance,
People & Culture, Clinical Services, Operations, and other departments to assess training needs, develop effective learning solutions, and reinforce best practices in real-world work environments.

This field-based role translates policies, systems, regulations, and quality standards into clear, practical training. The position requires strong facilitation skills, sound judgment, independent decision-making, and the ability to support adult learners with diverse roles and experience levels.

Schedule & Pay

• Schedule: M - F 8:30am - 4:30pm

• Pay Rate: $45k - $55k

• Role: Salaried & Exempt

• Location: Must be located within commuting distance of Hamden, CT - Hybrid 3 times a week minimum

Key Responsibilities

Training Delivery and Facilitation

• Facilitate required, role-specific, and assigned training programs across Aspire service lines.

• Deliver training in multiple formats, including in-person, virtual, onsite, and small-group sessions.

• Support onboarding programs such as All On Board and other new-hire training initiatives.

• Adapt facilitation methods to meet the needs of frontline, clinical, educational, and administrative employees.

• Provide coaching, observational feedback, and skill-building support to employees and managers.

• Participate in agency-wide learning initiatives, including micro-trainings during community meetings.

• This position will need to train to be a CT Investigator.

Field-Based Training and Practice Support

• Maintain a regular presence in Aspire programs, schools, offices, and team environments.

• Deliver training and coaching in real-world settings to reinforce skill application.

• Support supervisors with practice observations, feedback, and competency assessment.

• Share relevant observations with leadership and Quality Assurance partners to support follow-up and continuous improvement.

Training Needs Assessment and Quality Partnership

• Identify, analyze, and prioritize training needs using observation, employee feedback, quality reviews, and operational data.

• Participate in cross-functional meetings and workgroups to identify emerging training needs.

• Design and implement practical solutions, including training sessions, job aids, coaching, and refresher resources.

• Interpret regulatory changes, system updates, and quality concerns to determine appropriate training responses.

• Evaluate and escalate issues that require solutions beyond training.

• Recommend performance improvement strategies that support operational and quality objectives.

Curriculum and Content Development

• Deliver training aligned with Aspire policies, regulatory requirements, evidence-based practices, and quality standards.

• Create original learning materials, including: Facilitator guides Job aids Checklists Quick-reference guides Videos Frequently asked questions

• Apply adult learning principles to promote engagement, knowledge retention, and on-the-job performance.

• Analyze feedback, trends, and operational changes to improve training content and delivery methods.

• Share effective training practices and resources across programs, schools, and departments.

Technology and Systems Training

• Deliver training on systems such as Therap, Relias, UKG, Microsoft 365, and other assigned platforms.

• Serve in system administration roles, such as Super Admin, when assigned.

• Support employees and managers in accessing and using training resources.

• Provide follow-up assistance, refresher training, and implementation support for system updates.

New-Hire Onboarding and Manager Development

• Organize and facilitate the All On Board onboarding program.

• Support new hires throughout the onboarding process.

• Partner with Human Resources and organizational leaders to support manager development in areas such as: Supervision Documentation Scheduling Basic financial processes Compliance expectations Employee performance support

Training Compliance and Documentation

• Track and maintain accurate employee training records.

• Use systems such as Therap and Relias to document training completion and compliance.

• Support accurate reporting and follow-up related to required training.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Collaborate with Quality Assurance, Operations, Clinical Services, Children’s Services, People & Culture, Finance, Compliance, and other departments.

• Participate in meetings, workgroups, and organizational improvement initiatives.

• Perform additional duties as assigned to support Aspire’s operational and service goals.

Decision-Making and Scope of Responsibility

The Training Specialist exercises discretion and independent judgment when:

• Selecting instructional methods and adapting content for different audiences.

• Prioritizing training activities based on organizational needs.

• Interpreting policies, regulations, and quality standards.

• Developing training and performance improvement recommendations.

• Determining when an issue requires a solution beyond training.

• Managing field visits, scheduling, and day-to-day training activities under general direction from the Regional Training Manager.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in training, education, human services, organizational development, business, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.

• Two to three years of experience in human services, employee training, education, quality assurance, organizational development, or a related field.

• Experience facilitating training for adult learners required.

• Experience working in or supporting residential, day, school, clinical, community-based, or administrative service environments preferred.

• Experience creating training materials and using learning management, documentation, or compliance systems preferred.

• Valid driver’s license and successful completion of a background check required.

Skills and Abilities

• Strong in-person and virtual facilitation and presentation skills.

• Ability to translate complex policies, systems, and regulations into clear, practical instruction.

• Knowledge of adult learning principles and effective instructional design.

• Strong relationship-building, coaching, and collaboration skills.

• Excellent written communication and content development abilities.

• Ability to use data, observations, and feedback to identify trends and training needs.

• Strong organization, prioritization, time management, and attention to detail.

• Comfort using technology and learning new software systems quickly.

• Ability to work independently while aligning with team and organizational priorities.

• Commitment to person-centered services, inclusion, quality, continuous improvement, and Aspire’s mission.

Working Conditions

• Regular travel to Aspire locations throughout Connecticut, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, and Maryland.

• Frequent use of computers, video conferencing platforms, office equipment, and other technology.

• Physical activity may include standing, presenting, walking through work environments, and lifting materials weighing up to 10 pounds.

• Reasonable accommodations are available as needed.

• Comprehensive Health, Dental, & Vision Insurance - Choose from multiple medical plans, with vision coverage included at no extra cost.

• Lifestyle Spending Accounts with JOON - Monthly funds for wellness, fitness, commuting, childcare, pet care, and more.

You'll perform a variety of tasks, with clear pathways for growth:

• System Repairs: Address issues with aftertreatment systems (DEF/emissions), perform regens, and change filters.

• Collaborate & Optimize: Work with your team to maintain accurate records, optimize vehicle performance, and minimize downtime.

• Safety First: Adhere to all safety protocols and industry best practices to ensure our fleet is always DOT compliant.

What We're Looking For

We're searching for skilled professionals with a strong background in diesel technology.

• Experience: 3+ years of experience with Heavy-Duty Class 8 trucks and trailers or similar equipment (e.g., agricultural, construction, waste collection truck).

• Technical Skills:

• Strong diagnostic and troubleshooting skills for diesel engines, transmissions, and vehicle systems.

• Proficiency with diagnostic software and using a laptop for manuals.

• Experience with aftertreatment systems and electrical diagnostics.

• Comfortable with MIG welding is a plus.

• A minimum of two ASE Certifications within the first 6 months of employment (we'll reimburse you!).

• Requirements:

• A valid Driver's License with clean driving record

• Ability to perform physical tasks associated with vehicle maintenance (lifting, bending, etc.).

• Strong attention to detail and a commitment to quality workmanship.

• A solid attendance record and punctuality are essential for this role.

At Carvana, we're on a mission to change the way people buy cars. We're a technology company bringing transparency and convenience to the car buying process. Our team members are our greatest asset, and we're committed to providing a workplace where everyone can thrive.

jobs.title: Senior Azure DevOps Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Azure DevOps Engineer

Your Opportunity:

At PLACE, we’re building a category-defining company at the intersection of real estate, technology, business services, and the consumer. As a profitable, hypergrowth startup, on the path to an IPO, our standards are high, and our team is scrappy, and our commitment is to execute the best work of our lives.

This is YOUR CHANCE to shape the backbone of a company that’s scaling rapidly and innovating boldly. As our Senior Azure DevOps Engineer, you’ll partner with our Platform & Infrastructure Engineering leadership, founders, and executives to architect and govern our enterprise Azure cloud platform, drive CI/CD and infrastructure automation strategy, and set the technical standards that keep our systems secure, scalable, and reliable across every engineering team. If you thrive in complexity, entrepreneurial problem-solving, and believe in scaling through tech and AI, this is your PLACE. This is a hybrid role based in Bethesda, MD.

Who Develops You: VP Software Engineering and IT Operations

What You’re Great At:

You are a hands-on cloud platform expert who thinks in systems, not just servers. You’ve spent years deep in Azure — App Services, AKS, Key Vault, API Management — and you know how to turn that expertise into infrastructure-as-code that other engineers can trust and build on. You’re as comfortable designing a zero-downtime deployment strategy as you are leading a root-cause analysis after a production incident. Security and cost aren’t afterthoughts for you; they’re built into every architecture decision you make. You mentor generously, communicate clearly with product and engineering leadership, and you’ve got the scars — and the certifications — to prove you’ve done this at scale before.

What You’ll Do:

• Design and maintain enterprise Azure infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code (IaC); establish and enforce cloud architecture standards and operational best practices.

• Develop reusable infrastructure modules and deployment patterns, and monitor/optimize Azure infrastructure costs (FinOps) without compromising reliability.

• Design, implement, and govern Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines; standardize deployment processes across multiple development teams, including blue-green, canary, and zero-downtime strategies.

• Design and maintain load-testing environments and automated performance testing strategies; validate auto-scaling configurations for Azure App Services, AKS, APIs, and databases.

• Implement security controls aligned with enterprise standards, including Azure Key Vault, Managed Identity, RBAC, and least-privilege access models.

• Design, configure, and maintain Azure WAF policies and Azure API Management (APIM), including throttling, rate limiting, and API governance standards.

• Implement enterprise observability using Azure Monitor, Application Insights, and Log Analytics/KQL; lead root cause analysis following production incidents.

• Mentor engineers on Azure, DevOps, automation, and cloud-native architecture; lead technical design reviews and serve as subject matter expert for cloud operations and platform reliability.

• Partner with product and engineering teams using Agile/Scrum practices to align infrastructure delivery with business priorities.

Salary: $150,000-$155,000/year depending on experience.

Why PLACE:

We believe people do their best work when they’re trusted, supported, and surrounded by others who are equally driven. That’s why this role includes a “work from the PLACE you work best” approach – at home, in an office, or on the move. Our competitive benefits include PTO as needed, comprehensive insurance coverage, a 401(k) match, stock option grants, and a stock purchase plan. Every team member is an owner, building the “PLACE” they are proud to call “my company.”

jobs.title: Treasury & Finance Operations Manager
jobs.location: New York Support Office, 55 Water Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201
jobs.description:
The Role...

At Soho House, the Treasury & Fin Ops Manager will be in-market lead for treasury operations, cash disbursements and related financial controls across the North America business, providing the day-to-day link between our North America sites, US support office and the Soho Hub, our Finance Hub in the UK.

With core transaction processing and accounting activities managed centrally by the Soho Hub, this role provides critical in-market oversight of cash and payment activities and ensure the global treasury, payment and finance policies operate effectively across the US and Canada.

The role provides US time-zone coverage for time-sensitive treasury and payment matters, exercise judgement over exceptional cash requirements, supports the integrity of banking and payment controls and acts as a two-way liaison between local operations and the Hub. The role is also responsible for ensuring that time-critical financial and statutory matters requiring a local presence are appropriately managed and escalated.

Main Duties...

Treasury operations, cash management and controls

• Act as the North America point of contact for day-to-day treasury and cash management matters between our sites, US support office and the Soho Hub, supporting operations spanning four time zones.

• Provide in-market oversight of cash disbursement activities and related controls, ensuring payments are appropriately authorized, supported and executed in accordance with global treasury and finance policies.

• Support effective cash and banking controls across North America, identifying local workarounds or control gaps, agreeing remediation with the Soho Hub and escalating material exceptions.

• Partner with local FP&A, operations and the Soho Hub to ensure appropriate visibility of time-sensitive cash requirements and payment obligations.

• Promote strong cash management and financial risk awareness among non-Finance colleagues, ensuring treasury and payment control expectations are understood and applied consistently at site level.

Time-critical payments and treasury escalations

• Own US time-zone coverage for urgent treasury, cash and payment escalations across North America outside UK support hours.

• Exercise judgement over exceptional and time-sensitive funding and payment requirements, determining which requests require immediate action and which should be challenged or deferred through standard processes.

• Approve and facilitate exceptional payments within agreed delegated authority limits where deferring to the next working day would create material operational, regulatory or employee risk, including:

• F&B vendor payment holds that could prevent a House from opening a kitchen for service;

• Liquor holds with the potential to disrupt supply from vendors within a state;

• Regulatory or compliance payments required immediately for a House to continue trading;

• Same-day contractual payments required for scheduled events or performances; and

• Same-day employee payments where required by state law.

• Protect the integrity of the treasury and payment control environment while operating at pace, ensuring exceptional disbursements receive appropriate local approval and are communicated to the Soho Hub for subsequent accounting, reporting and compliance.

• Maintain a complete audit trail of exceptional treasury and payment activity, monitor root causes and escalate recurring issues for permanent resolution.

Financial authorities and statutory matters

• Serve as an in-market finance contact for relevant local city and state authorities where a US presence is required, helping ensure time-sensitive financial and regulatory matters are appropriately managed.

• Ensure time-critical financial and statutory correspondence is acknowledged, logged, routed to the appropriate owner and tracked to closure for US legal entities, including correspondence from tax authorities, labor authorities, lenders, insurers and legal or regulatory bodies.

• Coordinate with the Soho Hub, Tax, Legal, FP&A and other local stakeholders to ensure financial obligations arising from statutory correspondence are assessed and actioned ahead of applicable deadlines.

• Receive, log and route physical financial documentation and cheques where an in-market presence is unavoidable.

Treasury process improvement and stakeholder partnership

• Support North America sites and the US support office in complying with global treasury, cash management and payment processes, reinforcing established Hub processes and redirecting transactional activity to the Soho Hub as appropriate.

• Act as the in-market partner to the Soho Hub in resolving treasury, payment and site compliance issues at source.

• Identify recurring payment issues, manual processes, control gaps and business workarounds and partner with the Soho Hub to develop sustainable process improvements.

• Support continued enhancement of treasury controls, payment processes and ways of working as the North America finance operating model evolves.

• Promote a risk-aware and compliance-focused culture by providing guidance and support to local and Hub teams on treasury processes, payment controls and policy adherence.

• Invest in continuous professional development to enhance treasury, financial risk and broader finance capabilities.

• Perform additional duties as assigned by management.

Requirements...

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business or related discipline; treasury or accounting qualification (e.g., CTP, CPA, ACA, ACCA or CIMA) desirable but not required.

• 5+ years of finance experience, with relevant experience across treasury operations, cash management, payments, banking or financial controls.

• Experience operating in a centralized or shared-services finance environment and partnering with remote processing teams.

• Practical experience with cash disbursements, payment controls, banking processes and financial risk management.

• Experience in a multi-site, multi-entity environment; hospitality, leisure or retail experience desirable.

Technical knowledge and systems

• Strong understanding of treasury and payment controls, authorization frameworks, audit trails and segregation of duties.

• Understanding of cash management, banking operations and payment processes.

• ERP / finance systems experience required; Oracle experience desirable.

In-market and regulatory knowledge

• Familiarity with US federal and state authority correspondence and associated financial obligations desirable.

• Working knowledge of US unclaimed property (escheatment) requirements desirable.

Skills and personal attributes

• Strong judgement in assessing and challenging time-sensitive cash and payment requirements while maintaining controls.

• Ability to balance operational urgency with treasury governance, financial risk and global policy requirements.

• Highly organized and detail-focused, with the ability to manage time-critical activity across UK and US time zones.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the confidence to work across Operations, FP&A, Tax, Legal and centralized Finance teams.

• Able to work independently with confidential financial information and exercise sound judgement under pressure.

• Calm, pragmatic and solutions-oriented, with a strong understanding of financial risk and control.

Why work with us...

Soho House offers competitive compensation packages that feature global benefits and perks. Whether you’re seeking entry-level employment or a new opportunity to expand your profession, we offer training to develop the technical and managerial skills necessary to enhance your career.

• Health Care + 401K: Full time employees are eligible for full benefits; Medical, Dental & Vision as well as Retirement fund with a 2% match

• Paid Time Off: Full- Time Employees have sick day's + vacation days

• Career Development: Soho House can progress your career domestically or internationally as well as managerially or technically

• Soho Impact: Empowering the Soho House Community to make positive change, through mentoring, apprenticeship, local outreach and sustainability

• Learning & Development: An extensive range of internally and externally run courses are available for all employees.

• Cookhouse & House Tonic: Celebrating our passion for food and drink. Check out our monthly calendars and get involved in trips, training's and events. Available to all.

• Team Events: From fitness sessions to cinema screenings and art classes, each month we hold a series of fun events which you can sign up to.

• Team Meal: Whilst on duty in our Houses & Restaurants you will be provided with a substantial meal free of charge.
