jobs.title: Staff Product Manager - Data Supply Expansion
jobs.description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

About the Team
Our Network Enablement and Access team’s mission is to unlock the potential of the Plaid network by broadening and deepening our connection to data partners. We do this by providing solutions that allow our data partners to be part of the network and by providing best in class connections. By expanding and improving our connections to data providers, we are able to strengthen the Plaid network while also enabling great products and experiences.

Plaid's data access platform owns the deep-infrastructure layer that determines how reliably and efficiently data flows from our data providers to our customers. As the data supply network evolves, we are building the new platform capabilities that keep it strong: ensuring that our traffic stays smooth for the providers we depend on, building improved detection capabilities that enable us to catch issues as they happen, and evolving our data access toolkit to be more efficient over time.

About the role:

You will decide what data Plaid goes after next. Bank data got us here, but the picture our customers need now includes things we do not have: property tax, merchant and SKU-level purchases, utilities, tax, payroll. Some of it we should build with our own technology. Some of it we should partner or pay for. Someone has to make those calls with conviction and a real business case behind them, and that person is you.

This is a 0-1 role. You will start with two to three engineers and a mandate to prove something real: Plaid's first non-bank data offering, live, inside your first year. Along the way you will set the multi-year strategy for supply expansion, define what quality and completeness mean for data types nobody here has worked with before, and build the internal case that turns a promising vertical into a funded bet.

Responsibilities:

 - Set the multi-year strategy for non-bank data supply, grounded in what our products and customers need rather than what is technically interesting

 - Build and quickly execute against the one year plan - showcasing fast momentum and impact

 - Force-rank new data types across the company and own the business case for each, including the ones you recommend against

 - Make and defend build, buy, and partner decisions alongside data partnerships, corporate development, and legal

 - Ship Plaid's first non-bank data offerings, as internal insight inputs or externalized to customers

 - Partner with engineering and data teams on the taxonomies, quality controls, and coverage metrics that new data types require

 - Define the metrics for supply expansion and report progress to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders

Qualifications:

 - 8+ years of experience, including 5+ in product management or equivalent founder/operator roles.

 - Analytical rigor: You are comfortable working directly with data, cost models, and operational metrics to make and defend complex decisions.

 - Deep technical fluency: You can reason about large-scale systems, load management, API platforms, and machine-learning models and engage engineers as a close product partner.

 - Platform & systems thinking mindset: You think in systems, and design for reuse and the long term.

 - Leadership, stakeholder influence, and communication :You should be comfortable working cross-functionally (engineering, data, product) and influencing without direct authority. You must be able to explain complex technical ideas to non-technical stakeholders, drive alignment, and make trade-offs crystal clear

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!

We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. jobs.title: Lab Support Specialist
jobs.description:
Legend Biotech is a global biotechnology company dedicated to treating and, one day, curing life-threatening diseases. Headquartered in Bridgewater, New Jersey, we are advancing the next generation of cell therapy through a portfolio of innovative technologies, including autologous, allogeneic, and in vivo cell therapy approaches. Our research spans chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T), T-cell receptor (TCR-T), natural killer (NK) cell-based therapies, and other emerging platforms designed to transform the treatment of serious diseases. From our global network of research and development sites, we are committed to discovering and developing safe, effective, and cutting-edge therapies for patients worldwide.

Legend Biotech entered into a global collaboration agreement with Johnson & Johnson to jointly develop and commercialize CARVYKTI® (ciltacabtagene autoleucel; cilta-cel). Through this strategic partnership, we combine complementary expertise and capabilities to advance innovative immunotherapies for patients living with multiple myeloma.

Legend Biotech is seeking a Lab Support Specialist as part of the Information Technology team based in Somerset, NJ.

Role Overview

The Lab Support Specialist will assist in the operation of laboratory IT capabilities and R&D systems. This individual’s responsibilities will include supporting, and in some cases coordinating, the end-to-end process of onboarding an instrument system into a laboratory, from procuring the computer according to vendor specifications, connecting it to the network, configuring the instrument with the vendor, conducting risk assessments, and qualifying the system according to GxP procedures where applicable. In addition, the ideal candidate will provide operational support for existing laboratory computing devices and scientific applications.

Key Responsibilities

• The critical nature of these systems requires appropriate support to ensure a highly stable, secure, and reliable computing environment.

• This role will provide support and systems management for the laboratory computing environment in accordance with IT policies and procedures.

• Adherence to standard operating procedures, timely execution of work, and collaboration with scientists, IT colleagues, and vendors are essential to maximize productivity for bench scientists and ensure the integrity of both the laboratory data collected and the systems used to collect that data.

• Collaborate with scientists, vendors, and IT colleagues on new systems implementation, integration, and administration.

• Participate in the installation, documentation, and testing of instrument systems.

• Assist with the implementation of new capabilities and upgrades to existing computer systems utilized in the laboratory, including instrument software, operating systems, computer hardware, and additional PC accessories.

• Aid in troubleshooting and provide technical support for instrument software installed on laboratory computers, as well as connectivity between computers and instruments.

• Aid in troubleshooting and provide technical support for various laboratory equipment, including firmware and network connectivity where applicable.

• Provision user accounts on standalone and network-connected laboratory equipment and instruments.

• Provision user accounts for scientific software such as FlowJo, Zageno, SnapGene, journal subscriptions, and other related applications.

• Provide support for computer equipment and peripherals within GMP suites while following Grade B gowning and cleaning protocols.

• Contribute to the development of standard operating procedures (SOPs) and work instructions for the area.

• Assist in completing necessary risk assessments and qualification protocols to support the GxP applicability of instrument systems where applicable.

• Coordinate with engineering, facilities, and quality teams to ensure the timely installation, commissioning, and qualification of laboratory instruments and IT systems.

• Track, document, and update incidents and service requests accurately within the IT Service Management (ITSM) system.

• Assist in updating and maintaining knowledge base articles.

Requirements

• BS degree with 2 years of experience in the biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry.

• Understanding of laboratory science within the life sciences industry, preferably in the cell therapy space.

• Understanding of GxP software administration and configuration.

• Understanding of Windows-based operating systems.

• Experience installing, configuring, and supporting systems and applications in laboratory environments.

• Experience with direct customer and user interaction, including training.

• Demonstrated understanding of the need for standards, along with a willingness to provide input for improving strategies that support the laboratory computing environment.

• Experience supporting standalone or enterprise computerized systems and applications.

• Commitment to quality.

• Strong problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work on multiple complex assignments, supporting both routine and project activities, while demonstrating adaptability to changing priorities within a cutting-edge industry and scientific environment.

• Willingness to actively contribute to the team by offering candid and constructive feedback while supporting final decisions. Takes shared ownership of outcomes and works collaboratively to address issues with a high level of professionalism.

• Takes direction well and demonstrates a conscientious, team-first approach.

• Demonstrates professional integrity and is highly organized and detail-oriented.

• Familiarity with ticketing systems such as ServiceNow, Jira, or similar platforms.

• Knowledge of the software development lifecycle (SDLC) and computer systems validation (CSV).

• Proficient knowledge and understanding of Microsoft Office applications, including Access, Excel, Project, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams, and Word, as well as other relevant software programs.

• Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills with a service-oriented attitude. Must contribute to a collaborative, team-based, and positive environment while demonstrating a clear sense of purpose and a strong commitment to business goals.

Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. We bring these commitments to life through three core behaviors: ownership and collaboration, trust through outcomes and impact, and a challenge culture with ongoing feedback. Ready to make an impact at the company pioneering security transformation in the AI era? Join us at Zscaler.

Role
We are seeking a hands-on, self-starting Principal Technical Marketing Engineer with deep networking and monitoring expertise to drive technical enablement, customer validation, and field readiness for our next-generation Zero Trust Branch and Zscaler Digital Experience solutions. In this remote role, you will report to the Director of Product Management within the Zscaler Digital Experience department, serving as a critical bridge between our field teams and core engineering. Your mission is to accelerate adoption, reduce sales friction, and standardize post-sales time-to-value through hands-on technical validation and world-class enablement collateral.

Who You Are (Success Profile)

• You thrive in ambiguity, comfortably building the path as you walk it and seeing uncertainty as the raw material to create something meaningful.

• You are a learner with a true growth mindset, actively seeking feedback to continuously develop yourself and build stronger partnerships.

• You are deeply customer-obsessed, anchoring your decisions in solving real-world challenges for both internal and external stakeholders.

What We're Looking For

• Demonstrated curiosity and active exploration of AI tools, with a proven history of integrating new technologies to enhance daily workflows and augment problem-solving

• Proven track record of leading hands-on customer Proof of Value (POV) pilots and executive architectural evaluations

• 10+ years of hands-on experience in technical marketing, product management, or solutions architecture

• Advanced packet analysis and troubleshooting expertise using Wireshark, tcpdump, and traffic generation tools to diagnose routing anomalies, latency/jitter, MTU issues, and NAT/firewall traversal

What Will Make You Stand Out

Join us at Curaleaf to be part of a high-growth, purpose-driven company that champions corporate social responsibility through our Rooted in Good initiative, supporting community outreach and positive change. Retail Buyer
The candidate must be able to work on-site 5 days a week at either our Stamford, CT, or Wakefield, MA office.
Compensation is negotiable and will be based on qualifications and experience.

Travel requirements: 25%

About the Role:
As a Retail Buyer, you will lead sourcing, purchasing, and planning efforts for retail Curaleaf locations in the Northeast region, strategically managing the retail assortment to align with customer needs and market trends. Your role will involve analyzing data, forecasting, pricing, and inventory planning to drive sales and ensure an optimal product mix. You will foster strong vendor partnerships, negotiate pricing, and continuously seek new opportunities for business growth.

What You’ll Do:

• Strategic Buying & Planning Drive the strategic direction for assigned categories, ensuring competitive pricing, relevant assortment, and compelling promotions to enhance the customer shopping experience. Analyze market trends and customer preferences to select brands and items that align with current and future needs. Develop a bottom-up financial plan to meet category and total area sales and margin goals.

Partners with inventory and supply chain teams to ensure inventory optimization and support promotional activities. • Strong understanding of inventory management principles, product lifecycle planning, and replenishment strategies to maximize sales while minimizing inventory risk.

jobs.title: Security Architect
jobs.description:
This role is based in our Newton, MA office.

We are seeking a strategic Security Architect to define and drive our cloud and enterprise security architecture. You will own the security architecture vision, establish governance frameworks, and partner with Product, Engineering, and Infrastructure teams to embed security throughout our technology ecosystem.

Core Responsibilities

• Strategic Architecture & Governance

• Own and evolve the enterprise security architecture, including long-term roadmap and reference architectures for cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments
• Define organizational security principles, frameworks, and standards that align with business objectives and regulatory requirements
• Develop and present security strategy, roadmaps, and strategic initiatives to executive leadership and stakeholders
• Establish security metrics and KPIs to measure architecture effectiveness and communicate security posture to senior leadership
• Ensure compliance with industry regulations and standards including ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, and SOX
• Lead security audits and assessments, driving remediation plans and continuous improvement initiative

Cloud & Infrastructure Security

• Own cloud security architecture across AWS and GCP, including Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM), Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM), and Wiz remediation strategies
• Design and implement Identity and Access Management (IAM) architecture based on least privilege principles and Zero Trust security models
• Architect secure network segmentation strategies and defense-in-depth controls across all infrastructure layers
• Own the architecture and strategic direction for key security platforms including SIEM, vulnerability management, endpoint security, and threat detection systems
• Manage and optimize internal security platforms to ensure robust protection of organizational assets
• Design secure cloud infrastructures and hybrid environment protections that scale with business growth
• Conduct threat modeling and risk analyses to identify infrastructure vulnerabilities and recommend mitigation strategies

Application & Development Security

• Lead Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) and DevSecOps initiatives across the organization
• Integrate security controls into CI/CD pipelines, championing shift-left security practices in collaboration with DevOps leadership
• Ensure software architecture and applications are designed to mitigate vulnerabilities and prevent exploits
• Provide technical guidance and mentorship to development and DevOps teams on secure coding practices and emerging threats
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to embed security throughout the system development lifecycle
• Define security requirements and controls that support agile development while maintaining strong security posture

Innovation & Technical Leadership

• Lead security architecture for emerging technologies including AI/LLM initiatives, ensuring responsible and secure implementation
• Serve as the technical authority on security architecture, advising on security-related technologies and assessing risks associated with proposed changes
• Stay current with emerging security threats, vulnerabilities, and technologies to drive continuous innovation in security practices
• Inspire and influence engineering teams to execute security principles and adopt security-first mindsets
• Mentor and provide technical guidance to DevOps, operations, and development teams on security best practices
• Partner strategically with Product, Engineering, and Infrastructure leaders to align security architecture with business innovation
• Drive thought leadership through security documentation, architecture diagrams, design specifications, and security control matrices

Additional Responsibilities

• Lead incident response management and develop security policies that protect organizational assets from cyber threats
• Identify organizational vulnerabilities and weaknesses through systematic security assessments
• Recommend and implement security controls and solutions that balance security requirements with business enablement

• Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, information technology or a related field
• 7+ years of cybersecurity experience with deep cloud security expertise
• Proven track record leading enterprise security architecture in multi-cloud environments
• Deep understanding of cloud service provider security best practices around (AWS, GCP)Organization PoliciesAutomated threat detection toolsCentral logging/Siem practicesLest privilege architectureVPC design/perimeter controlsData Exfiltration preventionEncryption/Key Management designIdentity and Access Management (IAM) best practices.
• Web application security testing: Expertise in identifying and mitigating vulnerabilities in web applications, leveraging tools and methodologies like OWASP.
• Network vulnerability scanning: Skilled in detecting and addressing vulnerabilities in network configurations and infrastructure.
• Container and Kubernetes security: Proficiency in securing containerized environments, including Docker and Kubernetes, using best practices and tools like Trivy or Aqua Security.
• Experience with security testing tools and platforms: Familiarity with industry-standard tools for vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, and security auditing.
• Ability to lead security discussions with system architects and business leaders.
• Strong analytical and computer skills

Expert level understanding of cybersecurity and how it affects the modern business world.

• Thorough understanding of Unix operation systems
• Awareness of frameworks such as NIST, COBIT, ISO and Soc2
• Certifications: CISSP, CCSP, AWS Security Specialty, or Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer

The Transportation Design Specialist supports the planning and design of transportation infrastructure projects for state and local agencies. This experienced technical role develops high-quality design plans and digital models using MicroStation and OpenRoads Designer (ORD), applies applicable roadway design standards, and serves as a mentor and trainer to strengthen transportation design capabilities across HEI.

Essential Functions

• Prepare preliminary and final design plans for urban and rural roadway, highway, intersection, bridge approach, pedestrian, and related transportation improvement projects.
• Develop and maintain roadway geometry, alignments, profiles, corridors, cross sections, terrain models, drainage components, quantities, and plan sheets using MicroStation and OpenRoads Designer (ORD).
• Apply applicable Department of Transportation and local agency design standards, specifications, file structures, workspace requirements, and electronic delivery procedures.
• Coordinate with engineers, project managers, survey staff, and other technical team members to translate survey, design, and engineering information into accurate and complete project deliverables.
• Perform technical drafting appropriate to the position, and assist with the preparation of opinions of probable construction cost, quantities, specifications, and supporting documentation.
• Conduct quality control reviews of models, drawings, plan sets, and related deliverables for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and compliance with project requirements.
• Identify design, production, and software issues; recommend practical solutions; and help establish efficient and consistent transportation design workflows.
• Serve as a technical resource for MicroStation and ORD, including troubleshooting design and production questions and sharing best practices across project teams.
• While not required, there are opportunities to develop and deliver formal and informal training, reference materials, standards, and workflow guidance for employees with varying levels of MicroStation and ORD experience.
• Assist project teams with workload coordination and help provide redundancy for key transportation design and plan-production functions.
• Participate in project meetings and communicate effectively regarding design status, technical needs, priorities, schedules, and deliverables.

jobs.title: Content Lead
jobs.description:
About the role

Twist Bioscience is looking for a senior Content Lead to be the strategic and creative owner of how we sound, everywhere we show up. This is a partner-level seat at the table for brand voice, content strategy, content marketing, evergreen and funnel content, and integrated 360 campaigns, not a "write the blog posts" role. You'll work across marketing, brand, product, and sales to make sure every word we put into the world, from a landing page headline to a trade show campaign to a technical white paper, sounds like it came from the same company and pulls its weight commercially.

We need someone who has done this from both sides of the table. Agency-side, where you learned to move fast, pitch ideas, and defend creative under pressure. In-house, where you learned to build systems, work within scientific and regulatory guardrails, and make content strategy stick over the long haul. Life sciences or biotech/pharma experience is essential; you should be comfortable translating complex science into content that's accurate, credible, and still genuinely compelling to read.

What you'll own

• Brand voice and content strategy. Define and evolve our brand voice, tone, and messaging frameworks, and make sure they're actually usable, not just a slide in a deck nobody opens.

• Content marketing. Set the strategy and quality bar for content marketing across channels, and partner with writers, designers, and marketers to execute against it.

• Evergreen content. Build and maintain the core library of content that represents who we are and what we do, the kind that doesn't expire with a campaign calendar.

• Funnel content. Architect content across the funnel, from awareness through consideration through conversion, so every stage has the right message in the right format for the right audience.

• 360 campaigns. Act as the words lead on integrated campaigns spanning digital, events, sales enablement, PR, and social, making sure the creative concept and the copy are built together instead of bolted on at the end.

• Cross-functional partnership. Be the go-to partner for product marketing, brand, design, and sales on anything language-related, including naming, positioning, messaging hierarchies, and campaign concepts.

• Team and process leadership. Set standards, give sharp and constructive feedback, and build the systems (style guides, briefs, review processes) that let a growing content function scale without losing quality or voice.

What you bring

• 10+ years of experience across content strategy, content marketing, and brand/copywriting, with meaningful time spent in a senior or leadership capacity.

• A career that spans both agency and in-house environments. You understand how each shapes the way you work, and you know how to get the best of both.

• Direct experience in life sciences, biotech, pharma, or a related scientific/technical industry, with a demonstrated ability to make dense, technical subject matter feel clear and human.

• A strong point of view on brand voice and a portfolio that shows range, from a single perfectly-tuned headline to a fully integrated campaign.

• Proven experience building and executing content strategy across the full funnel, not just producing individual assets.

• Experience leading 360/integrated campaigns and collaborating closely with creative, design, and media partners.

• Excellent editorial judgment and the confidence to push back on stakeholders, including senior ones, when the words aren't working.

• Comfort operating both strategically (frameworks, roadmaps, positioning) and in the weeds, actually writing and editing when it counts.

Nice to have

• Experience writing for regulated or scientifically rigorous industries where accuracy and compliance are non-negotiable.

• Background managing or mentoring a team of writers, editors, or content strategists.

• Familiarity with SEO, content performance measurement, and using data to inform content decisions.

The base cash compensation for this California-based role is below. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for bonus, equity, and a generous benefits package. Final compensation amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate skill, experience, expertise, and location and may vary from the amount listed above. Compensation may be different in other locations.

San Francisco Bay Area Pay Range

$147,000—$201,000 USD

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Data Governance & Master Data Management
jobs.description:
The Director, Enterprise Data Governance & Master Data Management will be responsible for establishing and leading Relias's enterprise-wide data governance, master data management, and business information strategy necessary to support our evolution into a data-driven and AI-enabled organization. Reporting into the CFO organization, this leader will serve as the central authority for enterprise data definitions, stewardship, quality, ownership, and governance across all business and product domains.

The Director will also serve as the enterprise Data Governance Lead supporting Relias’ privacy operations and Data Subject Access Request (“DSAR”) operating model. In this capacity, the Director will be accountable for the enterprise data inventory and map, data stewardship, classification, lineage, and know where personal data starts, where it gets copied or sent, which systems should be addressed first, how that map stays current, and who must certify that each system handled a privacy request correctly. The Director will partner closely with the Privacy Operations, Legal, Information Security, Product, Engineering, Data & Analytics, Marketing, Customer Success, Support, HR, Procurement, and individual system owners.

The Director will create the framework that allows Relias to operate from a single source of truth by aligning Product, Engineering, Revenue, Finance, Customer Success, Operations, and Corporate functions around common business definitions, trusted reporting, governed data assets, and enterprise-wide accountability. This role will lead the development of enterprise data policies, stewardship programs, governance councils, master data standards, metadata practices, and data quality frameworks that support executive decision making, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, analytics, and AI initiatives.

The Director will support the implementation and ongoing governance of enterprise data-discovery, catalog, lineage, master-data, and privacy-operations technologies, including the data mapping and stewardship components of any DSAR automation platform.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

• Enterprise Data Governance Strategy & Operating Model:

• Define and implement Relias's enterprise data governance operating model, stewardship framework, governance councils, business ownership structure, and decision-making processes.
• Create accountability for business data across departments and establish governance standards that ensure consistency, transparency, and trust in enterprise reporting and regulated data-processing activities.
• Lead the Data Governance Council and steward network while partnering with business leaders to resolve data ownership and definition issues.
• Establish clear accountability for enterprise data assets and systems, including designated business owners, technical owners and Data Stewards, with defined escalation and certification requirements across downstream and third-party data flows.
• Create escalation mechanisms, supported by the CFO and applicable executive sponsors, for unresolved ownership gaps, overdue attestations, deficient data controls and non-participating system owners.
• Ensure that enterprise data governance standards align with privacy, records-management, information-security, AI-governance, contractual and regulatory requirements.

• Enterprise Metrics & Business Definition Governance:
• Establish and maintain enterprise-wide definitions for critical business metrics, including customer, learner, product usage, revenue, bookings, ARR, retention, churn, compliance, operational performance, and AI-related measures.
• Create the authoritative business glossary and semantic layer that standardizes reporting across Finance, Product, Customer Success, Revenue Operations, Marketing, and Executive Leadership
• Partner with Finance, Product, Revenue Operations, Customer Success, IT, and Technology leaders to eliminate conflicting definitions and create a consistent enterprise business glossary that serves as the authoritative source for reporting, forecasting, board reporting, and executive decision-making.
• Establish governed definitions for personal data, data-subject identities, authoritative identifiers, customer-controlled data, Relias-controlled data, derived data, de-identified data, suppression records, system of record, downstream system and other classifications required for privacy and DSAR workflows.
• Master Data Management & Information Stewardship:

• Develop and implement enterprise-wide master data management strategies across Customer, Account, Contact, Learner, User, Product, Content, Employee, and Organization hierarchies.
• Define data ownership, authoritative source systems, data stewardship responsibilities, matching and survivorship rules, and data lifecycle accountability that ensure consistency and accuracy across Salesforce Data360, Databricks, Tableau, operational applications, and future enterprise platforms.
• Partner with system owners to roll out programs.
• Define and govern the identity attributes, matching logic, source-system precedence and survivorship rules needed to locate and reconcile an individual across customer, learner, user, employee, CRM, marketing, support, product and analytics environments.
• Identify authoritative systems, replicated systems, downstream destinations, derived datasets and re-ingestion paths so that deletion, correction, suppression and access actions are not reversed or rendered incomplete by subsequent data synchronization.
• Establish lifecycle ownership for active, archived, backup, log, cache, index, unstructured, vendor-hosted and derived data locations.
• Data Quality & Trusted Data Program:

• Establish enterprise data quality standards, scorecards, monitoring frameworks, metadata management practices, data catalog capabilities, and lineage documentation.
• Develop KPIs that measure completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, and duplicate management.
• Partner with technology teams to identify root causes while maintaining business accountability for remediation.
• Establish data-governance controls and monitoring for completeness of system inventories, assignment of business and technical owners, lineage coverage, steward approvals, recurring attestations, retention classifications and unresolved data-location gaps.
• Define and monitor standards for system-owner attestations supporting privacy-rights execution, including identification of the applicable system, data location, action taken, date performed, responsible owner and supporting evidence reference.
• Partner with Information Security on technical evidence standards and control validation, and with Legal on approved retention, deletion, suppression and exception requirements.
• Produce residual-gap reporting identifying systems, datasets or vendors that are unsearched, unsupported, manually controlled, not yet integrated or otherwise unable to provide complete evidence.

• Privacy, DSAR & Data Lifecycle Governance

• Serve as the Data Governance Lead for Relias’s DSAR Data Governance Operating Plan and related technology implementation.
• Own and maintain the enterprise data inventory and data map required to identify where personal data is created, collected, stored, transformed, replicated, shared, archived and deleted across Relias-controlled systems, customer-controlled environments, vendors and subprocessors.
• Reconcile the initial privacy-platform baseline and subsequent discovery records into a validated enterprise inventory with named business owners, technical owners, Data Stewards, data classifications, data flows and applicable lifecycle requirements.
• Prioritize systems and datasets into risk-based implementation tiers based on privacy risk, identity significance, downstream propagation, legal role, business criticality, evidence gaps and implementation feasibility.
• Coordinate recurring steward review, platform change assessment, data-map certification and system-owner attestation processes so the inventory remains current after initial implementation.
• Partner with the Privacy Operations / DSAR Program Owner to identify in-scope systems and data locations for request workflows, while Privacy Operations retains accountability for case intake, classification, deadlines, assignments, requester communications, evidence completeness and closeout.
• Partner with Legal to translate approved retention, deletion, de-identification, suppression, legal-hold, accreditation, certification, contractual and controller/processor requirements into governed data classifications, lifecycle rules and operational metadata.
• Partner with Information Security, IT, Product, Engineering, Data & Analytics and system owners to define system-specific data locations, deletion or de-identification methods, downstream dependencies, manual execution requirements and evidence-return obligations.
• Support the proof of value, configuration, connector validation, acceptance testing, deployment and operational handoff of any approved DSAR or privacy-operations platform, including data-map stewardship, identity-resolution requirements, manual-task workflows, audit-evidence outputs and residual-gap reporting.
• Escalate incomplete inventories, absent system ownership, unsupported data locations, overdue attestations and recurring execution failures to the DSAR Program Owner and executive sponsor.
• Maintain clear separation between Data Governance responsibilities and the responsibilities of Privacy Operations, Legal, Information Security and system owners.

• Data Enablement & Organizational Adoption:

• Drive enterprise adoption of governance practices through Data Steward training, business glossary adoption, data literacy programs, governance communications, and process documentation.
• Create a culture where teams understand ownership and accountability for enterprise data assets.
• Train business owners, technical owners and Data Stewards on DSAR-related data-location, lifecycle, attestation, change-notification and evidence-return responsibilities.
• Develop reusable playbooks, ownership matrices, certification processes and escalation protocols that allow governance practices to scale across Relias’s enterprise platform environment.

COMPETENCIES

• Enterprise Data Governance Leadership: Demonstrated ability to build and mature enterprise governance functions, stewardship programs, governance councils, and operating models that create accountability and trust in organizational data assets.
• Master Data Management Expertise: Deep expertise designing and implementing master data strategies, ownership frameworks, business glossaries, stewardship models, and authoritative source governance across complex enterprise environments.
• Enterprise Metrics & KPI Governance: Experience establishing standardized business metrics, reporting frameworks, semantic models, executive dashboards, and enterprise-wide performance measurement methodologies.
• Data Quality & Information Management: Strong understanding of data quality management, metadata administration, lineage tracking, cataloging, governance tooling, and enterprise information management best practices.
• Analytics, AI & Modern Data Platforms: Working knowledge of modern data ecosystems, including cloud data platforms, Databricks, Salesforce Data360, Tableau, AI-driven analytics, and emerging metrics associated with enterprise AI adoption, together with the privacy, security, lineage and lifecycle controls required when enterprise data is used for analytics and AI.
• Executive Influence & Stakeholder Alignment: Exceptional ability to influence senior leaders, facilitate cross-functional decisions, resolve competing priorities, and drive enterprise-wide adoption of governance frameworks and standards.
• Organizational Change Leadership: Demonstrated success leading cultural and operational change initiatives that improve data accountability, consistency, transparency, and business outcomes.
• Privacy, DSAR & Data Lifecycle Governance: Working knowledge of privacy-rights operating models, DSAR data mapping, retention and deletion governance, durable suppression, data minimization, customer-controlled versus company-controlled data, vendor data flows and the governance requirements needed to support defensible request fulfillment.
• Enterprise Data Inventory & Lineage: Demonstrated ability to create and maintain enterprise inventories covering structured, unstructured, derived, replicated, archived, backup, log, cache, index and vendor-hosted data, with clear ownership, lineage, system classification and lifecycle accountability.
• Control, Attestation & Auditability: Experience establishing system-owner attestations, recurring certifications, evidence standards, control monitoring, issue escalation and audit-ready documentation across decentralized business and technology teams.
• Privacy Technology Implementation: Experience supporting implementation of data catalogs, data-discovery platforms, privacy-request automation, identity-resolution, workflow-management or similar governance technology, including requirements definition, acceptance testing, change management and operational handoff.

YOU’VE GOT WHAT IT TAKES IF YOU HAVE:

• 10 years of experience in Data Governance, Master Data Management, Enterprise Information Management, Data Strategy, Analytics, or related disciplines
• Minimum of 5 years leading enterprise-scale governance or information management initiatives
• Proven experience establishing data governance frameworks, stewardship models, governance councils, and enterprise business glossaries.
• Demonstrated ability to align business and technology stakeholders around common metrics, definitions, and data standards.
• Experience supporting executive reporting, analytics, forecasting, operational management, and enterprise performance measurement
• Experience creating or governing enterprise data inventories, data maps, lineage documentation, system-owner matrices and recurring stewardship or certification processes.
• Experience supporting privacy, DSAR, records-management, regulatory-compliance or other data-lifecycle programs involving multiple business systems, vendors and data domains.
• Demonstrated experience defining ownership and governance for personal data, identity matching, authoritative and downstream systems, retention, deletion, suppression, archives and derived datasets.
• Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Business Administration, Data Management, Computer Science, Finance, Analytics, or a related field

IT WOULD BE IDEAL IF YOU HAVE:

• MBA or advanced degree in Business Administration, Information Management, Analytics, Data Science, or related discipline
• Experience with Databricks, Salesforce Data360, Tableau, enterprise data catalogs, metadata platforms, and modern MDM solutions.
• Experience supporting AI governance, data ethics, privacy programs, and enterprise analytics initiatives, including privacy-rights or DSAR operating models.
• Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP), DCAM, or similar governance certification preferred.
• Experience within SaaS, healthcare technology, education technology, or other regulated industries preferred.
• Experience implementing or operating enterprise data catalogs, automated data discovery, privacy-request management, consent/preference management or DSAR workflow platforms.
• Experience with retention schedules, deletion and de-identification controls, durable suppression, legal holds, customer-controlled data and vendor/subprocessor data flows.
• Experience preparing data-governance controls and evidence for internal audit, external audit, regulatory review or customer diligence.

IN OFFICE REQUIREMENT:

Relias values collaboration and wants to ensure that our team members have opportunities to work with their teams regularly for professional development opportunities. Our flexible hybrid work environment requires that you live in the state of North Carolina, within a commutable distance to our office (~1-hour commute). You would be expected to work in our Morrisville, NC Headquarters (close to the Raleigh/Durham airport) approximately 40 days/quarter.

Relias welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities and is happy to make reasonable accommodations in all aspects of the selection process.  If you are an individual with a disability and require reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the job application process, please visit our career page for instructions.

The Complex Loss Specialist position at Golden State Claims Services reports to a Claims Supervisor or Claims Manager and will specialize in Allied Health claims. The chief duty of the Complex Loss Specialist for Allied Health claims is to adjust the most time-intensive, complex, and high exposure losses that require a higher level of technical expertise, knowledge, and negotiating ability, for the program(s) to which is assigned. The Complex Loss Specialist will have a high level of ability to provide analysis and presentations to Senior Executives and Program Executives for these complex matters and will be well-versed in leading strategic roundtable discussions to determine optimal resolution strategy.

Position Responsibilities

• Contribute to a collaborative environment by consistently demonstrating teamwork, high motivation, positive behavior, and effort to achieve goals and objectives.

• Research applicable coverage for our insureds. Document coverage dates, limits, and restrictions

• Identify and resolve any potential coverage questions. Draft reservation of rights and coverage denials for review and approval by their Supervisor/Manager

• Investigate facts of the loss by securing statements and supporting documentation such as contracts, cost of repair estimates, expert reports, photos, correspondence, etc.

• Document activities in writing within claim files

• Exercise judgment in applying legal liability to assigned claims and will have settlement authority up to their specific authority, which may vary from carrier to carrier.

• Assign defense counsel to answer and defend lawsuits where appropriate. Monitor and direct defense counsel, independent adjusters, and experts.

• Identify claims with potential exposure in excess of authority and advise their Supervisor/Manager

• Evaluate, set, or recommend reserves for each file they are handling.

• Prepare written reports as dictated by company policy and procedures.

• Handle claims within guidelines of the Fair Claims Practices 790.03

• Provide insureds, claimants, underwriters, and carriers with regular updates on status of file handling.

• Discuss unique and complex files with Supervisor/Manager

Core Technical Duties

• Healthcare liability claims investigation and evaluation, including medical malpractice, general liability, and professional liability exposures

• Coverage analysis and interpretation of allied health professional liability policies, including review of coverage dates, limits, exclusions, and endorsements

• Medical record review and interpretation across allied health disciplines (physical therapy, home health, diagnostics, behavioral health, etc.)

• Drafting reservation of rights letters and coverage denial communications for supervisor review

• Reserve evaluation, setting, and recommendation based on exposure analysis and claim trajectory

• Litigation management, including assignment and direction of defense counsel, independent medical examiners, and expert witnesses

Investigation & Documentation

• Securing recorded and written statements from insureds, claimants, and witnesses

• Gathering and organizing supporting documentation including incident reports, medical records, licensing records, contracts, and expert reports

• Maintaining accurate, detailed claim file documentation in compliance with carrier and program guidelines

• Preparing written reports and roundtable summaries consistent with company policies and procedures

Minimum Qualifications

• Minimum of 10 years of claims experience, with an emphasis on complex Allied Health claims

• College degree or equivalent claims management experience required.

• Active adjusters license under your name required

Under the direction of the Project Manager plans, organizes, directs, trains and supervises the staff of wastewater treatment plant operators, residual technicians, and supervisors, in the safe and cost effective operation of the 67 MGD Springfield Regional Wastewater Treatment Facility, wastewater and flood pump stations, combined sewer interceptor lines and CSO regulator stations. Ensures operation of the treatment facilities and performance of staff is accomplished in a safe and cost-effective manner, ensures completion of scheduled preventive and predictive maintenance tasks assigned to the operations group, plans and coordinates major equipment outages, works closely with the maintenance manager to establish maintenance priorities and develop programs for equipment replacement and facility improvements. Responsible for maintaining operational areas in a professional and well-kept appearance.

• Develops and monitors systematic, ongoing review of key performance indicators.
• Prepares weekly and monthly operations reports
• Directs the operations of biosolids storage, dewatering and drying processes, sets production schedules and coordinates a diversified sludge management program for delivery of residual solids products to multiple disposal options.
• Directs performance of facility operations staff and audits and controls expenditures of the operational cost centers; monitors quality of work to ensure adherence to Company and industry standards and compliance with state, and federal laws, regulations, and guidelines.

jobs.description:
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

Build and lead the go-to-market strategy for a new ultra-high-end performance tire channel in the U.S. replacement market. This role acts as the commercial entrepreneur for the channel, developing the business from the ground up, personally managing strategic accounts, and delivering profitable sales growth across approved sellout paths. The position owns revenue and unit-volume performance, helps establish the annual operating budget and commercial targets, and leads execution through influence across U.S. and global functions.

• Develop and execute the end-to-end U.S. go-to-market plan for the ultra-high-end replacement channel, including market segmentation, customer prioritization, route-to-market design, launch sequencing and multiyear growth plans.

• Personally identify, prospect, open, negotiate, develop and manage strategic key accounts. Pursue any sellout path aligned with the approved strategy, including exotic and ultra-luxury vehicle dealerships, elite independent installers, specialty distributors, performance shops, e-commerce partners, driving experiences, clubs and track-related partners.

• Own annual and long-range revenue and unit-volume plans. Build forecasts, sales pipelines, account plans and corrective actions; monitor sell-in, sellout, market share, conversion and repeat purchase performance.

• Develop pricing, trade terms and customer programs in partnership with Finance and Sales leadership. Protect premium brand positioning while driving sustainable growth and targeted margin performance.

• Create a disciplined channel-priority strategy that initially emphasizes high-touch, technically credible accounts and controlled fulfillment before broader distribution expansion.

• Translate customer, installer and market insights into product, fitment, inventory, service, training and lifecycle recommendations. Maintain technical credibility regarding staggered fitments, load and speed requirements, performance attributes and target vehicle applications.

• Develop sales tools, account education, installer standards, service-adviser training and premium customer-experience requirements that support safe, accurate and consistent product representation.

• Build strategic partnerships and event activations that generate measurable trial, qualified leads, account introductions and sales conversion, rather than awareness alone.

• Coordinate with global teams to share U.S. market requirements, leverage global capabilities and ensure alignment with product development, certification, manufacturing and brand strategy.

• Establish channel KPIs and provide clear business reviews to senior leadership, including opportunities, risks, competitive activity, inventory needs, forecast accuracy and recovery plans.

• Represent the company at customer meetings, industry events, enthusiast gatherings, driving programs and track-focused activities; travel frequently within the United States.

• 5+ years of related industry experience
• Demonstrated experience launching a new product, channel or business from the ground up
• Significant experience in the U.S. replacement tire market

jobs.title: Data Architect
jobs.description:
About Cook Systems

For over 30 years, Cook Systems has partnered with organizations across the country to solve technology challenges and build strong technology teams. As a veteran-owned IT consulting company, we combine decades of industry experience with a continued focus on how technology, AI, and the way people work are evolving.

Our work spans technology consulting, talent development, and AI-enabled solutions. We value people who take ownership, adapt quickly, communicate well, and care about the quality of their work. Whether you’re early in your career or bringing years of experience, you’ll have the opportunity to keep building your skills, contribute to meaningful client work, and grow with a company that continues to evolve with the industry.

Summary:
The Data Architect will join our Technology Architecture team in a high-impact, hands-on role responsible for defining enterprise data architecture strategy, establishing technology standards, and enabling modern data, analytics, business intelligence, and AI capabilities. This role will partner with business stakeholders, data engineering teams, technology leaders, and other technical teams to develop scalable data solutions and drive the evolution of enterprise data platforms.

Responsibilities:

• Develop and deliver long-term strategic goals for enterprise-wide data architecture, technology standards, and best practices.

• Architect and design structured and unstructured data platforms supporting large-scale analytics and data processing.

• Research database, data warehouse, and data store technologies and develop implementation strategies to support modern workloads.

• Define strategies and standards for enterprise Business Intelligence (BI), reporting, analytics, and self-service BI.

• Design strategies and standards for batch, micro-batch, and real-time data pipelines.

• Evaluate BI technologies and develop implementation strategies for agile reporting and self-service analytics.

• Create and maintain conceptual, logical, and physical data models and associated metadata.

• Establish and maintain standards, guidelines, and best practices for data modeling and database design.

• Collaborate with business stakeholders and data warehouse teams to define enterprise data warehousing, BI, analytics, and reporting strategies.

• Identify gaps and opportunities within the data and analytics environment and recommend improvements to maximize business value.

• Promote data governance, centralized metrics, common definitions, and trusted enterprise data.

• Work with technology teams to ensure solutions align with enterprise data architecture standards and participate in data analysis and solution design activities.

• Provide technical mentoring, training, and knowledge transfer to technology teams and business users.

• Research emerging data technologies and evaluate their applicability to enterprise business requirements.

Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, a related analytical field, or equivalent experience.

• 8+ years of experience leading the design and development of enterprise-class applications and solutions.

• 8+ years of experience with relational database management systems such as SQL Server, Oracle, DB2, or equivalent technologies.

• 5+ years of hands-on experience in a large enterprise data warehouse environment.

• 4+ years of experience as a Data Architect in a large enterprise data warehouse environment.

• 4+ years of hands-on experience with relational and dimensional data modeling in a large enterprise environment.

• 4+ years of experience implementing solutions using an enterprise data warehouse platform such as Teradata, Snowflake, or equivalent technology.

• 4+ years of experience with two or more BI tools such as Tableau, Power BI, QlikView, or equivalent technologies.

• 2+ years of experience with big data technologies such as Apache Spark, Databricks, Hadoop, or equivalent technologies.

• 2+ years of experience implementing data solutions in a public cloud environment such as Azure, AWS, or GCP.

• Demonstrated experience eliciting requirements from business stakeholders and partnering with technical teams to develop comprehensive solutions.

• Strong technical knowledge of BI best practices, including data visualization, dashboards, business metrics, KPIs, reporting, queries, search, predictive analytics, and master data management.

Benefits at Cook Systems

We want our employees to have benefits that support their health, financial well-being, and life outside of work. Eligible Cook Systems employees have access to a comprehensive benefits package beginning the first of the month following their hire date, including:

• Medical coverage through Blue Cross Blue Shield, with two plan options

• Dental and vision coverage

• Life, critical illness, and accident insurance through Unum

• Flexible Spending Account and Dependent Care FSA options through Navia

• Health Gap Insurance through Sun Life

• 401(k) retirement plan through The Standard, with eligibility after six months

Beyond benefits, Cook Systems is a place where we expect people to take ownership of their work, communicate openly, continue learning, and contribute to the teams and clients they support.

We have been building technology careers and client partnerships for more than three decades, and we continue to evolve with the industry. If you’re looking for an opportunity to do meaningful work, develop your capabilities, and be part of what comes next in technology, we’d like to hear from you.

Accurately measures intake and output on the I & O sheets and relays information to Charge Nurse at shift change. Performs procedures and treatments as instructed by Charge Nurse (i.e.:  Sitz bath, moist packs, isolation techniques, etc.). Maintains appropriate supplies and equipment on the unit and alerts Charge Nurse or purchasing clerk of additional needs.  Ensures that charge items are entered according to departmental procedure. Successfully completes job duties as CNA by attending continuing education classes and in-services, accepting reassignments to other areas, taking on increased responsibilities, and keeping Charge Nurse informed of pertinent information that may require follow-up. Interacts and maintains effective working relationships with other team members, charge nurse, and department managers. Maintains discretion in handling confidential information. Gives report to Charge Nurse at the end of each shift and completes walking rounds with the oncoming or leaving shift. May be assigned other duties as appropriate.

Qualifications

• High school diploma preferred

• Active Certified Nurse Assistant certification in the state you will be working

• CPR certification, or willing to obtain within six months of employment

• Long-term care experience preferred

• Excellent communication skills to interact verbally with patients, visitors, and staff

• Ability to manage time and organize daily schedule to meet productivity standards

• Ability to stand and walk for long periods of time

• Ability to lift heavy object using proper lifting techniques and with assistance when necessary

• Ability to transfer and move patients who vary with ability to assist weighing 200+lbs using proper lifting techniques and with assistance when necessary

• Ability to push and pull equipment weighing in excess of 40lbs using proper techniques and with assistance when necessary

• Manual dexterity, coordination and skillful use of hands when working with patients and equipment

• Ability to physically perform necessary documentation in writing or use of tape recorder

• Visual acuity with the ability to distinguish color

Pay Range: $16.08 - $25.24 per hour

Category: CNA

jobs.title: Performance Creative Strategist, New Ventures
jobs.description:
About us

Pomelo Care is the leading virtual medical practice for women and children, providing care across pregnancy, postpartum, pediatrics, menopause, and perimenopause. We combine proactive, 24/7 clinical care with technology that helps us reach patients earlier, identify risks sooner, and deliver personalized care throughout their journey. Our team includes clinicians, technologists, operators, and problem-solvers working together to make high-quality care more accessible for families nationwide.

About The Role:

Your north star: Build a high-velocity, data-backed creative engine that drives prospective patients to start their care journey with Pomelo.

As our Performance Creative Strategist, you will own the full creative lifecycle from deep patient insight and trend research to concepting, content creation, and post-campaign performance analyses. This is a high-ownership, strategy-and-ops-driven role: you will be the mastermind architecting our creative pipeline, diversifying our creative formats, and scaling winning concepts across paid channels.

This role reports to the Head of Growth, New Ventures and is open to any candidates located in the continental US.

What you'll do:

• Deeply understand our patients: Mine qualitative and quantitative data (reviews, surveys, community forums) to develop a deep understanding of who our patients are and what they care about. Translate key insights into high-converting messaging and creative angles.

• Fuel new concept generation: Spot emerging creative formats, viral hooks, and ad trends across Meta, TikTok, YouTube, and CTV. Continuously generate fresh, net-new concepts rather than just minor iterations.

• Own creative operations: Build and manage a streamlined project management system for creative assets. Proactively drive production timelines, manage external creative partners and agencies (holding them to high standards), and eliminate bottlenecks to ensure a smooth, end-to-end creative workflow.

• Accelerate output & testing Cycles: Build a rapid-fire production flywheel that moves assets from concept to live testing fast.

• Analyze performance & iterate: Work closely with the Growth team to review paid channel performance weekly. Turn performance data into actionable retros, double down on winning frameworks, and rapidly sunset underperforming assets.

Who you are:

• Experienced strategist: 3–5 years of experience in performance creative strategy, growth marketing, or creative strategy at a DTC brand, healthtech company, or high-growth agency.

• Master project manager: Highly organized and proactive with a track record of building efficient creative production workflows and managing external partners/agencies without hand-holding.

• Data & insight driven: Excellent understanding of performance metrics (Hook Rate, Hold Rate, CTR, CAC, LTV) and an ability to translate deep understanding of our patients to compelling ad messaging.

• Trend & benchmarking expert: Always tracking what is working across paid social, saving examples, pattern-matching successful ad structures, and adapting them to our brand.

• Action biased: Focused on speed to market and shipping volume at high quality. (Note: You do not need to be on camera, but you should know how to brief, direct, and assemble a winning video asset).

• Cross-functional communicator: Skilled at bridging the gap between brand identity, clinical nuance, and direct-response performance needs.

Bonus points if you have any of the following:

• Experience in healthcare, women's health, or high-trust/regulated DTC products

• Light hands-on video editing or static design skills (e.g., CapCut, Premiere, Figma, Canva) for rapid prototyping and mockups

• Experience managing external creator/influencer networks or agency workflows at scale

Why you should join our team

By joining Pomelo, you will get in on the ground floor of a fast-moving, well-funded, and mission-driven startup that always puts the patient first. You will learn, grow and be challenged, and have fun with your team while doing it.

We strive to create an environment where employees from all backgrounds are respected. We value working across disciplines, moving fast, data-driven decision making, learning, and always putting the patient first.

Benefits and Perks:

• Comprehensive Health, Dental, and Vision coverage for employees and their families

• High deductible Health Plans with Health Savings Account (HSA) options

• Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

• Equity grant participation

• 401(k) program

• Competitive vacation policy

• 16 weeks paid parental leave

• Fully remote work flexibility (within the US)

Compensation:

The expected base salary range offered for this role is $110,000-$130,000. This role is also eligible for equity, giving you an ownership stake in Pomelo’s mission. Actual compensation may vary based on relevant experience, skills, competencies, and certifications.

At Pomelo, we are committed to hiring the best team to improve outcomes for all mothers and babies, regardless of their background. We need diverse perspectives to reflect the diversity of problems we face and the population we serve. We look to hire people from a variety of backgrounds, including but not limited to race, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, national origin, religion, disability, and veteran status.

Potential Fraud Warning

Please be cautious of potential recruitment fraud. With the increase of remote work and digital hiring, phishing and job scams are on the rise with malicious actors impersonating real employees and sending fake job offers in an effort to collect personal or financial information.

Pomelo Care will never ask you to pay a fee or download software as part of the interview process with our company. Pomelo Care will also never ask for your personal banking or other financial information until after you have signed an offer of employment and completed onboarding paperwork that is provided by our People Operations team. All official communication with Pomelo Care People Operations team will come from domain email addresses ending in @pomelocare.com.

If you receive a message that seems suspicious, we encourage you to pause communication and contact us directly at careers@pomelocare.com to confirm its legitimacy. For your safety, we also recommend applying only through our official Careers page. If you believe you have been the victim of a scam or identity theft, please contact your local law enforcement agency or another trusted authority for guidance.

jobs.description:
JOB SUMMARY
The Learning and Development Specialist (Learning Content and OJT) is responsible for designing, implementing, and evaluating learning programs and initiatives to foster employee development and enhance organizational performance that are specific to the position. This position partners closely with production leaders and department managers to ensure employees receive the training, resources, and support needed to perform successfully and safely in their roles.
The position will not only develop training content but will also be analytical, detail-oriented, and eager to learn new skills. This position monitors program effectiveness through both qualitative and quantitative measures, including training records, competency attainment, KPI alignment, employee interactions, and feedback from department managers throughout the organization.
The ideal candidate is a self-starter who enjoys working with people, is highly organized and detail-oriented, and is comfortable balancing multiple priorities in a dynamic manufacturing environment. Success in this role requires strong communication skills, a proactive approach to problem-solving, and the ability to work effectively with employees at all levels of the organization.
 
COMPANY OVERVIEW
Component Repair Technologies, Inc. (CRT) began as a locally family-owned business, with operations in Mentor, OH since 1985, and grew into a global leader (500+ employees) in the aerospace MRO sector.  Specializing in the repair and overhaul of turbine engine components, CRT proudly serves the world’s largest airlines and jet engine manufacturers. Component Repair Technologies is focused on our valued employees, customers, and community. 
In 2025, CRT became a Safran Aircraft Engines company as a Center of Excellence for the repair of large jet engine parts in the Americas.
For over 120 years, Safran, through its Aircraft Engines subsidiary, designs, produces, markets and supports, alone or in partnership, aircraft engines offering world-class performance and reliability. Its core purpose is to contribute to a safer, more sustainable world, where air transport is more environmentally friendly, comfortable and accessible.
Operating through CFM International, its 50/50 joint venture with GE Aerospace, Safran Aircraft Engines is the world’s leading supplier of single-aisle commercial jet engines, the CFM56 and LEAP. Safran Aircraft Engines is fully committed to sustainable aviation through the RISE (Revolutionary Innovation for Sustainable Engines) technology development program. Safran Aircraft Engines also deploys a global network providing a full range of support, maintenance & repair services. 
Visit www.componentrepair.com and www.safran-group.com for more information. Take-off in your career, learn new skills and become part of a world-class workforce.
 
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Follow established safety protocols and guidelines to ensure full compliance with company safety policies and procedures.
Design and deliver training programs (onboarding, on-the-job, leadership development, and technical skills) based on organizational objectives.
Design, develop, and deliver training programs that support employee development, operational effectiveness, regulatory compliance, and organizational objectives, including onboarding, on-the-job training (OJT), leadership development, technical skills, and professional development initiatives.
Create, update, and maintain training materials, job aids, educational resources, presentations, and course content for instructor-led, hands-on, and computer-based learning environments.
Partner with department managers and supervisors to identify training needs and develop structured training plans that support departmental goals and are aligned with the specific department and position.
Conduct training needs assessments and skills gap analyses to identify opportunities for workforce development and performance improvement.
Evaluate the effectiveness of training programs through feedback, surveys, and other assessment tools and make recommendations for curriculum improvement.
Maintain training records and ensure compliance with company, customer, regulatory, and audit requirements, including FAA Part 145 and other applicable industry standards.
Monitor industry trends and best practices in learning and development to enhance organizational learning initiatives.
Support employee development, career progression, and succession planning initiatives by providing guidance, resources, and visibility to internal development opportunities.
Administer and maintain the Learning Management System (LMS), ensuring accurate tracking of training compliance, employee development, and training-related data.
 
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree in Education, Learning and Development, Human Resources, Organizational Management, or a related field; or a minimum of two years of experience in a related role within a manufacturing or production environment.
Two to three years of experience in designing, implementing, and evaluating training and professional development programs for young adults and adult learners or relevant experience in a training or educational environment.
Demonstrated experience administering and maintaining a Learning Management System (LMS).
Demonstrated strength and experience in project management skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines effectively and efficiently.
 
OTHER QUALIFICATIONS
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate with many different stakeholders. 
Previous experience as a mentor, coach, instructor, or trainer.
Excellent problem-solving abilities.
Ability to read, write, speak, understand English, and be able to effectively communicate with other employees.
Proficiency with software programs commonly used in training and development, including Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Learning Management Systems (LMS), and content authoring tools such as Articulate or similar platforms.
Experience in technical writing and editing documents that support employee training and production operations.

May be required to occasionally lift or move up to 10 pounds.

CRT currently offers two excellent health care options, one being a fully funded program (no premiums for employee and family) and the other being a traditional employee premium contribution.  Programs include health, vision, and dental coverages. Growth Platform builds the machine learning systems that help businesses discover and use the Stripe products that meet their needs. Our recommendations reach users across the Dashboard, email, onboarding, documentation, and AI agent interfaces. We combine an understanding of each business with models that decide which recommendation is useful, when to show it, and how to learn from the outcome.

Our work spans recommendation and ranking models, contextual bandits, agent-based recommendations, and the data and evaluation systems behind them. We build shared capabilities that product, marketing, and sales teams can use across Stripe. Success means helping businesses take useful actions and adopt products that help them grow, while keeping recommendations relevant and avoiding unnecessary messages.

What you’ll do

You will build and operate production ML systems that improve how Stripe recommends products, content, and next steps to businesses. You will own work from problem definition and feature development through training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and iteration. Working with data scientists, engineers, and product partners, you will turn model improvements into measurable user and business outcomes.

Responsibilities

• Design, train, evaluate, deploy, and maintain models for recommendation, ranking, and personalized action selection across Growth Platform surfaces.

• Improve contextual bandit and policy-learning approaches, including exploration, reward design, and how recommendations adapt to user context and feedback.

• Build agent-based recommendation capabilities that use business context to identify relevant products and integration options, with evaluations that test recommendation quality and usefulness.

• Develop reliable data and feature pipelines for training and inference. Improve data freshness, feature quality, and consistency between training and production.

• Build reusable tooling for model evaluation, retraining, and safe rollout so the team can test and ship improvements faster.

• Own the quality and operation of the team's ML components: write tested production code, monitor models and pipelines, investigate failures, and improve reliability, latency, and cost.

• Design and analyze online experiments with data science partners. Connect offline evaluation to product adoption and incremental impact, with guardrails for dismissals, unsubscribes, and user experience.

• Partner with product engineering to integrate models into recommendation delivery systems, and with ML infrastructure teams to use and improve Stripe's shared training, feature, and serving capabilities.

• Work with product, marketing, and sales partners to identify problems that shared ML capabilities can solve, and make practical choices about where modeling adds value.

Who you are

You are a machine learning engineer with a builder mindset. You care about the business problem, the quality of the model, and what happens after it ships. You can move between modeling and software engineering, make practical tradeoffs, and take ownership of an ambiguous problem through production and measurement.

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• 3+ years of industry experience in machine learning engineering, software engineering, or applied data science, with hands-on experience building and shipping ML models in production.

• Strong programming skills in Python and experience writing maintainable, tested production code.

• Practical experience designing, training, and evaluating ML models using frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost, or scikit-learn.

• Experience building data or feature pipelines, proficiency in SQL, and familiarity with distributed data processing tools such as Spark or PySpark.

• A strong understanding of statistics, model evaluation, and experimentation, including the ability to recognize data leakage and distinguish offline model improvements from business impact.

• Experience deploying, monitoring, and debugging production ML systems, and evaluating tradeoffs among model quality, reliability, latency, and cost.

• Ability to turn an open-ended business problem into a technical approach and collaborate effectively with engineering, data science, product, and business partners.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience with recommendation systems, ranking, personalization, or marketplace and advertising optimization.

• Experience with contextual bandits, policy learning, causal inference, or off-policy evaluation.

• Experience building and evaluating LLM applications, including structured extraction, embeddings, or recommendations grounded in user and business context.

• Experience building reusable ML capabilities used by multiple products or teams, including training automation, feature systems, or model monitoring.

• Experience with product growth, lifecycle messaging, or systems that balance short-term engagement with longer-term user outcomes.
