jobs.description:
Senior Manager, IT Infrastructure, Trexon, An Amphenol Company

FLSA Status: Salary, Exempt

Reports To: Trexon General Manager; dotted line to Trexon Controller

Direct Reports: Yes

Location: Hybrid, with on-site presence at a Trexon core facility (Boston, MA; Santa Clarita, CA; Chandler, AZ; Longmont, CO; or Cleveland/Akron, OH)

Travel: 25%

Summary

Trexon is a manufacturer of specialty cable, wire harness and interconnect solutions serving leading customers in the space, defense, medical, industrial and other specialty end markets. The business is made up of seven business units across the United States, with revenue in excess of $200 million and ~ 900 employees. Trexon is part of Amphenol Corporation (NYSE: APH), a global leader in interconnect and sensor solutions.

The Senior Manager, IT Infrastructure leads the infrastructure function for Trexon and is the technology leader for all non-application infrastructure across the business. The role owns the network, cloud and server environment, identity, end-user computing, backup and recovery, and IT service delivery at every site. ERP and application development are supported by separate teams.

The Senior Manager leads the corporate infrastructure team and works alongside IT resources based at the business units. The role is accountable for delivering through that team: running a clear intake and prioritization process, maintaining a realistic project roadmap, assigning and sequencing work, and holding the team to committed dates. Technical depth is expected, but the primary measure of the role is the reliability of the environment and the predictability of delivery across sites, not necessarily individual hands-on output.

Security operations are delivered through managed providers, including endpoint detection and response and a managed SOC and SIEM service. The Senior Manager owns those relationships and the escalation, vulnerability and remediation processes that sit behind them. The role also co-leads the CMMC Level 2 implementation alongside the IT Technical Lead, who has been driving the program to date, and an external implementation partner, against tight timelines.

Integration with Amphenol raises the standard for IT internal controls. The Senior Manager is responsible for strengthening controls and procedures across the Trexon IT organization and for installing the recurring routines that keep them running, documented and evidenced. The role interfaces periodically with Amphenol IT leadership on standards, reporting and reviews.

Effective communication is integral to the role. The Senior Manager must translate technical risk, cost and options into terms site and corporate leadership can act on, and set expectations the team can meet. The ideal candidate combines credible technical depth across network, cloud and infrastructure with the project management discipline and presence to operate as a leader.

Key Responsibilities

• Own the design, operation and reliability of Trexon’s infrastructure environment across all sites, including network and connectivity, servers and virtualization, cloud, storage, backup and end-user computing.

• Lead, develop and hold accountable the corporate infrastructure team. Set priorities, assign and sequence work, manage coverage across locations, and build technical bench strength.

• Partner with site-based IT resources and business unit leadership to set common standards, coordinate support coverage and deliver projects at the sites.

• Own project intake, prioritization and delivery for infrastructure. Maintain the project portfolio and roadmap, scope and estimate work, set achievable timelines, delegate execution and report status, risks and trade-offs to leadership.

• Own IT service delivery and support for the sites, including incident and request management, escalation paths, service levels, and measurable response and resolution performance.

• Own business continuity and disaster recovery for infrastructure, including backup and replication design, recovery objectives, documented recovery procedures and periodic restore testing.

• Co-lead the CMMC Level 2 implementation with the IT Technical Lead and an external implementation partner, covering system boundary and enclave design, access control, logging and evidence retention, and meeting committed timelines.

• Strengthen IT controls and procedures across the Trexon organization to meet Amphenol standards, and install the recurring routines that sustain them, including access and privileged account reviews, change management and software compliance. Support internal and external audit requirements with documented evidence and timely remediation.

• Manage outsourced security services, including endpoint detection and response and the managed SOC and SIEM relationship. Own alert escalation, vulnerability and patch management, and timely remediation at the sites.

• Own identity and access management, including the joiner, mover and leaver process, privileged access, multi-factor authentication and periodic access reviews.

• Standardize the infrastructure estate across sites and reduce one-off configurations and technical debt.

• Own vendor and contract management for infrastructure, telecom and managed services, including selection, performance management, renewals and support for commercial negotiations.

• Own the infrastructure budget, both capital and operating, including forecasting, asset lifecycle planning and cost transparency, and partner with Finance on spend approvals and reporting.

• Partner with the ERP and application development teams to ensure infrastructure supports application requirements, including environment availability, performance and coordinated change management.

• Maintain accurate documentation of the environment, including network diagrams, asset and configuration inventory, runbooks and standard operating procedures.

• Perform other job-related duties as requested by management.

Key Competencies

• Delivers through the team. Plans, delegates and follows up rather than absorbing the work personally.

• Strong project management discipline, including scoping, sequencing, realistic commitments and visible status reporting.

• Technically credible across network, cloud, virtualization and end-user computing, with the judgment to challenge vendors and engineers on design decisions.

• Practical approach to risk and cost, selecting fit-for-purpose solutions appropriate to the size and pace of the business.

• Comfortable operating across multiple sites and time zones, with regular on-site presence and travel.

• Able to set direction and drive standards across sites, including with resources outside the direct reporting line.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical issues and options to non-technical leadership.

• Ability to handle confidential company and personnel information appropriately.

• Ability to work under pressure and adhere to deadlines, including responsiveness to production-impacting issues outside standard hours.

• Forward-thinking in applying tools and automation that improve reliability, visibility and efficiency.

• Good organizational skills and the capacity to handle a high work volume.

• Self-motivated and positive team player who builds working relationships with site leadership.

• Ability to work flexible hours as needed.

Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree in information systems, computer science, engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience, is required.

Experience: Minimum eight (8) to ten (10) years of progressive IT infrastructure experience, including a minimum of three (3) years leading and developing technical teams. Demonstrated experience managing a portfolio of concurrent IT projects across multiple sites, including scoping, resourcing and delivery against committed dates, is required. Multi-site manufacturing or industrial environment experience preferred. Experience supporting aerospace, defense or space end market customers, and public company experience, are a plus.

Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of enterprise networking (LAN, WAN, SD-WAN, firewalls and wireless), Microsoft 365 and Azure, identity management, virtualization, backup and disaster recovery, and endpoint management. Working knowledge of NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC requirements; experience supporting a CMMC Level 2 implementation preferred. Experience managing outsourced security services and vendor relationships required. Familiarity with ITIL or similar service management practices preferred. Experience supporting ERP environments preferred; Epicor experience a plus. Relevant certifications are a plus. Training will be provided on internal Trexon and Amphenol processes and systems, as required for this position.

Compensation and Benefits

Trexon offers a competitive compensation package including base salary and variable pay components. Actual compensation will be determined based on qualifications, relevant experience, and internal equity.

The Company also offers a comprehensive benefits program, including medical, dental and vision coverage, paid time off, and a 401(k) plan with company match.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, sit, and talk or hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to fifty (50) pounds. The employee must occasionally crouch, stoop, reach, or work in confined spaces such as server rooms and wiring closets. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. The role requires periodic presence on the manufacturing floor and travel between sites. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Supervisor, Care Team provides day-to-day leadership and oversight of front-line Pharmacy Technicians and Leads, ensuring the delivery of high-quality support to our members, pharmacies, and providers — whether they reach us by phone, chat, or email. This role is critical to maintaining service level performance, coaching team members, monitoring attendance and resolving escalated issues in real time. You will work closely with the Managers, Sr. Managers and cross-functional teams to uphold operational standards and foster a collaborative team culture.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

• Provide day-to-day supervision and support for Pharmacy Technicians and Leads as their direct supervisor, including managing timecards, monitoring schedules, tracking attendance, and overseeing individual performance.

• Partner with the Workforce Management team to adjust staffing and queue assignments for your channel, maintaining service level performance and optimizing team productivity.

• Help implement and refine Care Team workflows to meet department standards, client expectations, and service guarantees.

• Foster a positive team culture by conducting regular structured feedback conversations, coaching team members, reinforcing development goals, and promoting collaboration.

• Monitor individual and team performance metrics, identifying trends and supporting action plans to improve outcomes.

• Participate in quality monitoring initiatives and NPS survey programs that promote first-contact resolution and reduce repeat member outreach.

• Assist with onboarding new clients by preparing frontline teams and coordinating across internal stakeholders to ensure readiness.

• Proactively monitor call or chat activity to identify emerging issues, escalating or supporting resolution as needed, including member escalations.

• Help maintain knowledge base materials, standard operating procedures, and training documentation shared across channels.

• Demonstrate a working understanding of PBM workflows, including pharmacy claims processing and industry terminology.

• Participate in special projects as determined by management, utilizing your expertise and skills to drive business outcomes.

• Support cross-training efforts, helping your team build skills across both phone and chat.

• Uphold compliance with regulatory and privacy requirements, including HIPAA, across all member interactions.

WHO YOU ARE:

• Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent work experience.

• Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician (preferred); state licensure or registration required where applicable by law.

• 3+ years of experience in a healthcare contact center, retail pharmacy, PBM, or pharmacy operations setting, with a strong understanding of pharmacy-related customer service.

• Experience as a people leader, having previously led teams of pharmacy technicians (preferred).

• Proven ability to coach, motivate, and support frontline team members in a high-volume, service-driven environment.

• Comfortable balancing team performance metrics with individual development and engagement.

• Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to think quickly and resolve member or provider issues in real time.

• Skilled at using data to identify trends, support team improvements, and drive operational efficiency.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with confidence handling escalations and communicating across teams.

• Detail-oriented, highly organized, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced setting.

• Familiarity with pharmacy claims, PBM systems, and HIPAA/privacy requirements preferred.

COMPENSATION:  $65,000 - $70,000 annually, in addition to bonus and equity

Compensation offered will be determined by geographic location, experience, and qualifications.

CYBERSECURITY AWARENESS NOTICE

In response to ongoing and industry-wide fraudulent recruitment activities (i.e., job scams), Rightway wants to inform potential candidates that we will only contact them from the @rightwayhealthcare.com email domain. We will never ask for bank details or deposits of any kind as a condition of employment.

ABOUT RIGHTWAY:

Rightway is on a mission to harmonize healthcare for everyone, everywhere. Our products guide patients to the best care and medications by inserting clinicians and pharmacists into a patient’s care journey through a modern, mobile app. Rightway is a front door to healthcare, giving patients the tools they need along with on-demand access to Rightway health guides, human experts that answer their questions and manage the frustrating parts of healthcare for them.

Since its founding in 2017, Rightway has raised over $200mm from investors including Khosla Ventures, Thrive Capital, and Tiger Global. We’re headquartered in New York City, with satellite offices in Denver and Dallas. Our clients rely on us to transform the healthcare experience, improve outcomes for their teams, and decrease their healthcare costs.

HOW WE LIVE OUR VALUES TO OUR TEAMMATES:

We’re seeking those with passion for healthcare and relentless devotion to our goal. We need team members that embody our core values:

1) We are human, first
Our humanity binds us together. We bring the same empathetic approach to every individual we engage with, whether it be our members, our clients, or each other. We are all worthy of respect and understanding and we engage in our interactions with care and intention. We honor our stories. We listen to—and hear—each other, we celebrate our differences and similarities, we are present for each other, and we strive for mutual understanding.

2) We redefine what is possible
We always look beyond the obstacles in front of us to imagine new solutions. We approach our work with inspiration from other industries, other leaders, and other challenges. We use ingenuity and resourcefulness when faced with tough problems.

3) We debate then commit
We believe that a spirit of open discourse is part of a healthy culture. We understand and appreciate different perspectives and we challenge our assumptions. When working toward a decision or a new solution, we actively listen to one another, approach it with a “yes, and” mentality, and assume positive intent. Once a decision is made, we align and champion it as one team.

4) We cultivate grit
Changing healthcare doesn’t happen overnight. We reflect and learn from challenges and approach the future with a determination to strive for better. In the face of daunting situations, we value persistence. We embrace failure as a stepping stone to future success. On this journey, we seek to act with guts, resilience, initiative, and tenacity.

5) We seek to delight
Healthcare is complicated and personal. We work tirelessly to meet the goals of our clients while also delivering the best experience to our members. We recognize that no matter the role or team, we each play a crucial part in our members’ care and take that responsibility seriously. When faced with an obstacle, we are kind, respectful, and solution-oriented in our approach. We hold ourselves accountable to our clients and our members’ success.

Rightway is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer that believes in the strength of diverse thought, beliefs, backgrounds, and education. We foster an inclusive culture where differences are celebrated to drive the best business decisions possible. We do not discriminate on any basis protected by applicable law. All employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, need, and performance.

jobs.title: Staff Design Reliability Engineer
jobs.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for a Design Reliability Engineer, reporting to the Director of Design Reliability, to support the development of the systems that will be required for the design and build of artificial-gravity human-rated space stations.

This will be a full-time, exempt position located in our Long Beach location.

Responsibilities:

• Technical Leadership: Lead the technical reviews that shape the future of artificial-gravity space habitats—providing clear, decisive guidance during milestone design reviews and major risk gates.

• Oversee qualification and test completeness for flight systems, ensuring our test campaigns are robust, disciplined, and aligned with human-rated reliability.

• Bring deep engineering intuition to test campaigns, identifying risks early and helping teams converge on safe, resilient solutions.

• Evaluate complex design and operational changes, safeguarding technical integrity as the system evolves.

• Design Excellence: Serve as the architect and guardian of Vast’s engineering standards, design guides, and review frameworks—tools that enable fast, confident decision-making across the company.

• Make engineering best practices accessible and actionable, especially for engineers moving rapidly under ambitious program timelines.

• Support and elevate engineering teams across the organization by bringing broad experience in design, build cycles, integration, and test.

• Turn organizational knowledge into lasting guidance by capturing lessons learned and strengthening future standards.

• Process Ownership: Build and steward the processes that ensure engineering rigor at scale—ensuring designs meet standards, reviews are comprehensive, and changes are consistently implemented.

• Own and continuously refine design review templates, reliability checklists, and internal design guides.

• Track design maturity and compliance across the station and vehicle architecture, ensuring nothing slips through the cracks.

jobs.title: Payer Partnerships Lead
jobs.description:
About Us

Health is the most important thing in life, and the American healthcare system is completely broken - poor outcomes, high cost, bad patient experience. We're building a new system from the ground up.

Our mission is to improve people’s health by making it easy to live a healthy lifestyle.

Nourish is the country's largest dietitian-led metabolic health clinic. We’re an AI-native digital health system matching patients with 10,000+ Registered Dietitians, physicians, medications, lab testing, and AI agents to deliver insurance-covered care across all 50 states. Founded four years ago, we've completed millions of appointments, tripled year-over-year, and partnered with health plans covering 200M+ Americans across 250+ health systems.

In 2026 we raised a $100M Series C, bringing total funding to $215M. The round was led by Menlo Ventures, with participation from Thrive Capital, Index Ventures, J.P. Morgan Growth Equity Partners, Maverick Ventures, Y Combinator, BoxGroup, Atomico, Daybreak, and Operator Partners.

Learn more about our Series C here: Nourish Blog, Bloomberg, Fierce Healthcare, Digital Native, The Pulse Podcast.

This is not a job for everyone. We hold an extremely high bar because we believe talent density is our biggest competitive advantage. We're looking for people who actively choose hard, ambiguous problems, who run toward unglamorous work, give and receive candid feedback, and bring relentless resilience without the ego. Our work is important, but we are not self-important. We do this because we’re solving one of the hardest problems in the world, and the problem matters. If that's you, we disproportionately reward it.

About the Role

As Payer Partnerships Lead, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the strategy and execution of Nourish’s partnerships with leading health plans. You will be responsible for owning the strategy and business development process end to end with the country’s top payers, designing and closing value-based deals and fostering close relationships with health plan executives. Your work will shape the future of Nourish as you designing innovative partnerships that expand access for nutrition therapy and deepen our impact on patients.

This role is full-time and open to NYC-based candidates only (expectation to work in-person 3-4 days per week, with some remote flexibility). Our office is in the heart of Flatiron. Occasional travel expected (e.g. to conferences, priority payer meetings, etc.)

Key Responsibilities:

• Manage a revenue generating book of top health plans - be the single point owner for 5-10 health plan relationships, defining the strategy and partnership playbook for each plan and executing against that strategy to help us expand access, increase rates, and build strategic, long-lasting relationships

• Design and drive our health plan strategy – define our partnership strategy and lead end-to-end relationships with top health plans. Shape engagement approaches, structure game-changing deals, and be the face of Nourish to your health plan partners

• Build trusted executive networks – develop deep, strategic partnerships with payer leaders. Create champions who will advocate for Nourish internally, unlocking influence and momentum across complex organizations

• Design & close transformative deals – craft and negotiate innovative agreements, including value-based care models. Push beyond status quo contracting to secure deals that expand access and align with Nourish’s long-term growth vision.

• Tell a powerful story – adapt and deliver Nourish’s value proposition compellingly to VP and C-suite audiences, tailoring every conversation to resonate with each payer’s unique priorities and challenges.

• Bring the ‘voice of the payer’ to our team – share and translate commercial, real-time insights to inform our product, clinical, and growth strategy. Partner cross-functionally to translate payer feedback into bold strategic moves, including new products.

We’d love to hear from you if:

• You have 3-5 years of experience in highly strategic roles (e.g. management consulting, business operations) — extra points if you have commercial/go-to-market experience or healthcare/payer knowledge, but not a must

• You’re energized by 0→1 work and ambiguity, and enjoy stepping into undefined spaces to build structure, momentum, and clarity where none exists.

• You’re a strategic thinker who values speed and learning, comfortable testing ideas, iterating based on signal, and evolving your approach over time.

• You have a strong commercial mindset and executive presence, with the ability to craft compelling narratives and influence VP- and C-suite stakeholders.

• You have experience building strong client relationships — whether in consulting, strategy, partnerships, GTM, or a high-growth startup environment — and are comfortable representing a company externally.

• You’re operationally excellent, able to manage a high volume of moving pieces and competing priorities with strong attention to detail, while still maintaining momentum and clarity in a fast-paced environment.

• You’re highly collaborative and cross-functional, able to work effectively across partnerships, growth, product, clinical, and operations teams to drive impact.

jobs.title: Director, Head of Protein Sciences
jobs.description:
Summary

We are seeking an accomplished scientific and organizational leader to serve as Head of Protein Sciences.  This role is accountable for defining and executing the Protein Sciences strategy to accelerate portfolio progression through the delivery of high-quality protein reagents, target-enabling solutions, and scientific insights for small molecule and peptide discovery programs across therapeutic areas.

As the functional leader of Protein Sciences, the successful candidate will ensure the organization delivers scalable, high-impact support across the portfolio while balancing current program needs with future capability requirements. The leader will report to the Head of Target Enabling Technologies organization and serve on the extended leadership team of Small Molecule Therapeutics and Platform Technologies. Working in close partnership with Biology, Screening, Structural Biology, and other functions, this leader will influence discovery strategies, optimize resource deployment, and enable successful advancement of programs against challenging targets.

This role requires a leader who combines deep scientific expertise, strategic thinking, and operational excellence to maximize organizational impact, improve portfolio execution, and build a high-performing scientific organization.

Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

• Define and execute a Protein Sciences strategy that maximizes impact across the discovery portfolio through efficient delivery of target-enabling proteins, scientific solutions, and resource deployment.
• Accountable for the overall performance, portfolio impact, scientific excellence, and organizational effectiveness of the Protein Sciences function.
• Partner with cross-functional leaders to influence discovery strategies, address target-enabling challenges, and ensure Protein Sciences resources are deployed against highest-value portfolio opportunities.
• Drive scientific innovation and adoption of emerging technologies, including AI/ML-enabled approaches, protein engineering, and next-generation protein production platforms to support emerging target classes and future portfolio needs.
• Manage project intake and lead functional resource planning and prioritization to ensure effective support across the portfolio.
• Manage external collaborations and CRO partnerships to augment capabilities and accelerate project delivery.
• Balance short-term portfolio needs with long-term capability building and technology investments
• Build external awareness of emerging scientific approaches and evaluate opportunities for scientific collaboration.

Scientific Leadership

• Provide scientific leadership and oversight to ensure delivery of high-quality protein reagents and scientific data that support project advancement.
• Lead teams in addressing complex scientific problems and developing innovative, fit-for-purpose solutions that advance discovery programs.
• Foster scientific rigor, innovation, and data-driven decision-making across the department.
• Represent Protein Sciences as a key scientific partner on cross-functional discovery teams.
• Establish and maintain external scientific relationships to ensure awareness and adoption of innovative technologies and best practices.

Talent Development and Organizational Leadership

• Build and lead a high-performing Protein Sciences organization that consistently delivers high-quality outcomes, develops talent, and contributes measurably to portfolio success.
• Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
• Develop future scientific and people leaders through coaching, mentoring, performance management, and succession planning.
• Foster strong cross-functional partnerships that accelerate progression of the programs and improve organizational effectiveness.

jobs.title: Financial Counselor
jobs.description:
Who is Spring Fertility?

We are a passionate, dedicated team of leading physicians and scientists who have trained at some of the world’s top research hospitals and fertility centers. Together, we are building the fastest-growing fertility group in the country, grounded in clinical excellence and innovation. We deliver deeply patient-centric, individualized, and compassionate care, recognizing that every journey is unique. Our mission is to partner with patients to help them achieve their goals, whatever those may be. We believe everyone deserves the opportunity to build a family if they choose, and our team is committed to guiding and supporting patients every step of the way.

Why should you join our team?

We are a mission-driven organization seeking motivated, high-performing professionals who are eager to innovate and make an impact. As we build a first-class fertility practice, we balance excellence with a culture that values collaboration, positivity, and enjoyment in the work we do. We are growing rapidly and are deeply committed to the professional and personal development of our team. Guided by optimism, compassion, and teamwork, we are united by a shared dedication to putting patients first.

Role Summary

Spring's Financial Counselors assists patients with treatment estimates and collaborates with external parties to ensure their financial coverage. Working independently, the Financial Counselor will explain financial information, determine insurance coverage, and educate the patients on their financial options.

Some day-to-day responsibilities include:

• Furnishing patients and healthcare providers with estimates related to upcoming treatment

• Collecting estimated liabilities from patients and applying payments to patient accounts

• Acquire knowledge of patient’s insurance coverage and benefit limits and communicate it to the patients to make them aware of their financial responsibilities

• Communicate to internal staff in a clear and concise manner the financial status of the patient by analyzing and reviewing the patient’s accounts receivables and trying to resolve any issues related to it

• Initiating prior authorization requests per insurance carrier requirements

• Ensure reimbursement is obtained for medical services provided for non-insured and under-insurance patients

• Identify and work to minimize potential financial risk of patient accounts through working daily time of service reports

• Act as a resource representative when questions arise regarding registration errors, proper insurance documentation and accounting correction

Education and Skills

• A Bachelor’s degree

• 2 + years of experience in fertility or healthcare

• Proficient knowledge of medical terminology and billing practices

• Proficiency in MS Office required

• Experience with electronic medical records

• Exceptional communication and organizational skills

• Ability to simplify complex concepts to patients

• Flexible availability which may include working some weekends and holidays

Employment Type

This is a full-time (40 hours a week/8 hours per day) exempt onsite position.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is $67,000 - $72,000 annually. Salary is based on several factors including job related knowledge and skill set, depth of experience, certifications and/or degrees.

Benefits

Investing in You Today and Tomorrow

Supporting your well-being

• Competitive medical, dental, and vision plans

• Paid time off to recharge and enjoy personal time

• Access to BetterHelp therapy sessions for mental and emotional wellness

• Commuter benefits and discounted rates on home, auto, and pet insurance

Investing in your future

• 401(k) with up to a 4% company match

• Comprehensive fertility and parental leave benefits

• Career development opportunities in a fast-growing organization

• Employer-paid life and disability insurance

*Temporary and contract roles may not be eligible for all benefits listed above

Don’t have it all? We still welcome you to apply!

At Spring Fertility, we believe that everyone who wants a family deserves to have one, regardless of gender, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, or religion. Just as we acknowledge and value the diversity of goals, life experiences, and unique paths to parenthood among our patients, we also actively celebrate diversity within our organization. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to a safe and inclusive work environment for all. We recognize that diversity among our team allows us to not only more effectively serve our patients, but also to advance innovation and opportunity within our field. We encourage qualified applicants of every background, ability, and life experience to apply to our employment opportunities.

We are scientists. We are humanists. We are passionate about fertility.

This is a highly visible, strategic role where your work will directly shape the way the organization leverages Workday for years to come.

Workday Ownership & Configuration

• Manage Workday tenant configuration, business processes, and system settings.
• Lead updates, releases, and system enhancements.
• Maintain documentation, configuration guides, and training materials.
• Evaluate and implement new Workday features to maximize organizational impact.

Troubleshooting & Tier 3 Support

• Train and enable Tier 1 & Tier 2 support teams to resolve issues effectively.
• Manage ticket queues and resolve challenging system problems.

Change Management & Cross-Functional Leadership

• Technical Proficiency: Experience with cloud platforms, enterprise integrations, Microsoft Office 365, and data reporting/analytics tools (Prism, calculated fields, dashboards).

• Professional Certifications: Workday certifications (HCM, Finance, Security), additional Workday security or reporting certifications. CompTIA A+ Certification, or other IT certifications.

Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with knowledge of cybersecurity, data privacy, disaster recovery, and compliance. Able to support complex, multi-unit environments efficiently.

jobs.title: 2026-27 Special Education Teacher (5th/6th HUM ICT)
jobs.description:
About Us

Brilla Schools, a growing K-8 network in the Bronx, serves over 2,000 students with plans to expand to educate 3,000 across four elementary and four middle schools. Managed by Seton Education Partners, Brilla Schools are dedicated to forming students of strong wisdom and virtue. Our classically inspired approach to education combines a content-rich curriculum, inquiry-driven learning, and a focus on virtues, while providing individualized support to meet each child’s unique needs. A national leader in character education and supporting students with varying needs, over the past two years, Brilla alumni have secured spots in the most prestigious high schools in the tri-state area, earning over $3 million in scholarships and financial aid. Our staff are mission-aligned change-makers who believe in fostering a joyful, rigorous learning environment, and Brilla offers some of the most competitive salaries in the market to honor their dedication. With high expectations and a supportive community, we’re preparing students to excel in high school, college, and beyond.

Position Overview
The primary responsibility of a Middle School Humanities Integrated Co-Teaching (ICT) Specialist is to cultivate and lead a learning environment where every child feels safe and confident to strive for and meet Brilla’s ambitious targets. The Middle School Humanities ICT Specialist understands, plans, and executes key elements of innovative pedagogy, co-teaching practices, and data-based decision-making through a deep love of learning and commitment to internalizing and teaching rigorous classical content in an inspiring and culturally relevant way. This position requires a classically-minded, positive, flexible, solutions-oriented, organized, and innovative educator who aims to challenge the status quo of the current educational landscape in urban areas. Brilla teachers must have a deep passion for student-engaged learning, a desire to accept, implement, and seek feedback, and a proven ability to manage multiple concurrent tasks and responsibilities while inspiring outstanding achievement in children in a fun and collaborative work environment, serving specific grade levels as assigned.

Core Competencies & Responsibilities

• Serve as the special education teacher in an Integrated Co-Teaching (ICT) classroom, ensuring delivery of the ICT mandate as written on students’ IEPs in alignment with NYSED requirements

• Collaboratively plan with the general education teacher using academic and behavioral data to design instruction that embeds SDI aligned to IEP goals while ensuring students can access grade-level Humanities curriculum and standards.

• Collaboratively plan with the general education teacher using academic and behavioral data to design instruction that embeds Specially Designed Instruction (SDI) aligned to IEP goals while ensuring students can access grade-level STEM curriculum and standards.

• Co-teach using a variety of co-teaching models intentionally selected to maximize student access to grade-level content

• Demonstrate deep knowledge of Specially Designed Instruction (SDI) through clear, objective-driven instruction and active student engagement, and provide SDI tailored to meet the unique needs of each student with disabilities

• Serve as the case manager for assigned ICT students, including writing Present Levels of Academic and Functional Performance (PLOPs), teacher reports, and facilitating IEP meetings with the Committee on Special Education

• Progress monitor and document student progress toward academic IEP goals at required intervals and complete accurate IEP Progress Reports

• Use progress monitoring data to inform the revision and development of IEP goals, ensuring goals remain responsive to student growth and instructional needs

• Implement proactive behavior supports and environmental structures aligned to students’ IEP needs to maintain access to instruction

• Collaborate with colleagues to improve outcomes for students with disabilities and contribute to an inclusive learning environment across the school community

• Participate in school and community events to build strong relationships with colleagues and families and contribute to a positive, inclusive school culture

• Participate in special education and content-specific professional development, grade team meetings, and school-based initiatives to continuously strengthen instructional practice

• Participate in MTSS meetings to analyze student data, contribute insights, and support the development of targeted interventions and instructional adjustments

• Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s Degree or higher from an accredited institution (preferably in the Liberal Arts, Philosophy, or Classics-related field)

• Active New York State teaching certification in Students with Disabilities or currently enrolled in an NYSED-approved program leading to special education certification required.

• Relevant urban, middle school teaching experience with demonstrated student results (preferred)

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills

• Experience using SESIS to manage IEP documentation (strongly preferred)

• Spanish language proficiency (preferred)

Benefits
At Brilla Schools, we celebrate the unique skills, experiences, and passions that each staff member brings to our mission. To support their work, we offer a thoughtfully designed benefits package to provide competitive and adaptable coverage. We are committed to offering a benefits portfolio that supports the holistic health and wellness of our team members including:

• Comprehensive Professional Development: More than 225 hours annually, featuring two weeks of onboarding, coaching, and targeted training sessions to ensure staff excel in their roles and flourish.

• Community and Culture: An intentionally joyful workplace with over 30 bonding events each year, fostering connection and collaboration among staff and families in the Bronx.

• Flexible Health Coverage: A full suite of medical, dental, and vision plans designed to support diverse needs, utilizing Cigna and Anthem provider networks.

• Competitive Compensation: A salary range of $71,020 - $115,479, with pay varying within this range based on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

• Retirement Plans: A 403(b) plan and 401(k) retirement options with matching contributions, helping you secure your financial future while you grow with us.

• Work-Life Balance: Generous paid time off, a DOE-aligned school calendar, and wellness resources to support personal renewal and sustained excellence.

At Brilla, your dedication fuels our mission, and we’re here to invest in your growth, well-being, and success—from recruitment to retirement!

Please note: The above is based on the 2025-2026 plan year. You can find more information here.

The base pay range for this position is $71,020 - $115,479 per year, with pay varying based on your unique job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. You'll enjoy a comprehensive benefits package including medical, financial, and more. Plus, as an extra incentive, candidates who begin employment on or before October 15, 2026 are eligible for a $4,000 signing bonus paid in two installments over the course of their first year of employment. Agency applicants are excluded from receiving this bonus.

Brilla Schools is an equal opportunity employer. Brilla Schools provides equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees.

Be sure to input your full legal name in your application.

Beware of phishing attempts. After applying, initial outreach from Brilla Schools will only come from an @us-greenhouse-mail.io email address. Brilla Schools will never reach out with a job offer before a face-to-face interview.

jobs.description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

What you’ll do

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

• Monitor VSI (forecasted status) vs. target related to total product business case per main system and streamline financial reporting and analyses to teams

• Leverage data to highlight key areas where business can reduce costs

• Identify process inefficiencies or bottlenecks in main system decision making processes

• Decision making value of up to 1M amount

• Conduct product business case calculations and steer discussions to address financial concerns and recommendations for implementation

• Ensure project decisions are delivered on-time to meet product development process (PEP) timing guidelines for on-time SOP delivery

• Work with cross-functional teams to manage product development targets, ensuring adherence to target constraints

• Prepare working packages for finance related topics because of main system discussions

• Administration of main controlling system FAKIS

• Central contact to VW AG IT administration

• Conduct ad-hoc scenarios upon request for strategic topics

• This role requires 3 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.

• Applicants should expect that the role may require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.

• Travel: Domestic and international travel required, approximately 1 - 10% of the time. Passport required.

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

• Education/Certifications: A Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Engineering, or a related technical field.

• 4+ Years of Experience Finance or other relevant experience (Project Steering, Engineering, Purchasing, Production, etc.)

• Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills

• Ability to accurately compile, translate, and present financial information in a clear concise manner, often in PowerPoint, to leadership and a broad audience including non-finance professionals

• Implement a solution-oriented approach for main project issues through cross-functional collaboration

• Strong analytical and data visualization skill (Excel advanced proficiency, including but not limited to: financial modeling, macro generation, business case evaluation, scenario & sensitivity analysis and PowerBI)

• Knowledge of business process management and organization

• Knowledge of automotive technology and market (component cost, production, market trends and strategies, automotive process knowledge, cost market strategy, portfolio strategy)

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up.  This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation.  In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. Program specifics are detailed in company policies and employee benefit guides, select highlights:

• Competitive insurance including: Medical, dental, vision and income protection plans

• 401(k) program with: An employer match and immediate vesting

• Generous Paid Time Off including: 20 days planned PTO, as accrued 40 hours of unplanned PTO and 14 company or floating holidays, annually Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave for biological and adoptive parents of all genders Paid leave for circumstances related to bereavement, jury duty, voting time, or military leave

Pay Transparency

This is a full-time, exempt position eligible to receive a base salary and to participate in an annual performance bonus program. Final salary offered will be determined based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience. The annual performance bonus program is preset and not candidate dependent.

Equal Opportunity

jobs.title: Growth Strategy, Senior Associate | Housing
jobs.description:
About EliseAI

At EliseAI, we're improving the industries that matter most: housing and healthcare. Everyone needs a place to live and access to quality healthcare, yet both are often harder to secure than they should be. 

By integrating AI agents deeply into existing workflows, we make them more efficient, reduce costs, and improve the experience for everyone.



 - Housing: We simplify how renters tour apartments, sign leases, submit maintenance requests, and stay connected with their property team—bringing everything they need for their home into one place.

 - Healthcare: We make it easy to schedule appointments, complete intake forms, and we help patients communicate with providers, so everyone can focus on health instead of paperwork.
   
   

With EliseAI, organizations reduce manual work, improve accessibility, and deliver a seamless experience across essential services. We recently raised a $250 million Series E round https://www.eliseai.com/blog/eliseai-raises-250m-series-e led by Andreessen Horowitz to accelerate this mission.

 

The Growth Strategy Team

The Growth Strategy team is responsible for defining how EliseAI is positioned, understood, and valued in the market. We own the positioning and identity of the platform and every product within it, and we design and execute the highest-leverage growth initiatives that drive the company forward and generate pipeline.

Growth Strategy operates as a startup within a startup-run with the intensity and ownership of a founding team, but with the capital, market access, and product depth of a well-funded Series E. The mandate is zero to one: take products and platform capabilities from undefined to sharply positioned, then drive execution against that positioning across every surface that touches the market. Deep cross-functional involvement (Product, Sales, Engineering, Leadership) and founder-level ownership from day one.

Roles on this team sit at the intersection that defines the best people at EliseAI: strategic thinking and deep context awareness, combined with technical ability and full ownership of execution. You will be expected to move fluidly between crafting a product narrative and building the automated systems that deliver it at scale-between shaping a go-to-market strategy and getting your hands into the data, tooling, and infrastructure to make it real.

 

About The Role

As a Senior Associate on the Growth Strategy team, you’ll own high-impact projects end-to-end-taking products and capabilities from undefined to sharply positioned, then building and executing the go-to-market programs that turn that positioning into pipeline and revenue.

The work has real range. In a given week, you might develop the positioning and messaging for a product capability, architect an automated customer engagement program, build the enablement materials for a major launch, and dig into performance data to sharpen our approach. You’ll operate with a high degree of direction and support on strategic priorities, but you’ll be expected to own the execution fully-from strategy through delivery, including the technical build where needed.

This role is ideal for someone with a strategy, consulting, or operational background who wants to apply that rigor to problems that directly determine how an AI company grows-and who is excited to get into the technical details of building the systems, not just defining the strategy.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Positioning & Value

 - Develop positioning and messaging for specific products and capabilities-translating complex AI functionality into clear, differentiated value propositions that resonate with buyers

 - Analyze win/loss trends, customer feedback, and market dynamics to surface insights that sharpen how we articulate value and where we focus

 

Customer Engagement & Growth

 - Design and build automated customer engagement programs-developing nurture sequences, onboarding flows, and retention campaigns that drive measurable pipeline acceleration and lifetime value

 - Track and analyze engagement performance-using data and dashboards to identify what’s working, what’s not, and how to improve

 

Go-to-Market Execution

 - Execute product launches from positioning through delivery-coordinating across Product, Sales, and Customer Success to bring new capabilities to market with clarity and momentum

 - Create high-impact sales enablement tools-developing decks, one-pagers, and training materials that equip our sales team to communicate value effectively

 - Contribute strategic thinking to leadership conversations about growth, market expansion, and customer value

 - Attract top-tier talent to join our driven team

 

Move at rocket speed, build something massive.

We’re scaling fast, solving real client problems with precision and ambition. Here, you own your impact-full autonomy, no micromanagement, no fluff. We hire the best, expect the best, and give you the masterclass of your career. It’s hard, it’s intense, and it’s the most rewarding work you’ll ever do. If you’re hungry, driven, and ready to build something massive, climb aboard.

 

Requirements

We’re looking for intensely driven, founder-minded people who want to test themselves and build something transformational. You likely:

 - Have 3–5 years of experience in management consulting, investment banking, strategy & operations, growth, or a generalist role at a high-growth startup

 - Are biased toward action and comfortable making decisions with imperfect information

 - Can structure ambiguous problems into clear plans and execute them independently

 - Communicate with precision-whether you’re writing a product narrative, building a deck, or presenting to executives

 - Are equally comfortable with strategic thinking and technical execution-you want to define the strategy and build the system that delivers it

 - Naturally build relationships across functions and can influence without authority

 - Are willing to work in person at our office 4 days a week

 

Why Join

Growth and impact. It’s not often that you can get in on the ground floor of a funded (unicorn!) startup that’s scaling so fast. That means that instead of following a playbook, you’ll be writing it. Every single day you will be challenged to identify how we can scale and execute on it. You’ll learn what works when you succeed and what doesn’t when you fail. Either way, the rest of the team will be here to support you.

 

Benefits

In addition to the growth and impact you’ll have at EliseAI, we offer competitive salaries along with the following benefits:

 - Equity in the company

 - Medical, Dental and Vision premiums covered at 100%

 - Fully paid parental leave

 - Commuter benefits

 - 401k benefits

 - Fitness & home services stipend to cover part of your expenses so you can focus on what matters

 - A collaborative in-office environment with an open floor plan, fully stocked kitchen, and all meals covered in the office

 - Unlimited vacation and paid holidays

 - We’ll cover relocation packages and make the move exciting, not painful!

 

Job Compensation Range

The salary range for this role is $130,000 - $180,000. EliseAI offers a competitive total rewards package which includes base salary, equity, and a comprehensive benefits & perks package. Exact compensation is determined based on a number of factors including experience, skill level, location and qualifications which are assessed during the interview process. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided by our Recruiting Team during the hiring process.

 

EliseAI provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Employment with EliseAI is on an “at-will” basis, meaning that either the employee or the company may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause or notice, subject to applicable law.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We will also consider qualified applicants in accordance with the Austin Fair Chance Hiring Ordinance.

If you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation during the application or recruiting process due to a disability, please contact us at interview.accommodations@meetelise.com.

jobs.title: Customer Success Executive
jobs.description:
Who We Are

QGenda is redefining healthcare workforce management everywhere care is delivered. We're on a mission to empower the healthcare industry to better onboarding, deploy, and manage their workforce. Over 4,500 healthcare organizations have trusted us to help them make strategic workforce decisions through our unified software platform. With more than 800 employees across the US, we are united in our vision and culture to make a difference for our customers, while enjoying the day-to-day.

At QGenda, we value our employees and their contributions toward the success of the business. We strive to create a dynamic work environment that fosters growth, innovation, and collaboration, where employees can be proud of the work they do and the impact it has on the healthcare industry.

QGenda is headquartered in Atlanta.

To learn more about QGenda, visit us at qgenda.com or follow us on Instagram or LinkedIn.

About Your Role

The Customer Success Executive works within our Customer Experience (CX) organization and provides exceptional program management to QGenda’s highest-value customers by driving adoption of QGenda product features and functionality to deliver measurable business outcomes, increase customer stickiness, and reduce churn risk.

By partnering closely with super users and executive sponsors, the Customer Success Executive ensures the QGenda platform is meeting enterprise needs while expanding realized value across the organization. The CSX is responsible not only for driving adoption, but also for helping customers define success metrics, track progress, and understand the operational and financial value achieved through QGenda.

Customer Success Executives leverage best practices, customer insights, and deep QGenda product knowledge when leading post go-live initiatives. They develop trusted advisor relationships with key stakeholders, clearly articulate outcomes and ROI to executive audiences, and open the door for system-wide growth opportunities grounded in demonstrated customer value.

How You’ll Make an Impact

As a critical member of the Customer Success team, you will strategically guide enterprise customers through their QGenda journey, utilizing personal touch, technical expertise, and outcome-oriented engagement to increase adoption, drive expansion, demonstrate realized value, and ensure long-term customer retention.

Core Responsibilities:

• Own success, renewal, and long-term value realization across an assigned portfolio of enterprise customers, maintaining continuous visibility into account health, risks, and growth opportunities

• Partner with customers to define success metrics and baseline outcomes, track progress over time, and connect QGenda usage to measurable operational, financial, or workforce impact

• Drive adoption and optimization of the QGenda platform in service of customer-defined outcomes, not just feature utilization

• Proactively identify emerging risks early and serve as the primary point of escalation for assigned accounts, exercising independent judgment to align internal teams and resolve complex issues

• Lead the development and execution of recovery or “get well” plans when accounts are at risk, remaining accountable through resolution

• Build and maintain trusted relationships with customer executive and operational leaders, earning credibility through preparation, insight, and clear points of view

• Lead Executive Business Reviews and other strategic engagements, presenting a data-backed narrative on realized value, risks, and recommended next actions aligned to customer priorities

• Support expansion and renewal conversations through demonstrated outcomes and executive-level value articulation

• Establish and maintain structured engagement and governance cadences that ensure predictable execution, clear communication, and alignment across stakeholders

• Ensure compliance with Customer Success operating standards, including accurate Account Success Plans, health indicators, success metrics, and reporting within the Customer Success Platform (Planhat)

• Prepare for and actively participate in internal Key Account Reviews, clearly communicating account health, value realization, risks, and recommended actions to leadership

• Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Support, Sales, and other teams to advocate for customer needs and drive aligned execution

Key Duties:

• Independently and confidently manages a portfolio of highly complex accounts, including large-scale, multiple-product deploys with unique or technically complicated business cases and/or ARR of $1M+ per customer

• Manages multiple key stakeholders, including internal, external, and executive leadership, for influence across all levels of an organization

• Acts as a QGenda platform master who can be brought into any situation to provide technical/functional expertise both internally and externally

• Holds a detailed understanding of the business case, technical capabilities, and market strategy for each product in QGenda's product suite

• Independently and confidently manages high-level customer escalations; identifies risk and drives mitigation strategies and get-well plans across QG leadership and teams

• Confidently resolves communication breakdowns with the ability to bridge the differences between stakeholders quickly

• Develops new ways of communicating technical information to various audiences; Creates repeatable SOPs, best practices, processes, templates, and systems for others to use

• Develops newer CSX employees by supporting employee growth and providing feedback to both them and to their managers

• Fully understands IT landscape of healthcare enterprises and strategically leverages this knowledge to drive expansion and integration while mitigating risk

• Portfolio demonstrates consistent NRR growth year over year

• Executes Key Account Reviews on-time and with minimal support; drives strategy and execution for Executive Business Reviews without significant support

• Leverages thorough knowledge of the the Customer Success Platform (Planhat) to implement new processes, metrics, and KPIs for CSX accounts

Who You Are

• Strong executive presence with the ability to lead complex customer conversations and influence outcomes at multiple organizational levels

• Ability to translate customer business goals into technical and workflow solutions that deliver measurable value

• Proven judgment in managing ambiguity, prioritizing effectively, and balancing strategic thinking with operational rigor

• Strong analytical and communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate outcomes, risks, and ROI

• Deep curiosity and growing expertise in healthcare operations, workforce management, and the healthcare IT ecosystem

Experience You Bring

• Bachelor's Degree

• 2+ years of post-sales customer relationship management OR 2+ years of relevant healthcare industry experience

• Ability to travel for customer meetings, conferences, and other industry events

Not Required, but Nice to Have

• Experience with Customer Success Platforms (i.e. PlanHat)

• Experience/exposure to healthcare market and IT ecosystem

Applicants for this position must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States (U.S.), including being located in the US. We are unable to sponsor, take over sponsorship of, or hire candidates with an employment visa at this time.

What’s In It For You

We offer a comprehensive total rewards package to support our full-time employees and their family’s day-to-day needs, well-being and major life events, which includes:

• Fully company-paid options for medical (both in-person and virtual), dental and vision insurance

• Generous paid time off (PTO) policy to enjoy periods of uninterrupted rest and relaxation for a healthy work/life balance

• Paid parental leave for birth, adoption or permanent placement

• 401(k) with company match

• Annual Costco membership, cell phone stipend, commuter benefits, in-office perks and more

QGenda delivers technology solutions to improve how healthcare is delivered and increase access — for everyone. We can only succeed by bringing together diverse minds, thoughts, ideas and team members to create better solutions for our customers and make us a better company as a whole. We are committed to creating a culture of embracing diversity, inclusion and equity for all.

QGenda is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and makes all employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, natural origin, ancestry, age, marital status, disability or genetic information, military status, status as a disabled or protected veteran or any other protected status under applicable law.

jobs.title: Electrical Design Engineer – Power Distribution
jobs.description:
Electrical Design Engineer – Power Distribution  | Burnsville, MN

JOB SUMMARY

We are seeking a motivated and hardworking individual to join our team in Burnsville, MN as a Electrical Design Engineer – Power Distribution . You will be part of a group of engineers dedicated to high-quality work, value-add solutions, skill development, and career growth. We  welcome candidates from the Minneapolis metro and beyond to apply.

This role leads electrical design efforts for a major product line redesign, developing schematics, wiring diagrams, one‑lines, and layout drawings for power distribution equipment. The Electrical Design Engineer interprets customer and site requirements, defines electrical specifications, supports certification and compliance activities, and produces detailed documentation for manufacturing and testing. This position works closely with cross‑functional teams, suppliers, and engineering partners while contributing to design standardization, process improvements, and on‑site engineering discussions in a fast‑moving, collaborative environment.

As a Electrical Design Engineer – Power Distribution , you will:

• Own all electrical design activities for a product line redesign effort

• Develop electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, one‑lines, and layout drawings using industry‑standard CAD tools

• Interpret customer specifications, site requirements, and technical constraints to create accurate, compliant electrical system solutions

• Define electrical specifications, component selections, and system architectures for power distribution equipment including switchgear, switchboards, transfer switches, load banks, and docking stations

• Produce detailed technical documentation supporting manufacturing, testing, certification, and customer requests

• Collaborate with SMEs, cross‑functional teams, suppliers, and internal stakeholders throughout the project

• Ensure electrical designs meet safety, performance, manufacturability, and relevant code/standard requirements

• Support certification and compliance activities including UL 1008, UL 508, UL 1640, NEC, and other applicable standards

• Maintain electrical documentation, BOMs, and revisions within ERP, PLM, and Vault systems

• Contribute to process improvements, modularization, and design standardization initiatives

• Participate in design reviews, prototyping sessions, and on‑site engineering discussions

• Work collaboratively with suppliers and Applied partners

• Contribute to projects that impact communities in the greater Minneapolis metro

• Apply your skills in a dynamic environment that values ownership and innovation

QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering

• Experience in electrical design for custom‑engineered power distribution or electromechanical systems

• Proficiency with electrical CAD tools for schematics, wiring diagrams, and layout drawings

• Experience interpreting customer specifications and site requirements to develop electrical system solutions

• Knowledge of electrical design best practices including safety, performance, manufacturability, and compliance

• Experience creating technical documentation to support manufacturing, testing, and certification

• Experience with switchgear, switchboards, transfer switches, load banks, or related power distribution equipment

• Familiarity with UL standards such as UL 1008, UL 508, and UL 1640

• Experience with ERP, PLM, and engineering vault systems for managing design documentation and BOMs

• Background in process improvement, modularization, or design automation

• Project management experience including coordinating cross‑functional teams and tracking deliverables strongly preferred

• Capable of working independently and as a team member

• Strong work ethic and unwavering integrity

• Excellent interpersonal skills and a learning mindset

• Curiosity, problem solving, and analytical thinking

• Effective verbal and written communication

• Desire to work on a variety of projects

Engineer I: $40.45–$46.52/hour

Engineer II: $44.14–$50.76/hour

Engineer III: $47.83–$55.00/hour

Senior Engineer: $51.51–$59.24/hour

Final compensation is based on experience, skills, and alignment with role expectations. Paid overtime may be available.

COMPANY OVERVIEW

Applied Engineering is a 100% employee-owned engineering consulting company dedicated to providing exceptional talent and service to manufacturers across the Midwest and beyond. We have won numerous awards, including Best Place to Work and Top Place to Intern.

Innovation, problem solving, integrity, and collaboration are a few things you'll experience and represent while working with Applied. If you appreciate a challenge, variety, and a quicker pace, then we would like to get to know you better.

Our unique company culture blends talent, technology, and flexibility. We offer a career trajectory few others can match, with opportunities to take on roles and assignments aligned with your skills and interests.

In addition, we offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package including:

• Competitive salary

• 401K retirement plan

• Paid time off and paid holidays

• Continuing Education Support

• Medical, dental, vision, life, disability, and other insurance options

• Paid overtime

jobs.title: Test and Commissioning Engineer
jobs.description:
Who we are:

Glydways is reimagining what public transit can be. We believe that mobility is the gateway to opportunity—connecting people to housing, education, employment, commerce, and care. By making transportation more accessible, affordable, and sustainable, we empower communities to thrive and unlock economic and social prosperity.

Our mission is to revolutionize transit with a solution that delivers high capacity, exceptional user experiences, unmatched affordability, and minimal environmental impact.

The Glydways system is a groundbreaking network of carbon-neutral, interconnected transit pathways powered by standardized autonomous vehicles on dedicated roadways. Operating 24/7 with on-demand access, it offers personalized and efficient mobility—without the burden of heavy upfront infrastructure costs or ongoing taxpayer subsidies.

With Glydways, we’re building more than a transportation system; we’re creating a future where everyone, everywhere, has the freedom to move.

About the Project:

The Glydways Atlanta ATN Pilot Project is the first passenger carrying Automated Transit Network deployed by Glydways in the United States, running from the Airport SkyTrain at the Georgia International Convention Center to the Gateway Center Arena. It spans construction, system integration and testing, commissioning, and pilot passenger service alongside project sponsors, contractors, the operating organization, local authorities, and emergency responders.

Glydways has established an independent Safety, Quality and Compliance organization, applying established transit and rail safety standards to a new class of automated technology. On the Atlanta site, the safety function owns the site safety management system, confirms that required controls are implemented before work and service proceed, and works in close partnership with Test and Commissioning, Operations, Maintenance, Quality, Engineering, contractors, local authorities, and emergency responders to sustain them.

About the Role:

The Test & Commissioning Engineer / Central Control Operator supports testing, commissioning and operations of the Glydways Atlanta ATN Pilot Project. The CCO reports to the Operations Manager, monitors the system, carries out approved operational and test actions within assigned authority, and escalates abnormal or unresolved conditions.

• Monitor vehicles, guideway and access locations, OCS and operator displays, alarms, communications, network status, cameras, and operating conditions.

• Complete startup and pre-test checks; execute approved integration, acceptance, commissioning, regression, and safety-validation tests; and record results and deviations.

• Assess alerts, provide approved remote assistance, and execute authorized stop, E-Stop, recovery, communication, and service-support actions; pause testing or operations when conditions are unsafe or outside the approved configuration.

• Coordinate field response, fault diagnosis, approved updates, and retesting with the CCO Lead, Field Operations, maintenance, engineering, and safety.

• Communicate clearly with riders, field personnel, and emergency responders, and maintain accurate operational, test, fault, incident, and evidence records.

• Provide complete shift handovers, maintain required training and qualifications, participate in post-incident reviews, and flag recurring faults or operational patterns for follow-up.

This is an in-person position in Atlanta, GA and will start as a one year contract. The role will start with an in-person 4-6 week training in Richmond, CA

Required Skills and Certifications:

• B.S. in Engineering Fields or equivalent

• At least three years of experience as a test and commissioning engineer, as an operator in a control room, dispatch center, transit, fleet, test-and-commissioning, industrial, or emergency-response environment.

• Ability to monitor multiple information sources, recognize changing conditions, and act promptly within approved procedures.

• Ability to execute structured test procedures, perform basic troubleshooting, and capture accurate technical evidence.

• Clear verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to remain calm and focused under pressure.

• Available for onsite rotating shifts in Atlanta, including nights, weekends, and holidays.

Nice to Haves:

• Experience with autonomous vehicles, public transit, rail, automated people movers, or another safety-critical system.

• Familiarity with Operation Control Centers and SCADA tools, fleet and network monitoring, vehicle diagnostics, Jira, test tracking, or log handling.

• Experience with system bring-up, acceptance or safety-validation testing, controlled updates, fault reproduction, or retesting.
